articles.title: Friendly’s Introduces New ‘Snow Days’ Menu
articles.titleKo: Friendly’s Introduces New ‘Snow Days’ Menu
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The Harvest Stack is sourdough bread piled high with stuffing, garlic red-skin mashed potatoes, grilled turkey breast and a spoonful of cranberry sauce, smothered in turkey gravy. Friendly’s is trading sunshine for snowflakes. Available now through the holiday season, the Snow Days menu brings three seasonal entrées, a peppermint-packed dessert lineup and a pair of value deals to restaurants systemwide. Leading the charge is a trio of stick-to-your-ribs plates made for sweater weather: Snowfall Burger: Friendly’s Big Beef Burger with white American cheese, Alfredo sauce and hardwood-smoked bacon on a Parmesan-dusted pretzel bun, served with golden fries. Fireside Melt: White American cheese and Tillamook sharp yellow cheddar with grilled chicken, hardwood-smoked bacon, tomatoes and garlic aioli on grilled sourdough, paired with golden fries. Harvest Stack: Sourdough bread piled high with stuffing, garlic red-skin mashed potatoes, grilled turkey breast and a spoonful of cranberry sauce, smothered in turkey gravy. To keep spirits bright, guests who order any Snow Days entrée will receive a FREE Happy Ending Sundae, because every good meal deserves a sweet treat. Dessert takes a wintry turn with creations that call for an extra spoon, including: Snowball Fight Sundae: Vanilla ice cream and donut holes dusted with powdered sugar and topped with hot fudge drizzle, mini marshmallows, whipped cream and chocolate sprinkles. Peppermint Stick Fribble: Peppermint Stick ice cream drizzled with hot fudge and crowned with whipped cream and a cherry. Jubilee Cake: A yummy blast from the past, layering chocolate chip and chocolate ice creams beneath fudge drizzle, almonds and chocolate candies, finished with a playful pink frosted border. Value keeps its seat at the table all winter with two deals running alongside the new menu. Better Together pairs two entrées with one appetizer starting at $24.99, or $29.99 for premium entrée picks. For a midday break, the Weekday Lunch Deal offers one of five select entrées plus a Happy Ending Sundae for $11.99, Monday through Friday from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. Kids also have another reason to come back, with every kids’ meal including a sealed pack of Conehead Crew trading cards for a chance to complete the 18-card collection. “Friendly’s has always been about making a meal feel like more than just a meal, and Snow Days gives people plenty of ways to have fun,” said Erik Jensen, vice president of marketing for BRIX Holdings. “Between a Snowball Fight Sundae piled high with toppings and a Conehead Crew card pack waiting to be opened, there’s a little something to make every winter visit memorable.” It’s a season of smiles at Friendly’s. Whether stopping in for a quick bite or rounding out a family meal, Friendly’s makes it easy to enjoy the classics without stretching the budget. Guests can also make the most of the new offerings by joining the Friendly’s Fan Club rewards program, which provides exclusive offers, alongside specialty promotions and updates. For more information, visit friendlysrestaurants.com. The post Friendly’s Introduces New ‘Snow Days’ Menu appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: Major Wendy’s Franchisee Significantly Cuts Footprint During Bankruptcy
articles.titleKo: Major Wendy’s Franchisee Significantly Cuts Footprint During Bankruptcy
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Wendy's franchisee declared bankruptcy in September. Large Wendy’s franchisee Meritage Hospitality Group has closed 33 Wendy’s restaurants since filing for bankruptcy in September, with another 20–60 shutdowns required by November 13 under a court-approved agreement. The company had already closed approximately 60 underperforming Wendy’s restaurants before bankruptcy, beginning in Q4 2025. Meritage estimated those earlier closures would improve annual EBITDA by $8 million. According to Meritage, these locations were losing money, and shedding their leases and franchise agreements would eliminate unnecessary expenses. The franchisee filed for bankruptcy on September 17 . At filing, it operated 320 restaurants across 15 states, including 314 Wendy’s, and employed approximately 8,850 people. Wendy’s moved to terminate Meritage’s franchise agreements one day before the bankruptcy filing and claims the operator owes roughly $146.9 million in royalties, fees, and other contractual charges. Meritage disputes the termination’s effectiveness and maintains its franchise agreements are still in place. Meritage’s financial troubles intensified over the past two years. Same-store sales fell 7.2 percent in fiscal 2025 and another 8.3 percent during the first half of 2026. The company reported net losses of $31.5 million and $23.1 million during those periods, respectively. The operator attributed its difficulties to weak sales, elevated beef costs, national discounting, disruptive weather, and what it described as less effective Wendy’s marketing under prior brand officials. Before bankruptcy, Meritage pursued cost reductions, changes to breakfast service, and sale-leaseback transactions to improve profitability and reduce debt. articles.title: Urbane Cafe to Open in Goleta, California
articles.titleKo: Urbane Cafe to Open in Goleta, California
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Urbane Cafe is growing its Central Coast presence with its new Goleta location, bringing its take on fresh, made-from-scratch dining to the broader Santa Barbara area. Known for its house-baked focaccia, gourmet sandwiches and signature bowls, the California-born brand will welcome guests at its newest location on Monday, October 26. Since opening its doors in Ventura in 2003, Urbane Cafe has set out to make fresh, high-quality food a staple of the fast-casual experience. The brand’s menu features focaccia baked from scratch every day, gourmet sandwiches paired with fresh side salads, hearty bowls and house-made sauces. Each location is an open scratch kitchen with a signature hearth oven, where guests can watch their meals come together. “We love the Central Coast and are excited to bring our scratch-made menu to Goleta,” said Tom Holt, Founder of Urbane Cafe. “The Santa Barbara community has been inquiring about a location for a long time – and we are thrilled that we are able to officially be a part of their amazing community. Their enthusiasm means a lot to us and we look forward to serving them for years to come.” To mark the Goleta debut, Urbane Cafe will celebrate with a lineup of grand opening offerings for community members to enjoy: Grand Opening Day (October 26): The first 50 guests in line will receive a free sandwich every month for a year (12 sandwiches total). A ribbon-cutting ceremony with the Santa Barbara South Coast Chamber of Commerce will take place at 10 a.m. Student Giveback Day (October 28): Students can enjoy a complimentary sandwich, salad or bowl when they order through the Urbane Cafe app with a promotional code. Students must sign up here in advance to receive the code and present a valid student ID at pickup. Limited to 500 Students. Teacher Giveback Day (November 4): Teachers and school staff can enjoy a complimentary sandwich, salad or bowl by completing the RSVP form here to receive a promotional code and placing an online order. This opening comes on the heels of opening the first-ever location in Glendale in September, furthering the brand’s ambitious growth goals. Urbane Cafe plans to open six new Southern California locations in 2027, with a long-term target of 100 total locations by 2030. Building on its active growth into Las Vegas and Arizona, the brand continues to prioritize strategic expansion while preserving the food quality, guest experience and company culture that have defined Urbane Cafe since its founding. URBANE CAFE GOLETA DETAILS Grand Opening: Ribbon Cutting Ceremony at 10 a.m. Address: 7000 Hollister Ave, Suite 102, Goleta, California 93117 Hours of Operation: Monday–Saturday, 10:30 a.m.–9 p.m.; Sunday, 10:30 a.m.–8 p.m. The post Urbane Cafe to Open in Goleta, California appeared first on QSR Magazine .

Those looking for something warm and filling can settle in with Polly’s Chili, a slow-simmered bowl of ground beef, sweet onions, garlic, red and green bell peppers, tomatoes and a blend of spices. As the weather cools and the holiday season approaches, Polly’s Pies is giving guests more reasons to gather around the table with a seasonal lineup of comforting dishes inspired by the flavors of fall. From a familiar breakfast favorite with a seasonal twist to savory bites filled with Thanksgiving staples, the latest offerings bring together the kind of homestyle cooking guests have come to know and love from Polly’s. Breakfast gets a seasonal addition with Pumpkin Pancakes ($14.99), featuring two buttermilk pumpkin pancakes made with Coach’s Oats and topped with house-made cinnamon whipped cream. The plate comes with two large eggs and a choice of Jones Dairy Farms smoked sausage, applewood smoked bacon, turkey sausage or a 3-ounce ham slice. The Holiday Hushpuppies ($9.99) feature six crispy bites filled with oven-roasted turkey, stuffing, red-skin smashed potatoes and cheddar cheese, finished with turkey gravy and served alongside zesty cranberry sauce. Those looking for something warm and filling can settle in with Polly’s Chili, a slow-simmered bowl of ground beef, sweet onions, garlic, red and green bell peppers, tomatoes and a blend of spices. Kidney and pinto beans round out the entree, with sour cream, shredded cheddar cheese and green onion on top. Served with freshly baked cornbread, the chili is available in a cup ($4.99) or bowl ($8.99). Thanksgiving classics also make an appearance with Turkey Day Sliders ($11.99), boasting slices of oven-roasted turkey breast layered with stuffing and zesty cranberry sauce on two freshly baked dinner rolls spread with mayonnaise and served with fries. For the full holiday spread, Polly’s Traditional Turkey Dinner ($19.99) brings together oven-roasted turkey breast, homestyle stuffing, red-skin smashed potatoes, smashed sweet potatoes, Southern-style green beans with applewood smoked bacon, zesty cranberry sauce and turkey gravy. “Fall and the holiday season are all about gathering around the table and enjoying the dishes that make this time of year special,” said Meghan Meadors, advertising and public relations manager at Polly’s Pies. “We wanted this season’s menu to bring some of those familiar Thanksgiving flavors into the Polly’s experience, alongside the favorites our guests know and love. Whether it’s stopping in for breakfast or sitting down for a traditional turkey dinner, there’s something for everyone to enjoy.” These signature fall specials are available for a limited time at all 12 locations. Polly’s Pies is also accepting catering pre-orders for the Thanksgiving season including holiday feasts and its variety of famous pies. Juice It Up!, one of the nation’s leading açai bowl, handcrafted smoothie and raw juice chains for over 30 years, has opened a new location in Temecula, expanding the brand’s presence across Southern California. The new location is owned and operated by Temecula residents Fatemeh Toori and Peyman Zamanian, who plan to grow the brand’s presence throughout the region. Located at Palm Plaza in Temecula, the new Juice It Up! is now proudly serving its signature açaí bowls, blended to order smoothies and fresh-squeezed raw juices to guests seeking delicious options to fuel up on the go. “We were immediately drawn to Juice It Up! for its strong brand foundation, innovative product offerings and reputation for delivering an exceptional guest experience,” said Toori, Juice It Up! Temecula franchisee. “We’re excited to bring that experience to our community and see tremendous opportunity to introduce more Riverside County residents to the brand, build lasting relationships with our guests and grow alongside the community for years to come.” Juice It Up! offers a wide variety of handcrafted menu options that bring flavor and functionality to everyday occasions. An innovator of açaí and lesser-known ingredients since 1995, the brand’s menu includes customizable açaí bowls, blended-to-order smoothies, fresh-squeezed raw juices, toasts, pretzels and more. For more than three decades, Juice It Up! has helped guests “Live Life Juiced!,” a motto that underscores the brand’s longstanding commitment to providing products geared to fuel each day. Juice It Up! Rewards® members can enjoy exclusive perks, starting with a Free Medium Classic Smoothie with a $5 minimum purchase upon registration, plus the ability to earn points toward future rewards, access special offers and enjoy easy ordering and payment options. With more than 130 locations open or under development in seven states, Juice It Up! continues to attract partners that value franchise opportunities with relatively lower costs of development, attractive and simplified food costs and a lighter labor model compared to many other franchised brands, especially in new, untapped markets. Juice It Up! invites qualified franchisees to explore how they can benefit from partnering with a trusted, thriving brand in the popular açaí bowl, smoothie and raw juice segment, especially as the demand for fresh and convenient menu options continues to grow across the United States. Juice It Up!’s new Temecula store is located at 26475 Ynez Road, Suite 9, and can be reached at (951) 726-5583.The location is open Monday through Friday from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. and Saturday and Sunday from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. For more information about Juice It Up!, including the full menu with nutritional values and franchising opportunities, visit www.juiceitup.com . articles.title: White Castle Chosen for 2026 Fortune Best Workplaces in Retail List
articles.titleKo: White Castle Chosen for 2026 Fortune Best Workplaces in Retail List
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Great Place To Work and Fortune magazine have selected White Castle for the 2026 Fortune Best Workplaces in Retail list. This is White Castle’s fifth consecutive year being named to this prestigious list, this year coming in at 11 th place in the large category. Earning a spot means that White Castle is one of the best retail companies to work for in the country. The Best Workplaces in Retail award is based on analysis of survey responses from nearly 76,000 employees at Great Place To Work Certified™ companies in the retail industry. “From our founding in 1921, my great-grandfather Billy Ingram dedicated his leadership to creating a workplace where people are respected, valued and supported,” said John Kelley, chief people officer and fourth-generation family member. “And in the 105 years since, we’ve never wavered on that commitment. It’s an honor to be recognized as a one of the very Best Workplaces in Retail, and we share this recognition with every one of our nearly 9,000 team members.” The Best Workplaces in Retail list is highly competitive. Great Place To Work, the global authority on workplace culture, determines its lists using its proprietary Trust Index™ Survey to evaluate and certify thousands of organizations in America’s largest ongoing annual workforce study, based on over 1.3 million survey responses and data from companies representing more than 7.3 million employees. Survey responses reflect a comprehensive picture of the workplace experience. Honorees were selected based on their ability to offer positive outcomes for employees regardless of job role, work status, or other demographic identifier. “Congratulations to the Fortune Best Workplaces in Retail,” says Michael C. Bush, CEO of Great Place To Work. “People are at the heart of work in every industry, and retail is no exception. These companies show how delivering for your people drives financial performance and turns fear of the future into the confidence to win.” White Castle is widely recognized for its family-centered culture and team member growth. Today, more than one in four team members has been with the business for 10 years or more, and in October White Castle inducted its latest class into the 25-Year Club, which now totals more than 2,500 members. White Castle has been certified as a Great Place to Work every year since 2021 and has been on the Best Workplaces in Retail™ list for five consecutive years — the only restaurant brand to claim this distinction. Tropical Smoothie Cafe, one of the nation’s leading fast-casual restaurant brands, has announced a 40-unit franchise development deal across New York and Connecticut with franchisee Aurify Kingstar, expanding the brand’s presence in key Northeast markets. The agreement marks a significant step in Tropical Smoothie Cafe’s next phase of strategic franchise growth. With more than 1,750 cafes and a robust development pipeline, the brand is on track to open its 1,800th location by the end of 2026. As part of its continued investment in franchise development, Tropical Smoothie Cafe recently appointed Joe Sieve as Chief Development & Growth Officer to lead the brand’s development strategy and growth initiatives. The deal will expand Tropical Smoothie Cafe’s presence across Albany, Westchester County, the Bronx, and Western Connecticut, with Aurify Kingstar planning to open its first location in early 2027. “New York and Connecticut represent tremendous growth opportunities for Tropical Smoothie Cafe and reflect the potential ahead as we enter our next phase of growth,” said Max Wetzel, CEO of Tropical Smoothie Cafe, LLC. “Aurify Kingstar brings the restaurant experience, infrastructure, and proven multi-unit development capabilities we look for in growth partners. Together, we can meaningfully expand our presence in the Northeast while continuing to deliver the guest experience and community connection that define our brand.” Andy Stern, John Rigos, and Jeremy Tannenbaum spearhead Aurify Kingstar’s development efforts, bringing more than 25 years of experience building and operating restaurant concepts. Throughout their careers, the team has developed their own concepts and built a diverse franchise portfolio, gaining extensive expertise in restaurant operations, brand development, and multi-unit growth. “We’ve followed Tropical Smoothie Cafe’s growth and success for some time, and the strength of the brand and the experience it creates for guests stood out to us,” said Tannenbaum. “As operators, we’re passionate about restaurant concepts that bring people together and become part of the communities they serve. We see a tremendous opportunity to build Tropical Smoothie Cafe’s presence throughout the Northeast, create great experiences for our guests, and establish meaningful connections in each community we enter.” As Tropical Smoothie Cafe advances its franchise growth strategy, the brand continues to see strong confidence from both new and existing franchisees while prioritizing experienced developers like Aurify Kingstar, who bring strong market knowledge, established infrastructure, and the ability to scale multi-unit operations. Aurify Kingstar identified Tropical Smoothie Cafe as a strong addition to its portfolio based on the brand’s established system, growing consumer demand, available development whitespace, and continued nationwide growth. For more information about Tropical Smoothie Cafe and its menu offerings, visit TropicalSmoothieCafe.com. articles.title: Pollo Campero Names Julio Sánchez CEO of U.S. Segment
articles.titleKo: Pollo Campero Names Julio Sánchez CEO of U.S. Segment
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . With more than 25 years of experience, Julio Sánchez has led operations, franchising, development and transformation across North America, Latin America, the Caribbean and Europe. Pollo Campero, the Guatemalan-born quick-service restaurant known for its fried and roasted chicken, has named industry veteran Julio Sánchez CEO of its U.S. business, effective immediately. The company thanks outgoing chief operating officer Luis Javier Rodas, who concluded nearly 26 years with CMI on Oct. 16, for his contributions to the brand’s growth in the U.S. With more than 25 years of experience, Sánchez has led operations, franchising, development and transformation across North America, Latin America, the Caribbean and Europe. Most recently, he served as chief operating officer of CKE International (Carl’s Jr.), and previously held leadership roles at Pizza Hut, Burger King and Church’s Chicken, where he successfully introduced brands into new markets and drove strong same-store sales growth. As CEO, Sánchez will lead the next phase of profitable growth for Campero USA, initially focusing on improving operational excellence, accelerating same-store sales growth, increasing brand awareness and elevating the guest experience to bring the Campero flavor to even more consumers across the United States. His appointment comes as the brand grows beyond 150 U.S. restaurants and works toward continued U.S. expansion. Known for his hands-on style, Sánchez leads from the restaurant floor, staying close to the team members, franchise partners and guests who shape the experience every day. “Julio combines deep operational expertise with sound business judgment and a proven record of delivering results. He is the right leader to guide Campero into its next stage of growth,” said José Gregorio Baquero, global CEO of CMI Foods. Pollo Campero was founded in Guatemala in 1971 and is part of Corporación Multi Inversiones (CMI), a family-owned company with 106 years of history. “I was immediately drawn to Campero’s heritage, sense of hospitality and, of course, flavor,” said Sánchez. “As we bring Pollo Campero to more communities across the U.S., I’m committed to putting our restaurant team members and guests at the forefront to ensure a memorable experience every time they come to our table.” The post Pollo Campero Names Julio Sánchez CEO of U.S. Segment appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Fine-Dining Concept Aria Names Elissa Hayward Executive Pastry Chef
articles.titleKo: Fine-Dining Concept Aria Names Elissa Hayward Executive Pastry Chef
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Aria has named Elissa Hayward executive pastry chef, adding another creative voice to a team where ideas already move between the kitchen, pastry, bar, and wine programs. Hayward reunites with executive chef Austin Goetzman, with whom she previously worked at Lazy Betty, and joins bar lead Eric Simpkins and lead sommelier and assistant general manager Princeton Saunders as the group continues developing, tasting, and exchanging ideas across their respective areas. That collaboration is already taking shape. Hayward and Saunders have been tasting wines for a red wine sorbet, and conversations with Simpkins about smoked flavors have connected what is happening in pastry with what’s happening behind the bar. She and Goetzman regularly taste one another’s work, continuing a creative relationship they first developed while working together previously. “Elissa’s approach immediately stood out to us,” says owner Andrés Loaiza. “She understands the entire kitchen, not just one part of it, and that comes through in the way she thinks about dessert. She has a strong technical foundation, but she also brings curiosity and personality to what she creates. We’re excited to give her the room to explore that at Aria.” For Hayward, joining Aria is an opportunity to develop her own style while working alongside a team whose individual specialties often inform one another. “I think what is exciting is that everyone is really immersed in their own area, but we’re still constantly talking and tasting together,” says Hayward. “Austin is focused on the savory menu, Eric and Princeton are bringing new ideas to the bar and wine programs, and I’m focused on pastry. We all have our own areas, but there is a lot of opportunity for those ideas to come together.” An early glimpse of her approach appears in a dessert Hayward is beginning to develop, featuring smoked vanilla mousse (pictured below), green apple, turmeric, brown butter crumble, and caramel. The combination reflects several elements of her style: familiar flavors and classical technique paired with unexpected ingredients, contrasting textures, and a subtle savory influence. Hayward’s path to pastry has shaped the way she approaches dessert. She trained in both culinary arts and baking and pastry, then spent much of her early career on the savory side of the kitchen before choosing to focus fully on pastry several years ago. Her experience includes time at Bouchon Bistro in California and, most recently, The Deer and the Dove in Decatur. That background still influences her work. Hayward gravitates toward French classics and traditional technique, but she is equally interested in texture, unexpected flavors, and the memories certain ingredients can evoke. A dessert might recall fall, a childhood favorite, or time spent around a campfire, then reinterpret that feeling through a more refined lens. “I love the classics, but I also love playing with nostalgia and finding ways to make something feel familiar and new at the same time,” says Hayward. “There can be something playful about the flavors while there is still a lot of technique behind them. That combination is what I’m always drawn to.” At Aria, Hayward wants pastry to carry the same attention to detail as the savory menu while still giving guests a final course that can surprise them. “I’m excited to involve guests in the pastry side of the menu in the same way they experience the savory side,” says Hayward. “I want dessert to feel like part of the complete meal, with just as much thought behind it, while also giving guests something they may not have expected.” The post Fine-Dining Concept Aria Names Elissa Hayward Executive Pastry Chef appeared first on FSR magazine .

Throughout his career, he has worked across several restaurant brands and gained experience in accounting, finance, development, and day-to-day restaurant operations. His path into restaurants began while attending Ohio State University and later working at Skyline Chili, where he discovered a passion for hospitality, serving others and building strong teams. “After spending nearly two decades in the restaurant industry, I knew I wanted to build something of my own with the right brand and the right people,” said Cunningham. “Currito checked the boxes we were looking for: simple operations, clean and comfortable restaurants, a product people can feel good about and a leadership team that feels like a true partner. A Certified Public Accountant (CPA) by trade, Patel has previous restaurant ownership experience and operates his Currito business alongside his family, including his brother and their wives, who help run the business day to day. Before becoming a franchisee, Patel was first a loyal Currito customer, eating at the restaurant consistently and becoming impressed by the brand’s ability to deliver the same quality, flavor, and experience every time. “Before I ever became a franchisee, I was a Currito customer for two years, and what stood out to me was the consistency,” said Patel . “Every time I came in, the food quality and experience were the same. Expanding with another location in Liberty Township is a natural next step for our family and our team.” Together, Cunningham and Patel represent two important growth paths for Currito: a new franchisee bringing deep restaurant leadership experience into the system and an existing operator expanding after seeing the brand’s potential firsthand. Michelle Chin spent her first year as Applebee’s CMO visiting restaurants, meeting franchisees, and watching how employees interacted with their regulars. Some guests had favorite seats. Others called ahead to make sure a particular server would be working. A few employees even considered themselves the mayor of the neighborhood. Those relationships gave Chin a starting point for the brand’s marketing. Applebee’s had spent decades building its identity around being a neighborhood gathering place. Inside its restaurants, she found evidence that the promise still meant something. The task now is translating that experience into a reason to visit, including among younger consumers who have chosen other restaurants or have little familiarity with Applebee’s. She sees opportunity in the occasions surrounding the bigger events on people’s calendars. A family can stop in before a game. Friends can catch up after a movie. Sunday church services can lead to a meal together. None requires a birthday, holiday, or elaborate plan.` “It’s all about that human connection and that socialization at the table where people can have a conversation,” Chin says. “And it could be big conversations, but even more importantly, it’s those little moments. Sure, I would love game days and birthdays and all of that. But I think what’s even more important are those in-between moments. And I’ve been playing with this notion of, really wanting people to get together at Applebee’s on those pre and post moments around the main event and their lives.” That thinking gives Applebee’s a role in everyday life that Chin wants its marketing to communicate more clearly. The restaurant can be an easy place to reconnect, with familiar food and a setting that doesn’t demand much preparation. “I think we’ve put this whole notion of dining out on a pedestal and it makes it hard and kind of like out of touch with it. And so make it casual again. Like I just want to connect. I just want to see you. Let’s just grab some wings,” Chin says. Making that message relevant involves changes across marketing and the menu. During her first year, Chin has added talent, tested products, and increased the brand’s participation in social conversations. Applebee’s also named BBDO Chicago its new creative agency of record, following nearly a decade with Grey. The roster includes new vice presidents of integrated marketing and culinary. Chin sees those positions as important to connecting the brand’s message with what guests actually encounter when they sit down to eat. A social team that came aboard shortly before her arrival has helped Applebee’s listen to customers and identify conversations where it can participate naturally. Chin says the brand has seen traffic gains among Gen Z consumers. The objective is to earn a place in people’s daily conversations without turning every interaction into a product pitch. “When we do jump into the conversation and be part of their everyday conversation, the brand’s showing up authentically,” Chin says. “We’re not trying to hard sell anything. This holiday season, Whataburger is bringing the heat, the holiday cheer and plenty of bold flavors to the table. Beginning Oct. 20, the Bacon Blaze lineup fires up the menu with the fan-favorite Bacon Blaze Jalapeño Double and new Bacon Blaze Chicken, both packing the perfect kick. And for Guests who’d rather sip than sizzle, the Sleigh Berry Whatafresher and the Whataburger White Chocolate Raspberry Shake give Guests two festive ways to satisfy their sweet tooth. The full limited-time lineup includes: Bacon Blaze Jalapeño Double – The Bacon Blaze lineup offers just the right amount of heat that never sacrifices flavor. The Bacon Blaze Jalapeño Double layers two fresh, 100% beef patties with creamy Jalapeño Ranch, jalapeño cream cheese, smoky bacon, sliced jalapeños and real aged cheddar cheese. Guests looking for a smaller bite can order it in a Jr. size. Bacon Blaze Chicken – The new Bacon Blaze Chicken puts that same perfect kick on premium chicken, with Guests’ choice of grilled or Whatachick’n® on a toasted potato bun. Sleigh Berry Whatafresher – The new Sleigh Berry Whatafresher is a bright, festive refresher that brings together tart cranberry, juicy citrus and a hint of cozy holiday warmth for a perfectly balanced seasonal sip. Real cranberry pieces and a lightly sweet, creamy soft whip make it even more festive. White Chocolate Raspberry Shake – For dessert, the new Whataburger White Chocolate Raspberry Shake pairs sweet white chocolate and tart raspberry flavors in a creamy vanilla shake that tastes like white chocolate raspberry cheesecake. “Guests are looking for more variety from restaurant menus — from bold, spicy flavors to beverages that feel fresh and seasonal,” said Whataburger Corporate Chef James Sanchez. “This lineup lets us deliver both: bringing back a flavor Guests have already told us they love while introducing new choices that feel right for the season.” The Bacon Blaze Jalapeño Double starts at $9.99, with the Jr. Bacon Blaze Jalapeño Double and Bacon Blaze Chicken starting at $7.99. The Sleigh Berry Whatafresher starts at $3.69, and the White Chocolate Raspberry Shake starts at $3.99. Prices vary by location. The whole lineup is only around for a limited time at participating locations, so get it while you can. Hungry for more? Whataburger serves fans 24/7, whether they swing through the drive-thru, order online or use the Whataburger App. Guests who download the app and create an account automatically receive a free Whataburger and begin earning points toward their favorite menu items. articles.title: Newport Beach’s Sushi Ii Changes Name to Sushi Suhama
articles.titleKo: Newport Beach’s Sushi Ii Changes Name to Sushi Suhama
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Sushi Ii, the intimate Japanese restaurant in Newport Beach’s Mariner’s Mile, has entered its next chapter as Sushi Suhama, with a new name that reflects both the restaurant’s Japanese roots and its connection to the coastal landscape it calls home. While the name is new, Sushi Suhama remains an evolution of the restaurant guests have come to know, continuing its commitment to seasonality, craftsmanship, and traditional Japanese culinary technique. The intimate setting and culinary team that have defined the restaurant remain at the heart of Sushi Suhama. Since opening, the restaurant has been recognized by the MICHELIN Guide six times, a distinction Sushi Suhama carries with it into this next chapter. The name Suhama comes from an ancient Japanese term referring to a beautiful or picturesque shoreline. For the restaurant, Suhama evokes the natural shoreline that defines Newport Beach, creating a connection between Japanese culture and the coastal setting that has been part of the restaurant’s identity since opening. Renowned Japanese artist Hiroshi Sugimoto was commissioned to help shape this next chapter and selected the name Sushi Suhama for the restaurant. One of Sugimoto’s celebrated seascapes will also be displayed within the space, further connecting the restaurant’s new identity to the meeting of sea, landscape, and Japanese artistry. “Suhama felt meaningful because it gives the restaurant a sense of place. This is still the restaurant our guests know, but the new name gives us an opportunity to express more clearly who we are today and where we are going, while remaining true to what has always defined the experience,” said Director Natsuko Travioli. Along with the new identity, Sushi Suhama has refined its omakase offerings to give guests distinct ways to experience the restaurant. The Sai Kaiseki Course offers the most expansive progression through the traditions of Japanese multi-course dining, while the new Ran Signature Course balances composed seasonal dishes with a greater emphasis on sushi. The Mio Sushi Course places nigiri at the center of the experience, offering the most sushi-forward expression of the three. The new structure allows guests to choose the style of omakase experience that most appeals to them, from a complete kaiseki progression to an experience centered more heavily around sushi. Across each, menus continue to evolve with the seasons and the availability of ingredients at their peak. The evolution comes under the continued culinary leadership of Chefs Norio Izawa and Koji Takahashi, alongside Director Natsuko Travioli. Izawa heads Sushi Suhama’s kaiseki program, drawing upon his training in respected kaiseki kitchens in Tokyo and Kanazawa and experience at Nobu in New York and Bluefin in Newport Beach to guide the restaurant’s multi-course culinary experience. Takahashi, who has been with the restaurant since its opening and brings nearly four decades of experience to his craft, leads the sushi program. Working alongside him is Chef Tatsushi Wakabayashi, who joined the team approximately a year ago and brings experience from Nobu, Ikko, and Oshima. Together, the chefs preserve the discipline and precision of traditional Japanese cooking while allowing the experience to evolve with a modern sensibility. That philosophy extends beyond the menu. From the ceramics selected for each presentation to the intimate counter experience and considered pace of service, Sushi Suhama remains rooted in the Japanese belief that hospitality is expressed through attention to detail. The restaurant’s new identity builds upon that foundation rather than redefining it, marking a natural evolution of a restaurant that has continued to refine itself since opening. TJ Rice brings more than five years of restaurant and hospitality experience. Corner Bakery Cafe is welcoming a new franchise partner in Pennsylvania as TJ Rice, founder of Rice Equity Group, takes ownership of its Horsham cafe. Rice adds Corner Bakery to a multi-brand portfolio that includes Subway, Captain D’s and Massage Envy, bringing an experienced operator with existing business and family ties to the Philadelphia region into the brand’s growing franchise network. “Welcoming experienced operators like TJ is an important part of how we’re building Corner Bakery’s future,” said Erin Hasselgren, president of Corner Bakery Cafe. “He brings a strong operating foundation, a focus on developing teams and a personal appreciation for the guest experience that defines our cafes. We’re excited to welcome him to the Corner Bakery family and support his investment in the PA Market.” Rice brings more than five years of restaurant and hospitality experience, with a focus on multi-unit operations, franchise development and team leadership. Through Rice Equity Group, he emphasizes consistent guest experiences, strong operating systems and opportunities for employees to develop and advance. For Rice, joining Corner Bakery also builds on a connection formed as a guest. He and his family have enjoyed visiting the brand’s cafes throughout the Washington, D.C., Maryland and Virginia region, drawn to the inviting atmosphere and variety of food. “We have tremendous confidence in Erin Hasselgren’s leadership and his vision for the future of Corner Bakery Cafe,” said Rice. “At Rice Equity Group, we are deliberate in selecting the brands and leadership teams with whom we partner, and we see an exceptional opportunity to grow alongside Erin and the Corner Bakery team. Our ambition is to become one of Corner Bakery’s most trusted and valued franchise partners, bringing the operational infrastructure, financial discipline, experienced leadership, and multi-unit execution capabilities necessary to support disciplined expansion.” Rice’s family and business interests already have roots in Pennsylvania. His wife is a Temple University alumna, and the couple owns and operates health and wellness clinics in the Philadelphia and Pittsburgh markets. Taking ownership of the Horsham cafe builds on those connections and his commitment to continued investment in the region. The Horsham acquisition marks the beginning of Rice Equity Group’s investment in Corner Bakery, with Rice looking to build a broader presence with the brand. His long-term commitment reflects the opportunity he sees in Corner Bakery’s future and adds an experienced, growth-minded partner to its franchise network. articles.title: Vicious Biscuit Signs Deal to Open in Valdosta, Georgia

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Vicious Biscuit, the original home of unapologetically bold biscuits, has signed veteran restaurant operators Doug Puryear and Brian Smith as franchise partners in South Georgia. The longtime business partners, who own and operate nine Surcheros restaurants, will open their first Vicious Biscuit in Valdosta, with an anticipated spring 2027 opening. The agreement marks Vicious Biscuit’s entry into the market as the Charleston-born fast-casual breakfast and brunch brand continues expanding across the Southeast and Midwest. Puryear and Smith, whose restaurant group operates as SAP Saint Simons, bring 30 years of combined restaurant industry experience to Vicious Biscuit. Puryear has spent 10 years in the business, while Smith has 20 years, including a decade owning two Hardee’s locations. Together, they previously operated two Huddle House restaurants for 10 years. Their Surcheros locations in Valdosta and Brunswick consistently rank among the brand’s top performers. Their interest in Vicious Biscuit began when Puryear visited the brand’s flagship restaurant in Mount Pleasant, SC. Impressed by the food and guest experience, he encouraged Smith to visit. After experiencing the concept firsthand and meeting with Vicious Biscuit’s leadership team, the partners decided to add the brand to their restaurant portfolio. “The food is what initially got our attention, but the more we learned about Vicious Biscuit, the more impressed we became,” said Puryear. “We’ve worked with several restaurant brands over the years, and the operations, technology and support systems Vicious Biscuit has already put in place really stood out. They’ve built a strong foundation, and we wanted to be part of it.” The partners were also attracted to Vicious Biscuit’s single-daypart operating model, which focuses on breakfast and brunch. Having previously operated 24-hour restaurants, they recognized the appeal of a more focused approach to staffing, restaurant operations and the guest experience. “Vicious Biscuit has put a lot of thought into how the business operates,” said Smith. “The leadership team understands what franchisees need, and they’ve built the systems to support them. At the same time, the food and hospitality are what make the brand different. That’s an important combination for us.” The approximately 4,000-square-foot Valdosta restaurant will be located at 3259 Inner Perimeter Road, Suite G, in the North Oak Square Shopping Center, adjacent to the partners’ existing Surcheros restaurant. The restaurant is expected to seat 80 to 90 guests. “Doug and Brian have a proven track record of operating successful restaurants and building strong teams,” said George McLaughlin, co-founder and CEO of Vicious Biscuit. “They’re actively involved in their businesses, understand their markets and share our commitment to great food and hospitality. They’re exactly the kind of experienced operators we want to grow with.” As Vicious Biscuit expands into new markets, the brand continues to invest in franchise training, operational systems and technology to support its single-daypart restaurant model. Vicious Biscuit currently operates 13 restaurants, including seven corporate and six franchise locations, with eight additional franchise units signed and under development. Another 33 restaurants are committed under existing franchise agreements, with development contingent upon securing leases. Vicious Biscuit is seeking multiunit operators to join its growing franchise system. For more information, visit www.viciousbiscuit.com/vicious-biscuit-franchise . Visit www.viciousbiscuit.com for additional brand updates. Follow on Instagram @viciousbiscuits, Facebook at ViciousBiscuit1, and TikTok @viciousbiscuitchs to stay in the loop as we continue making big moves and bold biscuit creations. articles.title: McDonald’s and ‘Top Chef’ Winner Tristen Epps-Long Unveil One-Day Chef’s Table Experience

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . McDonald's is inviting fans to experience a curated tasting menu of its iconic menu items at Inside the Golden Arches, the brand's first-ever chef’s table experience, taking place in New York City on October 29. Ever wondered what makes a Quarter Pounder with Cheese sandwich so craveable? Why the egg on an Egg McMuffin breakfast sandwich is perfectly round? Or what goes into the fries you’ve loved for years? On October 29, fans in New York City can snag a seat and find out for themselves. For one day only, McDonald’s and “Top Chef” Season 22 winner and former McDonald’s Crew member Tristen Epps-Long are opening the doors to Inside the Golden Arches , a complimentary chef’s table experience where fans can hear directly from chefs and experts about the quality ingredients, attention to detail and small touches behind some of McDonald’s most iconic menu items. Stepping into the spotlight is the hot and deliciously juicy Quarter Pounder with Cheese. Guests will see how it’s prepared, from the 100% real beef cooked fresh when ordered to the simple ingredients that make it a fan favorite. They’ll also enjoy other McDonald’s iconic menu items, including the Egg McMuffin, Chicken McNuggets and World Famous Fries. Is your mouth watering yet? Chef Tristen will guide guests through the experience, sharing his perspective as a chef—and as one of the 1 in 8 Americans who have worked behind the counter at McDonald’s. “McDonald’s was where I got my start, and the experience helped shape the way I think about food and hospitality,” said Chef Tristen. “Even now, I have a deep appreciation for the consistency that allows millions of people to enjoy the same great meal wherever they are. Inside the Golden Arches gives fans a rare opportunity to see the people, processes and care behind that experience.” While seats at the table are limited, the Quarter Pounder with Cheese celebration is just getting started. Beginning Nov. 2, fans across the country can enjoy the Quarter Pounder with Cheese complete with medium fries and a drink for just $8, at participating McDonald’s restaurants. “Inside the Golden Arches is about creating a new level of access and transparency for our fans,” said Gina Hardy, Vice President, U.S. Marketing & Menu Strategy. “People know the Quarter Pounder with Cheese as one of McDonald’s most iconic burgers, but they may not know that it’s made with 100% beef, never frozen, delivered to local restaurants 2-3 times a week and grilled once you order. We’re excited to give fans a firsthand look at these quality ingredients and gold standard practices, helping them see what makes McDonald’s uniquely McDonald’s.” READY TO PULL UP A CHAIR? articles.title: Pancheros Plays the Long Game on Value and Growth
articles.titleKo: Pancheros Plays the Long Game on Value and Growth
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Pancheros has around 75 restaurants systemwide. Back to normal. It’s a state of being restaurants have been scratching and clawing for in the years since the pandemic sent shockwaves through the industry. For Pancheros founder and CEO Rodney Anderson, 2026 has proven to be the year that the phrase has actually become real. “We’ve been working really hard and trying to make the unit level economics exactly what they were before the pandemic, and I think we’ve done a great job with that,” Anderson says. The roughly 75-unit Pancheros worked with suppliers to mitigate protein costs and leveraged AI tools to better calculate the right yield amounts and reduce waste. As a result, according to Anderson, Pancheros is back to the lowest food cost it’s ever had, even with continued cost increases related to taxes, digital services, and other expenses. Franchisees appear to be on board with the brand’s direction, especially because of better operations. Pancheros has focused on remodeling older locations with digital make lines, a feature that’s led to increases in overall sales—not just digital. That’s in addition to better customer satisfaction, more efficient throughput, and lower employee turnover. More digital make lines are being added to restaurants each week. “First you say, ‘Well, digital sales should go up, but you don’t realize that the in-restaurant guest really likes being treated properly, and those digital sales and the old design with the single make line were interfering with the in-restaurant experience. So that pain went away,” Anderson says. “…It is great for business. It really helps with those peak periods. And not just in handling the third party and the digital stuff, but handling the overall restaurant and the entire package—the entire experience that the customer has.” The rise in digital sales, which account for about 33 percent of sales, has coincided with increased loyalty membership. This year, Pancheros reached 1 million members, or about 13,500 per location. About 26.17 percent of members actively participate. These guests have access to promotions around National Burrito Day, Cinco de Mayo, Teacher Appreciation, and more. Pancheros plans to offer a Halloween BOGO deal for its loyalty members next week. “During the pandemic, we had a real strategy to push digital. Only a couple weeks into it, we realized that we had to have that pickup and delivery work, and we took our entire budget and canceled a lot of projects, canceled a lot of creative, and we really pushed it into developing digital, and our digital grew like crazy, and it’s really given us an advantage over other restaurant chains,” Anderson says. Anderson describes these promotions as rewarding loyal customers as opposed to discounting. The executive says Pancheros is in an advantageous position because it limited price increases a few years after the pandemic. The chain raised prices no more than 4 percent, he says. So for those brands that may have implemented double-digit price increases, guests are pushing back, according to Anderson. The same isn’t happening for Pancheros because of its willingness to accept lower margins in the short term. “We have kept our prices low. We will probably see a price increase this spring again, probably no more than a few percent. And we just want to treat the customers right, and be concerned with long-run sales and value with them, and not go out and start doing these bundled meals and discounts and things like that,” Anderson says. “But we do have a good loyalty program where we do reward them for eating there, and we do some promotions to bring them in. But we’re just very stable in how we approach the consumer, and we try to respect that long term.” Growth is coming as well. Pancheros has several leases signed, mostly in the Midwest. At the core of its offering is a commitment to premium produce, notably Atlantic fatty bluefin tuna, and a culinary philosophy rooted in near-perfect execution “99% perfect,” reflecting the brand’s belief that absolute perfection remains unattainable. The menu is designed as a journey through refined Japanese gastronomy, subtly infused with European techniques and influences inspired by the travels of founders Pedro and Fernando de León. This fusion creates a distinctive culinary identity that challenges conventional expectations of a traditional sushi restaurant. articles.title: 100 Days In, Dakota Manchester Airport Established as a Stylish Destination For Travellers Both Near and Far
articles.titleKo: 100 Days In, Dakota Manchester Airport Established as a Stylish Destination For Travellers Both Near and Far
articles.originalSummary: The UK’s first luxury airport hotel at Manchester Airport has proven to be a hit with air travellers and local residents alike in its first 100 days. Dakota Hotel Group’s stylish, luxury hotel welcomed over 15,000 guests in the opening 100 days, including new guests experiencing the brand for the first time. Guests range from business travellers staying ahead of early morning domestic flights, alongside leisure guests heading to destinations across the globe. Recent guests have travelled on to New York, Los Angeles, Barbados, Singapore and Bangkok, as well as domestic and European routes. The hotel offers a luxury experience with ultimate comfort, to ensure travellers get a great night’s sleep before embarking on their journeys around the globe. Dakota Manchester Airport has seen strong demand throughout the week, with Thursdays and Fridays proving to be particularly busy as guests set off on long weekend breaks or prepare for early flights. The hotel’s parking packages have been extremely popular from the outset. Guests appreciate the convenience of leaving their vehicle at the hotel and being transferred directly to their airport terminal in comfort by Dakota’s concierge team. It also provides guests with the added reassurance of knowing their vehicle is parked in a secure hotel environment while they are away. It’s not just air travellers that are visiting Manchester Airport’s new luxury hotel, local residents and businesses have been enjoying the hotel’s stylish food and beverage offerings alongside hotel residents. For 2026, London’s original grand hotel will be brought to life with frosted botanicals, sculptural branches, crystal and glass details, and starry lighting. Designed to evolve from day into evening, the design combines luminous winter whites with deeper, warming tones, to create a sense of discovery throughout the property. At the heart of the experience, the Lobby will bloom into a grand Winter Garden, guiding guests to Palm Court for the hotel’s celebrated afternoon tea. In Palm Court, guests can take in ‘The Blooming Winter Garden’, inspired by the Victorian glasshouses that allowed exotic plants and fruits to flourish throughout winter. The Winter Garden Festive Afternoon Tea (available 9 November 2026 to 3 January 2027) will feature seasonal flavours, with finger sandwiches such as Roast Bronze Turkey, stu1ing, pickled cranberries and chestnut with a delicate savoury of Potato farl, crème fraiche and oscietra caviar. Snowy white throughout, with bright pops of colour, the cakes and pastries will showcase the likes of Plum and Ginger and Chestnut and Blackcurrant, all in which will be served alongside scones with clotted cream, preserves, a showstopping sharing cake, alongside The Langham’s Glasshouse; an Earl Grey infused layered sponge with bergamot jelly. As day turns to night, ‘Midnight in the Winter Garden’ will see Artesian cocktail bar transformed into a shimmering evening setting inspired by the season. Head Bartender Giulia Cuccurullo and the talented team at Artesian have created two exclusive festive cocktails for the occasion, the Pineapple & Brioche, a decadent take on the Ramos Gin Fizz, combining caramelised rum with bright pineapple and citrus, balanced by rich brioche notes and finished with a velvety foam and the Fig & Port, a luxurious cocktail inspired by the Manhattan, pairing crisp vodka with rich fig and warming aged port, lifted by the dry, saline character of fino sherry. Guests can also choose to explore the festive cocktails alongside Artesian’s elevated bar snacks menu; perfect for predinner bites or a light supper. For those looking to settle into a cosy space, The Wigmore, The Langham’s modern British pub, will grow into ‘The Evergreen Garden’, o^ering a warm and welcoming embrace for the winter season. Guests can choose from the extensive a la carte menu featuring the likes of Roast Turkey Pie, or opt for festive sharing platters such as The Wigmore Favourites Platter, consisting of XXL stovetop 3 cheese and mustard toastie, fat chips and Bloody Mary salt, buttered crumpets, citrus cured salmon and crème fraiche. Hearty dishes made with seasonal ingredients will be served alongside the festive drinks we all crave as the temperature drops. The celebrations continue across The Langham, London on New Year’s Eve, with a choice of three ways to see out 2026 in style. In Palm Court, guests can enjoy an elegant five-course dinner, beginning with Champagne and canapés and accompanied by live music throughout the evening. At Artesian, celebrations step up from 8pm to enjoy an evening of exceptional cocktails, festive atmosphere and late-night glamour accompanied by the delicious bar snack menu and a live DJ taking guests through to midnight. articles.title: The £95 Restaurant Ripple Effect: How Dining Out Drives Spending Beyond the Bill
articles.titleKo: The £95 Restaurant Ripple Effect: How Dining Out Drives Spending Beyond the Bill
articles.originalSummary: For more than 25 years, OpenTable has worked alongside restaurants to help them fill tables, connect with diners and grow their businesses. Its 2026 Restaurant Impact Report explores the vital role restaurants play in local economies, communities and everyday life, as well as how diners can help them thrive. The findings demonstrate that restaurants contribute far more than dining alone. They drive spending and footfall for surrounding businesses while creating spaces where people can come together and reconnect. The report explores the challenges restaurants face, including the impact of no-shows, and how small actions from diners can make a meaningful difference. Among the findings: Dining out has an economic ripple effect: 56% of UK diners spend at neighbouring businesses before or after their meal, spending an average of £95. Restaurants bring people together: 98% say local restaurants are important to their community, while 71% of Gen Z diners are likely to book a meal out to feel better or reconnect when they feel stressed or low. Supporting restaurants goes beyond the bill: Among Gen Z diners who made a restaurant reservation in the past year, 57% admit to having failed to show up at least once. A no-show for a table of two costs £55.70 on average, according to restaurant workers,² while 48% say understanding the financial impact of a no-show would make them more likely to honour or cancel a booking. “Restaurants are so much more than places to eat, they create jobs, bring people together and play an important role in the life of communities across the UK,” explains Sasha Shaker, Senior Director of Restaurant Sales and Service, OpenTable UK and Ireland . “This report showcases the industry’s wider impact and highlights why restaurants matter and why OpenTable is dedicated to advocating for their success.” Restaurants Fuel Employment and Local Economies More than half (56%) of UK restaurant diners said they spent money on other activities the last time they ate out locally.¹ Those who spent elsewhere alongside their meal spent £95.20 on average, rising to £126 among Gen Z and £118 among Millennials.¹ Restaurants see this impact first-hand, with 51% of hospitality workers saying their restaurant drives footfall or spending at nearby businesses. According to UKHospitality, hospitality is the UK’s third-largest employer, with restaurants employing 1.3 million people and contributing £44 billion to the economy annually. Restaurants Drive Community and Personal Wellbeing Restaurants provide spaces where people meet, celebrate and connect. More than half (56%) of UK diners are likely to book a meal out to feel better when stressed or low, rising to 71% among Gen Z diners.¹ If their favourite local restaurant disappeared tomorrow, 53% would miss the atmosphere and character it brings. Dr Martha Newson, Associate Professor of Psychology at the University of Greenwich , explains: “Sharing a meal at a restaurant is one of the oldest ways of bringing people together, because sitting around a table lets us focus on each other. Our research with over 10,000 people worldwide found face-to-face contact remains a strong predictor of wellbeing, as social bonds deepen through eye contact and shared experiences.” The Balancing Act for Restaurants While restaurants support their local areas, they are also navigating significant pressures. OpenTable’s research found that if VAT were reduced from 20% and restaurants passed the savings on through lower menu prices, 39% of diners would eat out more often, while a further 22% would spend more when they did. The report also explores how restaurants could use potential VAT savings. According to the research, 42% would primarily use a reduction to protect or increase staff wages and hours, 31% would lower menu prices for customers and 30% would reduce how often they need to raise prices. An award-winning master of Cantonese cuisine whose distinguished career has seen him helm some of the city’s most respected Chinese dining establishments, Chef Lau brings a fresh perspective, two decades of experience and vibrant energy to the kitchen. Blending both innovation and tradition, his core culinary philosophy is grounded in three essential chapters – craft, heritage and memory – that unite to expand the possibilities and showcase the evolution of Cantonese cuisine. These fundamentals underpin a newly unveiled à la carte menu which retains signature classics for convivial celebrations, reimagines family favourites with nostalgic warmth, and introduces inventive creations that heighten the excitement of fine Chinese dining. Watching elders transform simple, fresh ingredients into a banquet of rich flavours – and seeing the joy it brought to loved ones – deeply moved him. This early realisation that delicious food brings happiness and nostalgia nourishes the soul ignited his lifelong passion for cooking. Chef Lau’s career in Cantonese gastronomy spans leading hospitality brands including The Hong Kong Bankers Club, Hong Kong Parkview and the Clearwater Bay Golf & Country Club. He honed his expertise at the Chinese Culinary Institute under the Vocational Training Council, completing advanced master classes and the Master Chef Course in Chinese Cuisine, where he was honoured as Outstanding Trainee of the 10th programme. His talent has earned widespread industry recognition, with consecutive gold and silver awards at the Vocational Training Council’s Asian Culinary Exchange from 2017 to 2019. Dedicated to promoting Cantonese culinary culture, he serves on the committees of the Asia Art of Cuisine Society and the Hong Kong Chinese Chefs Association, and was a judge at the 2019 Hong Kong International Culinary Classic. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Serve First , the operational excellence platform for customer experience across multi-location service businesses, today announced the expansion of its US operations. Brad Christian joins as Managing Director and will lead Serve First in the US from its office in Alpharetta, GA. Brad brings more than 20 years of experience working with clients in the customer experience industry. He was previously Chief Customer Officer at a customer experience consultancy and Chief Commercial Officer for the experience practice of a global market research firm. He has helped brands design and deploy measurement systems that drive strategic insight and deliver real business performance improvement. The US office supports the global expansion of existing client programs. Serve First is building US customer success and marketing teams to serve those and other US-based clients. Brad will work with brands across restaurants, hotels and hospitality, convenience stores and retail petroleum, and facilities management. Most US operators already measure plenty, through surveys, audits, mystery shops and review tracking. The problem is that many times nothing changes at the location because of it. The report arrives next month, and the site manager never sees it. Serve First captures every signal in one platform, from guest feedback and audits to mystery shopping. EVA, the analyst built into the platform, measures each location against the brand’s own standards, finds where it falls short and why, and builds the plan to fix it. The fix goes to the person who can make it, with proof it got done. “Traditional CX programs have many times been more of an academic exercise than a true focus on actually impacting the customer experience,” said Brad Christian, Managing Director, Serve First. “These programs have been optimized for collecting data, but they lack the actionability to drive meaningful change at the front line. Metrics matter, but meaning matters more. When teams have the feedback, the right tasks and the support to change how they work, brands deliver better customer experiences.” “Brad knows what it takes to turn customer experience programs into real change at every location,” said Erol Ayvaz, CEO, Serve First. “Expanding our US operations under his leadership is the next step in Serve First’s global growth, and it gives our US clients a team on the ground.” The post Brad Christian Joins Serve First as Managing Partner to Lead U.S. Expansion appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: 5 Lessons in Leadership from WiRL Keynote Speaker Meg Farren
articles.titleKo: 5 Lessons in Leadership from WiRL Keynote Speaker Meg Farren
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Meg Farren’s path to president of Taco Bell North America ran through JPMorgan, strategy consulting, luxury desserts, grocery retail, and a decade at KFC, where she led a brand turnaround. Then came her biggest move yet: a transatlantic relocation with her family to lead one of the most beloved brands in the world. In a conversation with QSR magazine earlier this year , she reflected on what she has learned along the way. Listen before you lead When Farren started at Taco Bell, she skipped the big pronouncements and went on a listening tour, traveling with second- and third-generation franchisees and learning from managers. “Sometimes you see people come into a new role and feel like they have to prove themselves by telling others what they should be doing,” Farren says. “But the heart of great trust and collaboration is an ability to listen really well and slowly start to say, ‘Have we tried this?’” Registration is now open for Year 4 of the Women in Restaurant Leadership Summit! Bring your whole self to work Farren doesn’t pretend the juggle isn’t real, and she doesn’t expect her team to either. Instead, she tries to create space for openness and vulnerability, starting with her own. “I am a whole person, not just a work person, and most people are juggling the same kinds of trade-offs and priorities at home that I am,” Farren says. “I try to be a role model to my team that yes, we’re all trying to make our lives work.” Stay healthily dissatisfied Taco Bell can turn a great idea around in two weeks, which is rare for a company of its size. Farren credits a culture that never settles and isn’t afraid to disrupt the status quo through thoughtful innovation. “Taco Bell operates like an $18 billion startup, and to execute brilliantly at our size requires a certain culture and level of partnership across the entire business,” Farren says. “There is this constant healthy dissatisfaction with the status quo, and every franchisee can tell you that we are relentlessly innovating for the next generation of growth.” Never underestimate a thank-you To Farren, culture isn’t a corporate slogan. It’s a set of daily behaviors, shaped at every level of the organization in ways seen and unseen, and recognition is one of the most powerful. “You don’t always show up in your best form every day,” Farren says, “but I do try to make sure all voices are heard in the room, that I foster a culture of recognition, and I’m saying ‘thank you’ and recognizing the contributions of others.” Take the big leap, even when life is messy Farren spent six months commuting from London while her kids finished the school year, building relationships over Zoom while managing what she calls “life admin” and big emotions. “I was getting to know a new organization and learning how to navigate these relationships while driving great performance and delivering well for your team and customers—all while managing a huge family transition,” Farren reflects. “I have depths of resilience, and I’ve been lucky to land with a team who cares about me … it’s been a big step up, but totally worth it.” Hear more from Farren live in Scottsdale. She will deliver the afternoon keynote at WiRL 2027, Feb. 7-9, 2027, at the Grand Hyatt Scottsdale Resort, alongside fellow keynoters Nivera Wallani and Amy Ellis Durini of KFC. WiRL has sold out three years running, and registrations are outpacing every previous year. Save your seat here. For guests who make the most of Halloween night, Chipotle has November 1 covered with $0 delivery fees on digital orders. Some Halloween traditions are worth keeping. Boorito is back. For more than 25 years, fans of Chipotle Mexican Grill have dressed up in costume and shown up for Boorito. The fan-favorite Chipotday — the brand’s term for the food holidays and cultural moments it celebrates throughout the year, returns to participating Chipotle restaurants across the U.S. on October 31. Fans know the drill. The rules are frighteningly simple: Wear a costume. Visit Chipotle after 3 p.m. local time on Halloween. Scan your Chipotle Rewards member card at checkout. Score a $6 entrée. 1 For guests who make the most of Halloween night, Chipotle has November 1 covered with $0 delivery fees on digital orders. 2 “We love that Chipotle has become part of so many fans’ Halloween traditions,” said Stephanie Perdue, Senior Vice President, Brand Marketing. “The passion around Boorito inspires us to find new ways to celebrate and surprise our fans year after year.” Boorito Lore 2000 – Boorito began as a burrito-themed costume contest. 2020 – Boorito went fully digital for the first time, inviting fans to virtually trick-or-treat for BOGO codes. 2021 – Boorito entered the metaverse with a virtual Chipotle restaurant. 2023 – Boorito expanded with late-night hours in select college towns. 2024 – Chipotle introduced meme-inspired costumes. 2026 – Chipotle summoned the return of its $6 margaritas in select cities leading up to Boorito 2026. 1 – Chipotle Rewards members can receive one (1) entrée item for US$6 when appearing in costume, as determined by restaurant, and scanning for Rewards at point of sale at participating U.S. locations. Valid only on October 31, 2026 after 3:00 p.m. local time through restaurant closing; redemption is subject to availability. Limit one discounted item per costumed guest. Redeemable in-restaurant only; not valid for kids meals, catering, mobile, online or delivery orders. Extra cost for guacamole (except for veggie entreés), queso, extra meat or other modifiers. Taxes, gratuities, and any sides are not included and are the responsibility of the guest. Purchased entrées are eligible for Chipotle Rewards points; the promotion may not otherwise be combined with other coupons, promotions, or special offers. Additional restrictions may apply; void where prohibited. 2 – Higher menu prices are charged for delivery; additional service and other fees applied at checkout as well (except in CA, CO, CT, MA, MN and VA). Available only on November 1, 2026, within Chipotle’s delivery areas from participating U.S. locations, during normal operating hours for such locations. Minimum order $10 USD excluding tax and fees; maximum item numbers apply as well. Deliveries and redemptions are subject to availability. Offer is not valid on catering or Burritos by the Box orders. Redemptions of Chipotle Rewards and other promotional offers may be included in a qualifying delivery order but do not count towards satisfaction of minimum purchase requirements. Valid only on the Chipotle website or the Chipotle app; not valid on orders placed via third-party delivery platforms. Chipotle reserves the right to modify or terminate this offer at any time without notice. Additional restrictions may apply; void where prohibited. articles.title: Cheba Hut to Open in South Scottsdale, Arizona
articles.titleKo: Cheba Hut to Open in South Scottsdale, Arizona
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . A fresh place to grab a bite, kick back with a cold drink and stay awhile is headed to South Scottsdale. Cheba Hut “Toasted” Subs , the counter-culture sandwich shop known for its chill atmosphere, cottonmouth cures, and bold flavors that hit just right, arrives Oct. 26, planted at 2200 N. Scottsdale Road, Suite 110, south of Oak Street and north of McDowell Road. Just south of Old Town Scottsdale, with its world-class shopping, buzzing nightlife, major events and tightly packed arts scene, the restaurant sits close to some of the region’s go-to outings. Guests can fuel up before visiting the Phoenix Zoo, swing by after exploring Papago Park, stop in on the way to Scottsdale Stadium during Cactus League season or make a side quest out of browsing The Antique Trove, Scottsdale Pawn Shop and Sidewalk Surfer Skate Shop. South Scottsdale marks the 13 th Cheba Hut in the Phoenix area and the latest milestone in a fast run for franchise owners Justin and Michelle Lemos, who now operate five shops in less than two years. They launched in North Scottsdale in February 2025, followed with the 101 and Shea a month later, additionally taking over Paradise Valley from Cheba Hut headquarters in January and adding Arcadia in June. “Long before we owned a Cheba Hut, we were regulars who came in for the best sandwich we’d ever had and stuck around for the music, the art and a crew that actually loved being there,” said Justin Lemos, franchise owner. “Those folks are still what it’s all about for us. We promote from within and hire locally, so every opening creates a path for someone on our team to step into something bigger. South Scottsdale means more homegrown careers taking root right alongside the subs.” Like every destination across the Chebaverse, the location tells a local story on its walls. Joshua Finley, who has left his mark on more than 50 Cheba Hut locations nationwide, reimagining the surrounding Old Town “village” as a scene straight out of an anime series. Additional Cheba Hut references fill the frame, along with Easter eggs that reward a second look (and maybe a third). Beyond the centerpiece mural, the space doubles as a showcase for Valley creators, featuring work by pop cannabis artist Aubri Swell ( @MaryJaneArtCompany ) and wood artist Basile Taylor ( @BasileMakesThings ). The owners plan to extend that spotlight to more makers and artisans, with original art for sale so fans can take a little piece of Cheba home. Behind the counter, a full-service bar pours liquor, beer and wine from shelves meant to keep changing. The team will keep adding bottles and taps based on Arizona favorites and crowd requests, so the lineup grows right alongside the neighborhood. For first-timers, Cheba Hut serves more than 30 signature toasted subs named for classic strains and available in Nug (4-inch), Pinner (8-inch) and Blunt (12-inch) sizes. Regulars reach for the White Widow, stacked with chicken, bacon and ranch. The Kali Mist turns up the heat on a club piled with turkey, pepper jack and more of that bacon. The Dank layers pepperoni, salami, marinara and melted mozzarella into a pizza-inspired build, and the Griefo goes green with cream cheese, avocado and fresh vegetables. For something beyond the main event, the menu has plenty of options built for late-night cravings, from pretzel nugs and garlic cheese bread to Krispy Bars, goo balls and cookies, plus the Kool-Aid that’s been quenching thirst since day one. Cheba Hut South Scottsdale will be open Sunday through Thursday from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m., with extended hours until midnight Friday and Saturday. With its mix of toasted sandwiches, unserious humor, neighborhood-first mindset and a disrespectful mascot named “Flip the Bird,” Cheba Hut is ready to make Scottsdale a little more dank, one sub at a time.
