articles.title: Maine’s White Barn Inn Welcomes Executive Chef Cornelia Sühr
articles.titleKo: Maine’s White Barn Inn Welcomes Executive Chef Cornelia Sühr
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . From a working barn to celebrated culinary destination, White Barn Inn, Auberge Collection has spent more than five decades evolving alongside the landscape that surrounds it. Once home to livestock, horses and chickens – and later used as an ice creamery – the historic barn was restored in 1973 and transformed into White Barn Inn Restaurant, establishing a legacy of elevated dining rooted in Maine’s agricultural and coastal bounty. This autumn, the acclaimed restaurant enters a new culinary chapter under Executive Chef Cornelia Sühr, whose international fine-dining career brings a distinctly European perspective to the New England landmark. German-born, Sühr has worked in some of the world’s most acclaimed kitchens, including Alain Ducasse at The Dorchester and The Savoy in London, and later at The Carlyle, A Rosewood Hotel in New York, where she became the hotel’s first female Chef de Cuisine. She went on to lead kitchens at Jean-Georges Philadelphia at Four Seasons Hotel Philadelphia, before joining The Surf Club Restaurant by Thomas Keller in Florida. Now, taking the helm at White Barn Inn, Auberge Collection, Sühr is translating years of classical training and global experience through the lens of coastal Maine, allowing the landscape and its changing seasons to dictate the menu. As autumn settles over Maine, the signature Coast Line & Forest tasting menu evolves to reflect the season, tracing a progression from the coastline to the deeper flavors of land, smoke, and fire. Drawing on Maine’s farms, waters, and forests, Sühr uses techniques including fermentation, preservation, smoking, and live-fire cooking to bring depth and character to ingredients at their peak. The menu continues to evolve with seasonal availability, allowing each harvest to shape the experience. Priced at $250 per guest, with an optional $125 wine pairing, the current menu features: Halibut | Razor Clams | Potato | Dill This dish captures the character of Maine’s coastline while incorporating the elegance of classical French cooking. The halibut offers natural sweetness and a delicate, flaky texture, while the razor clams bring subtle brininess and a slightly firmer bite. Potato adds an earthy, comforting element suited to the fall season, while dill provides freshness and a gentle aromatic lift. The sauce draws inspiration from traditional French moules marinières , using shellfish, white wine, and aromatics to create depth without detracting from the purity of the fish. The result strikes a balance between simplicity and refinement, bringing together familiar coastal New England ingredients through a delicate, contemporary interpretation of French technique that allows the natural flavors of the sea to remain the focus. Stonington Lobster | Parisian Gnocchi | Sea Beans | Fennel Sourcing lobster from Stonington, known as one of Maine’s premier lobster fishing towns, is particularly special. With its deeply rooted fishing heritage, the small coastal community represents much of what makes Maine’s culinary identity unique: tradition, craftsmanship, and a close connection to the sea. Stonington lobster is prized for its natural sweetness and beautiful texture, with succulent, tender meat that retains a delicate firmness and almost buttery richness. Parisian gnocchi introduces a light, airy texture that contrasts beautifully with the lobster, while sea beans bring a crisp bite and subtle ocean salinity. Fennel adds freshness and gentle anise notes. The sauce draws inspiration from a traditional Provençal bourride , lending silky, velvety richness that enhances the lobster’s natural sweetness without overpowering it. The dish brings together two coastal traditions: Stonington’s fishing heritage and the elegance of southern French cuisine. articles.title: Bar Prince Unveils Mythical Legends: A New Cocktail Menu Inspired By Scotland’s Most Enchanting Folklore
articles.titleKo: Bar Prince Unveils Mythical Legends: A New Cocktail Menu Inspired By Scotland’s Most Enchanting Folklore
articles.originalSummary: Following the success of last year’s Connected Icons , Bar Prince at The Balmoral invites guests into a world of myth, magic and storytelling with the launch of its newest cocktail menu, Mythical Legends . Launching this autumn, Mythical Legends draws inspiration from Scotland’s most enduring folklore, transforming legendary creatures and ancient tales into an immersive cocktail experience. From unicorns and selkies to witches, dragons and kelpies, the menu celebrates the stories that have captivated imaginations for generations. Overseen by Head Bartender Mattia Rovaris, each signature cocktail has been individually created by Bar Prince’s mixologists, with every serve inspired by a different Scottish legend. Guests are invited to discover the inspiration behind each creation, with every drink offering its own connection to Scotland’s rich mythical heritage. The theme extends beyond the cocktails themselves. Bespoke illustrations bring each character to life, transforming the menu into a contemporary storybook. Each copy has been meticulously handcrafted by Edinburgh’s Crawford Bookbinders, whose traditional techniques and attention to detail add another layer of craftsmanship, echoing Scotland’s long tradition of storytelling and artistry. Enhancing the experience further is a bespoke Mythical Legends Scent Mist, inspired by Scotland’s ancient forests, mist-covered lochs and legendary landscapes. Blending notes of cedarwood, chamomile and sandalwood with Scots pine, citrus and warming spice, it has been designed to transport guests into the world that inspired the cocktails. Capturing the spirit of Scotland’s wild landscapes and folklore through new techniques and evocative flavour combinations, highlights include The Untamed One , a shimmering tribute to Scotland’s national animal, the unicorn, blending Scottish vodka with coconut water, white chocolate, banana and lime leaf for an elegant serve. Double Identity , inspired by the selkie’s existence between land and sea, reimagines the whisky sour with coastal Scotch whisky, honey, citrus and warming spice. Meanwhile, Kingdom’s Cauldron draws on the tale of the Witch of Fife, combining whisky, botanicals, chocolate, vanilla and caramel into a rich and mysterious after-dark cocktail. Elsewhere, guests can discover the inspiration behind Messy-Nessie , a bright and herbaceous whisky highball inspired by Scotland’s most famous monster, or enjoy Fairy Queen , a decadent take on the Mai Tai featuring aged rum, roasted Brazil nuts and dark cacao. More than a cocktail menu, Mythical Legends is an invitation to explore Scotland’s legendary past through flavour, artistry and imagination. Continuing Bar Prince’s commitment to innovative cocktail storytelling, each drink reveals a new chapter in Scotland’s rich folklore. Mattia Rovaris, Head Bartender at Bar Prince, said: “Building on the success of Connected Icons, Mythical Legends gave our team the opportunity to tell a new chapter of Scotland’s story through the lens of folklore. Each cocktail has been created by a different member of the bar team, making the menu a true collective of ideas, creativity and personal interpretation. Paired with bespoke illustrations and scent, we’ve created an experience that invites guests to discover something new with every serve.” Discover the stories, flavours and aromas behind Scotland’s most captivating folklore at Bar Prince at The Balmoral. Mythical Legends launches this autumn. For more information or to reserve a table, visit: https://www.roccofortehotels.com/hotels-and-resorts/the-balmoral-hotel/dining/bar-prince/cocktail-menu/

Alexa Bunting’s career began in sales at fine jewelry retailers, where she grew curious about the psychology behind why customers buy. That curiosity sent her back to school for a master’s degree in integrated marketing. Her first taste of food and beverage marketing came at Black Rifle Coffee Co., where she led marketing for the brand’s retail coffee shops. She dove headfirst into a fast-moving environment with a constant rotation of new beverages, new menu items, and seasonal flair to promote. But her biggest takeaway was how to build a community and tell a story. “I learned the importance of building a community around your brand,” Bunting says. “Black Rifle has a strong customer base, and I learned pretty quickly that although sales and discounts drive consumers in, it’s the brand that keeps them coming back.” Today, Bunting is the director of brand marketing at P.F. Chang’s. “That’s what I’ve carried through to P.F. Chang’s,” she says. “The question here is, how do we build something that goes beyond our food? How do we create a community and that emotional storytelling component that keeps people coming back and supporting us? Those little moments where you can be involved with your community make your marketing so much stronger, and your brand so much stronger.” There, she approaches marketing as a sequence: It starts with a strong menu, followed by a compelling story that draws guests in, then operational execution and interactive touches in the dining room. It’s a fully integrated approach that spans every channel, but it all starts with the brief. Join women leaders at WiRL! Reserve your spot today. That approach is part of a broader resurgence at P.F. Chang’s . Under CEO Jim Mazany and chief marketing officer Holly Smith, who joined in January, the chain posted a 7.7 percent same-store sales gain in the second quarter, with traffic up 6.8 percent. “Holly and I sat down and thought to ourselves: How do we create something that’s uniquely ownable to P.F. Chang’s?” Bunting says. “How do we tie it back to something culturally relevant that only we can own?” Working with brand manager Olivia Liu, the team built 2026 around a series of seasonal campaigns inspired by Japanese culture. It started in February with Flavor In Bloom , a nod to Japan’s cherry blossom season that paired best-sellers like Chang’s Lettuce Wraps with spring cocktails, led by a Cherry Blossom Martini. Summer brought the city lights and street culture of Tokyo with Summer in Tokyo , which combined a new seasonal menu with the debut of the Sushi Boat, a shareable platter that arrives tableside in a cloud of dry ice. “At the heart of every campaign we’re doing, we give the consumers an educational element or a story that will pull it all together for them,” Bunting says. “We’ve really started to color a little outside of the lines with our LTOs and integrate them with things that are P.F. articles.title: Bread Zeppelin Announces $2 Discount on Chicken Caesar Zeppelin Combo
articles.titleKo: Bread Zeppelin Announces $2 Discount on Chicken Caesar Zeppelin Combo
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . While other sandwich chains are introducing scaled-down options to reach a lower price, Bread Zeppelin is keeping its Chicken Caesar combo exactly the size guests know and charging less for it. From Oct. 21-28, guests at participating Dallas-Fort Worth locations can get the Chicken Caesar Zeppelin combo for $2 less than the usual $9.99. The promotion follows the Oct. 12 rollout of Jersey Mike’s $7.99 Mini Bundle , which features a smaller cold sub and a bag of chips. Bread Zeppelin is matching that price and upping the protein — its Caesar packs 41 grams, roughly 128% more than the 18-gram minimum Jersey Mike’s reports for those sandwiches. “I’m a Jersey Mike’s fan. I’ve got the rewards account to prove it,” said co-founder Troy Charhon. “But I’ll put our deal up against theirs any day. We know many of our neighbors are being more mindful of how they spend their hard-earned money. We want to give them something they can feel good about choosing, without having to compromise on quality or value.” The build features their full-sized toasted baguette, cored out and loaded with romaine, Parmesan, Caesar dressing and chicken marinated and grilled in-house, never frozen — also available as a salad bowl. Even the croutons have a backstory. They’re housemade from the bread cores pulled during prep, so nothing goes to waste. “When we sat down to put this offer together, making the Zeppelin smaller never even came up,” said co-founder Andrew Schoellkopf. “Same delicious baguette, same grilled chicken, same 41 grams of protein. We’d rather just charge less for it and let our guests taste for themselves what all the hype is about.” For more information or to view the menu, visit breadzeppelin.com or follow @breadzeppelin on social media. *While supplies last. Additional restrictions may apply. Available for dine-in, take-out and in app purchases only, no third party orders accepted. articles.title: KNEAD Hospitality + Design Names Juan Pablo Loza Culinary Director of Mi Vida
articles.titleKo: KNEAD Hospitality + Design Names Juan Pablo Loza Culinary Director of Mi Vida
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . KNEAD Hospitality + Design has announced that Chef Juan Pablo Loza has joined Mi Vida as Culinary Director. This is the first menu change of its kind for both KNEAD and Mi Vida since opening in 2018 as the group continues its ongoing market expansion with locations across Washington, D.C., Philadelphia, and Virginia Beach. The exciting new chapter is a culmination of seven years of a professional relationship and friendship with KNEAD Hospitality + Design co-principals, Jason Berry and Michael Reginbogin, who first connected with Loza during his tenure at Rosewood Mayakoba. “We’ve known Chef Juan Pablo for many years and have always admired his approach to cooking and hospitality,” said Berry. “We’ve had the opportunity to watch his career evolve since we first met him at Rosewood Mayakoba, so having him lead the next chapter of Mi Vida’s culinary direction feels like a very natural fit.” Loza grew up in Mexico City’s Xochimilco neighborhood, spending afternoons at the local market with his mother and grandmother cleaning beans and prepping tomatillos. He began training at 16 under French chef Olivier Lombard, followed by four years in the high-pressure kitchen of Mexico City’s Lasser. He went on to win the Guillermo Ríos Young Mexican Chef Competition, a national competition hosted by Ambrosia Centro Culinario and judged by chefs including Enrique Olvera and Ricardo Muñoz Zurita. After culinary positions at Le Cirque, Ciboulette and L’Olivier, Loza built an international hospitality career with Rosewood Hotels & Resorts, Belmond and Auberge Resorts Collection across Mexico, the Caribbean and South America. He spent eight years as Executive Chef and Director of Culinary Operations at Rosewood Mayakoba, overseeing six restaurants and bars—including Zapote Bar, ranked No. 11 on North America’s 50 Best Bars in 2023 and 2024—and transforming a beach food truck he launched into the $8 million Aqui Me Quedo beach club. Most recently, he served as Director of Culinary Experiences at Chileno Bay Resort & Residences before opening Señora Cocina, Casa & Cantina in San José del Cabo in March 2025. His extensive experience across international luxury resort markets gives him a unique perspective on bridging American diners’ tastes with authentic, regional Mexican flavors and ingredients. Loza will bring what he calls his own version of Mexico to the Mi Vida menu – lighter, brighter cooking built on vegetables, acidity, and technique. His approach challenges misconceptions that Mexican cooking is “heavy” by highlighting its fresh, vibrant nature. He’s rebalancing the menu’s traditional weight, turning some of Mi Vida’s richer dishes into starters while building new main courses designed to feel lighter without sacrificing flavor: a chile-rubbed salmon over avocado-citrus purée with a cucumber and preserved lemon salad; ribs reimagined through the lens of tacos al pastor, finished with charred pineapple and cured onion; a crispy pork shank recast as carnitas alongside a bright, citrus-lifted salsa verde; and a banana leaf-wrapped barbacoa short rib served with a chilled, chickpea salad for contrast. A guacamole built with grasshoppers and chorizo, “Guacamole Oaxaca,” reflects his belief that trying something unfamiliar is part of what makes dining out worth it. Mi Vida, Spanish for “my life,” is a fitting name for what Loza calls deeply personal cooking. By merging his culinary vision with KNEAD’s signature design, Loza is looking forward to being a part of DC’s thriving culinary scene. “Cooking has always been a deeply personal expression of who I am, where I come from, and the experiences that have shaped me,” said Loza. “I’m excited to bring my perspective to Mi Vida, while honoring the cuisine I grew up eating. The new wrap marks the latest step in a partnership designed from the beginning to go beyond a traditional athlete endorsement. Just Salad, the fast-casual restaurant chain committed to making everyday health and sustainability possible, brings The Clutch Wrap to its menu, a limited-time offering created by Jalen Brunson, point guard for the New York Knicks, 2026 NBA Champion and Finals MVP, and Just Salad partner and equity owner. Launching as the NBA season tips off and available at all Just Salad locations through December 31, The Clutch Wrap brings the partnership directly to the menu for the first time, giving guests and fans a new way to experience what Brunson and the New York-born brand are literally building together. The Clutch Wrap layers baby spinach and shredded cabbage with oven roasted chicken, roasted corn, hot honey goat cheese and spicy harissa pita, finished with Just Salad’s homemade Chipotle Vinaigrette. The combination delivers sweet heat, crunch and bold flavor in every bite, featuring 48 grams of protein and 36 grams of fiber. “I wanted this to be something I’d actually order with a lot of flavor, plenty of protein and just the right amount of heat, so we got to work until we got it just right,” said Jalen Brunson, 2026 NBA Champion, NBA Finals MVP and Captain of the New York Knicks . “It’s unreal to now have something on the menu that fans can go in and try for themselves, but starting the season with The Clutch Wrap felt like the right move.” The new wrap marks the latest step in a partnership designed from the beginning to go beyond a traditional athlete endorsement. Brunson joined Just Salad as a partner and equity owner in June before debuting their first creative campaign , “ New York Always Knew ,” built around the fans who believed in both Brunson and the brand long before everyone else caught on. “From day one, this partnership was never about simply putting Jalen’s name on something,” said Nick Kenner, Founder and CEO of Just Salad . “When we announced the partnership, we said Jalen’s impact would become part of the brand in ways our guests would start to see over time. The Clutch Wrap is another step in bringing that to life, and it’s time for guests across all of our locations to taste it for themselves.” The Clutch Wrap continues a relationship centered on shared values, authenticity and building together, as Brunson closely worked alongside Just Salad’s culinary team to craft it. Brunson is expected to continue engaging with Just Salad’s leadership and beyond, visiting restaurants, connecting with guests and continuing to bring his perspective into the business over time. The wrap launch will also be supported by a new connected TV (CTV) spot that puts Brunson’s reputation for coming through in clutch moments front and center. Building on September’s documentary-style ‘New York Always Knew’ campaign, the new creative focuses on the clutch performances that have defined his career and now his first signature Just Salad menu item. The spot will run across select CTV channels as well as out-of-home advertising across Just Salad markets. At Just Salad, health and sustainability are built into every meal, serving approachable, flavor-packed meals. This means homemade dressings, prepped-daily produce, chef-designed recipes and fresh, flavorful ingredients. A leader in sustainable dining for two decades, Just Salad is best known for its reusable bowl program , which rewards guests with a free topping for every reuse, proving that small choices can add up to meaningful impact. Enjoy The Clutch Wrap through December 31 in-restaurant, via mobile app or online at Order.JustSalad.com. articles.title: Olo’s New App Could Change How Restaurants Compete for Digital Orders
articles.titleKo: Olo’s New App Could Change How Restaurants Compete for Digital Orders
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Olo app launches on Tuesday. More than two decades after Noah Glass first envisioned a digital network connecting restaurants and their customers, the Olo founder and CEO is preparing to bring that idea directly to consumers. On Tuesday, Olo will launch its namesake mobile app, giving customers a single destination to order pickup and delivery from restaurants across its network. The platform introduces what Glass calls “second-party” ordering, a model that combines the convenience of third-party marketplaces with the economics and customer relationships associated with restaurants’ direct ordering channels. The proposition is straightforward. Customers can browse multiple brands without paying inflated menu prices, and operators receive the full profit from each order without marketplace commissions. Olo, meanwhile, collects a 5 percent fee from consumers. The launch represents a significant expansion of Olo’s business, taking a company known primarily as a behind-the-scenes technology provider into a consumer-facing market dominated by DoorDash and Uber Eats. Glass says the concept dates to an executive summary he wrote in December 2003, years before Olo became an established restaurant technology provider. “To say that this is like a nearly 23-year dream come true this launch Tuesday is not hyperbole,” Glass says. Olo’s acquisition by private equity firm Thoma Bravo helped accelerate the initiative. Glass says the shift from a publicly traded software provider to a privately owned company created greater flexibility to pursue a network business model. His conviction was significant enough that he and his family reinvested 75 percent of their transaction proceeds into Olo. The immediate opportunity lies in addressing longstanding friction in restaurant digital ordering. Individual restaurant apps can be expensive to acquire customers for and difficult to sustain engagement with. Third-party marketplaces offer considerable consumer reach, but restaurants sacrifice margins through commissions, advertising expenses, and limited access to customer information. Olo believes there is an underserved audience between dedicated restaurantttt loyalists and consumers committed to subscription programs such as DashPass and Uber One. “There’s a big group in the middle, I would argue, and probably the majority of the overall population that wants the convenience of being able to order from many different brands in one place,” Glass says. Glass doesn’t view the app primarily as a vehicle to shift existing transactions away from restaurant-owned channels. He expects the lower cost of ordering to encourage additional occasions among consumers who have become discouraged by delivery prices. The potential savings are a significant component of Olo’s consumer pitch. Glass says menu markups on traditional marketplaces frequently range from 15 to 30 percent, adding costs that customers may mistakenly attribute to restaurants. He points to an $85 delivery order he recently placed through the Olo app that cost $19.34 less than the equivalent marketplace transaction, even after Olo’s 5 percent fee. The platform will disclose that fee during checkout and inform customers that ordering directly from a restaurant is the least expensive option. Delivery fees and tips still apply when customers choose delivery, but Olo avoids the additional menu markups that can make marketplace orders considerably more expensive. Another advantage is that Olo isn’t starting its consumer network from scratch. articles.title: Carlos Boozer Takes on Role of Chief Growth Officer at Impeccable
articles.titleKo: Carlos Boozer Takes on Role of Chief Growth Officer at Impeccable
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Impeccable announced that co-founder Carlos Boozer has taken on the full-time role of chief growth officer, expanding his involvement with the vertically integrated real estate and restaurant platform as it continues to grow throughout the Southeast. In his new role, Boozer will work across Impeccable Capital’s diverse portfolio, including Impeccable Development and Impeccable Restaurant Group, to strengthen the companies’ public presence, build strategic relationships and identify new business opportunities. He will also participate in executive planning and work directly with leaders across Impeccable’s investment, development and restaurant businesses. “Carlos has been an integral part of Impeccable from the beginning,” said Rob Tanner, founder and CEO of Impeccable. “He has an extraordinary ability to connect with people and see opportunity across industries. We want that perspective involved as we grow our existing businesses and explore what comes next.” “I helped build Impeccable because I believed in what we could create together,” Boozer said. “I’m excited to take a bigger role in the day-to-day business, spending time with our teams, showing up in the communities we serve and bringing the right people together to help us grow.” As chief growth officer, Boozer will help drive Impeccable’s growth by using his visibility, credibility and relationships to open doors to investors, strategic partners and new business opportunities. Working closely with CEO Rob Tanner and the company’s leadership team, he will build key relationships, make qualified introductions and evaluate potential new lines of business. Boozer will represent Impeccable at conferences, speaking engagements, media appearances, investor meetings and company events, including restaurant openings. He will also visit restaurants and development projects, strengthen connections with employees, franchise brands and community leaders, and participate in executive planning to help turn promising opportunities into long-term growth. A two-time NBA All-Star and Olympic gold medalist, Boozer played 13 seasons in the NBA for the Cleveland Cavaliers, Utah Jazz, Chicago Bulls and Los Angeles Lakers. He represented the United States at the 2004 and 2008 Olympic Games, winning bronze in Athens and gold in Beijing. The 2008 U.S. Olympic men’s basketball team, known as the “Redeem Team,” was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame as part of its class of 2025. Since retiring from professional basketball, Boozer has focused on entrepreneurship, franchising and commercial real estate. As a co-founder and investor in Impeccable Capital, Impeccable Development and Impeccable Restaurant Group, he also serves on Impeccable Development’s board of directors and real estate committee. Boozer’s expanded role comes as Impeccable continues to scale its real estate development and restaurant operations throughout the Southeast. Impeccable Development has more than 25 active projects, with approximately 2 million square feet developed or under development. The company specializes in ground-up retail, restaurant and select mixed-use developments, working with national and regional brands throughout its portfolio. Boozer’s transition into a full-time role reflects Impeccable’s plans to expand its development and restaurant businesses, strengthen its investment platform and explore new lines of business. Bringing him into the company’s day-to-day leadership allows him to apply his relationships, visibility and credibility more directly to those priorities. As chief growth officer, he will help attract investors, build strategic partnerships and identify opportunities that support Impeccable’s next phase of growth. Looking ahead, 2027 and 2028 are shaping up to be an exciting next chapter, with major acquisitions, new brands and strategic partnership

articles.title: What the Meritage Chapter 11 Teaches Restaurant Franchisees
articles.titleKo: What the Meritage Chapter 11 Teaches Restaurant Franchisees
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Meritage shows that a single day can decide whether a debtor has hundreds of restaurants to reorganize or none at all. One day after Wendy’s cut it loose, the operator of 314 Wendy’s-franchised restaurants filed for bankruptcy to keep its franchises alive. The case tests a question many distressed franchisees face: Can bankruptcy save a franchise the franchisor says is already gone? Timing and venue are critical. Quality Is Our Recipe, LLC (“QIOR”), a Wendy’s subsidiary, notified Meritage Hospitality Group on Sept. 16, 2026, that all its franchise agreements were terminated “effective immediately.” Meritage, which operates 314 franchised restaurants in 15 states, filed chapter 11 the next day in the Western District of Michigan to stay termination. In re Meritage Hospitality Group Inc. , No. 26-02947 (Bankr. W.D. Mich.). QIOR claims roughly $146.9 million, including $119.5 million in “continuous operations fees.” The Adversary Proceeding On October 1, 2026, the debtors sued QIOR and Wendy’s seeking declaratory relief that the termination was ineffective, the franchise agreements are estate property and the automatic stay bars enforcement. The dispute traces to an October 2025 payment-default notice and three forbearance letters, the last expiring August 18, 2026. QIOR’s emailed termination notice demanded more than $146 million by Oct. 16, 2026, and tendered a short-term license agreement (“STLA”) through year-end. The debtors allege the termination failed because the agreements required physical (not email) notice; QIOR did not give lenders the required notice and cure opportunity under the consents to collateral assignment; cure periods restarted upon forbearance expiration; and the STLA and QIOR’s reserved purchase option presupposed a continuing relationship. Can Chapter 11 Resurrect a Terminated Franchise Agreement? The answer turns on timing. A franchise agreement not fully terminated at filing becomes estate property under 11 U.S.C. § 541, and the automatic stay (§ 362(a)) bars termination without stay relief. See In re Welcome Group 2, LLC , 660 B.R. 874, 879 (Bankr. S.D. Ohio 2024); In re Mirant Corp. , 440 F.3d 238, 252–53 (5th Cir. 2006). Conversely, contracts that have expired or were validly terminated prior to bankruptcy leave the debtor “with nothing to assume or reject.” In re P.I.N.E., Inc. , 52 B.R. 463, 465 (Bankr. W.D. Mich. 1985). QIOR and Wendy’s respond that the agreements “have been terminated” and are not estate property. Meritage argues that even a valid termination leaves residual interests, including the right to seek reinstatement. Meritage’s fight turns on whether the Sept. 16 notice completed the job or merely started a process interrupted by the stay. The notice reserved QIOR’s options to buy equipment and take over leases, obligations Meritage calls “diametrically inconsistent” with a completed termination. The default notice set state-specific cure periods of 90, 60 and 30 days, later deferred by forbearance, inviting arguments that fresh notice was required. The interim license offer arguably belies a clean break. And the lender-notice argument may prove decisive; QIOR admits the consent language but pleads compliance. Notably, a bare right to terminate may not itself establish “cause” for stay relief under § 362(d)(1). See Mirant , 440 F.3d at 253. Meritage’s Restructuring Strategy and Operations Meritage operates as a debtor in possession, with a strategy of closing or selling underperforming stores, resolving the QIOR dispute, potential market sales and a recapitalization. Its chief restructuring officer calls Wendy’s system access “indispensable to any viable restructuring.” The interim cash collateral order requires closing at least 30 EBITDA-negative stores by Oct. 16; termination of the Wendy’s agreements, or a finding that they were terminated, is a cash collateral

articles.title: New York–Style Pizzeria Barsella to Open Near SMU’s Campus
articles.titleKo: New York–Style Pizzeria Barsella to Open Near SMU’s Campus
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . A new locally-owned restaurant and bar is coming to SMU Boulevard this winter. Barsella, an Italian-American restaurant, New York-style pizzeria and cocktail bar, will open at 5600 SMU Blvd., Suite 120 in Dallas for dinner and late night, with slices from a walk-up window during the day. Barsella is the first hospitality concept from Dallas native Oliver Steinberg. Barsella is meant to work for more than one kind of night. Guests can settle in for dinner and a bottle of wine, meet friends for happy hour, grab a New York-style slice from the window, enjoy spritzes on the patio or end the evening with drinks and late-night bites. “Barsella was designed in hopes of becoming a neighborhood institution, elevated enough for a great dinner or date night, approachable enough to become your regular spot, and lively enough to be where you want to end the night,” says Dallas resident and creator of the concept, Oliver Steinberg. “We wanted to create a place where families, couples, friends and neighbors all feel equally at home, whatever brings them in that night,” he adds. From the dining room to the slice window, each space has its own identity and energy, all served by the same kitchen and consistent approach to food and hospitality. At its core, the new restaurant offers a thoughtful take on Italian-American dining. “The menu is intentionally filled with dishes people know, love and want to order such as rigatoni alla vodka, ravioli and lasagna, yet executed at a high level,” expresses Steinberg. Many dishes take inspiration from iconic New York pizzerias and restaurants the culinary team visited while developing the menu. The goal is food that is craveable and memorable without ever feeling overly complicated or intimidating, paired with an extensive spritz and craft cocktail program and a thoughtfully developed wine list. New York-style pizza isn’t an accessory to the bar or dining room; it is one of the foundations of the concept. Inside, a seven-seat pizza bar offers a more casual way to experience the restaurant, sharing the slice window’s menu along with offerings beyond pizza. Walking up to the slice window is meant to feel like stepping beneath the marquee of a Broadway theater, with bright, theatrical signage recognizable from down the street. The window serves individual slices from a mix of staple pies and rotating specials. The patio, envisioned as a bit of an Italian escape with a pergola and lemon-vine plantings overhead, is a natural place to enjoy one, and large sliding windows connect it to the interior bar. As dinner fades into night, Barsella becomes a late-night spritz and cocktail bar. Live music fills the room most Thursday through Saturday nights, and a dedicated menu of light bites, featuring dishes guests won’t find everywhere else, is served until 2 a.m. An intimate private dining room of approximately 16 seats can also host private dinners, celebrations and events, carrying the same green tones, tile and millwork throughout. Liz Johnson of Wallace Johnson Studio is leading the interior design, drawing on classic Italian-American concepts, New York cafés and European aperitivo culture for a space that feels polished, bright and colorful rather than dark and rustic. Hexagonal mosaic floors, olive-green millwork, green tile and red pleated booths set the tone inside the approximately 3,100-square-foot space which will seat 80 in the main dining room. Barsella is slated to open this winter at 5600 SMU Blvd., Suite 120, Dallas, Texas. Additional details on the menu and opening date will be announced closer to opening. articles.title: Hangry Joe’s New CEO Wants to Build a Better Franchise System, Not Just a Bigger One
articles.titleKo: Hangry Joe’s New CEO Wants to Build a Better Franchise System, Not Just a Bigger One
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Brandon Wihelm was named Hangry Joe's CEO in early October. Brandon Wilhelm wasn’t necessarily looking to take on another major role in the restaurant industry. After spending nearly two decades developing Subway franchise territory across the Midwest, he was considering opportunities outside the business. Then he discovered Hangry Joe’s. Wilhelm traveled to Virginia to explore the emerging hot chicken concept, arriving a day early to secretly visit several restaurants before meeting with the corporate team. He came away impressed with the food, but also saw opportunities to improve the young franchise’s marketing, real estate strategy, and operational infrastructure. That combination eventually led him to become a multi-unit franchisee, equity investor, board member, and, as of October 6, CEO of the growing fast-casual chain. “I went out to Virginia and and tried the food and checked out the brand and it was the best chicken sandwich I ever had,” Wilhelm says. Founded in 2021, Hangry Joe’s has expanded to more than 90 restaurants across over 20 states and international markets, including the United Arab Emirates. Another 20 locations are in the pipeline. But Wilhelm isn’t measuring the company’s future success solely through restaurant count. His immediate priority is creating a more profitable, sustainable franchise system that can support expansion without repeating some of the mistakes that accompanied its early growth. His experience includes overseeing operations strategy for more than 500 Subway restaurants and working with more than 140 franchisees. He also served as president of Hangry Development Texas and acting chief marketing officer of Hangry Joe’s. Those experiences informed a series of proposals he presented to the company’s founders and board over the past year. The discussions eventually resulted in an invitation to implement the plans himself. “I have no real desire to say, ‘OK, we’re going to grow this to a certain level and then we’re going to sell it to private equity.’ That’s never been my goal, and I’ve told those guys from the beginning,” Wilhelm says. Wilhelm’s initial priorities include reducing food costs, improving purchasing efficiency, increasing consumer awareness, and establishing more rigorous development standards. Supply chain improvements represent one of the most immediate opportunities. Historically, individual franchisees have had considerable flexibility in sourcing certain products, creating inconsistencies that can limit the company’s purchasing power. Wilhelm wants greater compliance with approved distribution relationships to negotiate more favorable pricing across the system. The company is also examining freight expenses, including proprietary ingredients that some operators currently purchase by the pallet and ship directly to individual restaurants. articles.title: How Chili’s Took Control of the Cultural Conversation Again
articles.titleKo: How Chili’s Took Control of the Cultural Conversation Again
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Chili’s same-store sales have gained a collective 50 percent over the past three years. So, CMO and EVP George Felix wasn’t dealing in hyperbole when he told investors recently the brand had been “pretty busy.” What Chili’s was up to boils down to a few investment-laden storylines. The company spent $100 million-plus in facilities. It reworked hospitality by pouring back into labor. Chili’s refocused on core execution and menu architecture. But when talking about one of the most-vivid turnarounds in category history, people often start with how loud the brand became. Chili’s in that opening calendar under Felix and CEO Kevin Hochmann—who worked together at Yum! Brands—spent about $32 million in marketing. Three years later, the figure was closer to $132 million. Felix during Brinker’s investor day dove deeper into what’s been the most outward effect of that higher backing: value perception. This chart below, which uses YouGov data, lays out value perception scores among the general population of adults 18–49. Since rerouting, Chili’s result increased by 50 percent, placing it atop the company’s competitive set, widely speaking. However, Felix said, what’s more interesting is the following, which unpacks how value perception turned among customers who saw the brand’s advertising in the past two weeks. Trends were similar. There, too, Chili’s witnessed a sizable increase over the past three years. And again, it topped the competitive field. “But you can see that the increase in value perception is much bigger and the gap between us and competition is much wider,” Felix explained. What that tells Felix, he continued, is Chili’s “Better Than Fast Food” campaign continues to resonate. When customers find the messaging, it makes them think differently about the value Chili’s offers. What gives Chili’s confidence there’s still room to go? “Well,” Felix said, “when you think about ad awareness and the way to think about ad awareness is that is basically asking consumers, ‘have you seen a brand’s advertising in the past two weeks?’” MORE: Chili’s Turnaround Clears Way for New Restaurant Growth How Chili’s Plans to Remain ‘America’s Hottest Restaurant Brand’ For Chili’s, that particular measure hiked roughly 40 percent over the last three years. You’d expect it to, Felix said, when you toss $100 million into the mix. Yet Chili’s, even with such a vivid bump, still trails the largest spenders in its category. “And so that tells me that there are still probably large pieces of the population that have not seen or been exposed to the ‘Better Than Fast Food’ campaign,” Felix said. “And if you look at the last chart, you know that once we do get people to see that, it does change the way that they think about Chili’s.” In plain terms, Chili’s marketing hook has been to reintroduce guests to a brand they might have lapsed on. How they feel about it. What it offers compared to competitors. And then, invest via operations in an experience and environment worth coming back to. That education process, Felix said, remains underway. There’s also the familiar question marketers face—how have holistic metrics translated to sales? Felix pulled up a slide on Chili’s “Five to Drive” categories. Years ago, in 2017, Chili’s slashed 50 menu items and started to refocus on core products. Its offerings had ballooned to 125 items (40 percent cut). That work continued when Hochman arrived, with about 60 percent of the menu getting renovated. Chili’s sliced more than 25 percent of overall items and moved, as Felix said, to what the brand was known for: burgers, crispers, fajitas, margaritas, and now, the Triple Dipper. Meanwhile, Chili’s devised a heavy labor approach where, when 2026 rolled around, the company was investing $160 million more than it did in fiscal 2022. articles.title: Honey Baked Ham Names Kylie Kelce Brand Ambassador and Launches ‘Traditions that Bring Us Home’ Campaign
articles.titleKo: Honey Baked Ham Names Kylie Kelce Brand Ambassador and Launches ‘Traditions that Bring Us Home’ Campaign
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . As brand ambassador, Kelce brings her real-life take on family, food, and hosting to HoneyBaked. The Honey Baked Ham Company today announced Kylie Kelce, podcast host of “Not Gonna Lie with Kylie Kelce” and mom of four, as its brand ambassador and launched “Traditions That Bring Us Home,” a new holiday campaign celebrating how family traditions evolve from one generation to the next. The national campaign runs across TV, streaming, digital, social, and radio now through the holiday season. For generations, HoneyBaked has been part of the moments families look forward to year after year. “Traditions That Bring Us Home” celebrates those moments: the traditions we look forward to, the ways each generation makes them its own, and the people who make them feel like home. For Kelce, that idea is personal. HoneyBaked has been on her family’s holiday table for years, from the signature Bone-In Ham that always makes the menu to the Cinnamon Apples her grandmother, Mimi, loved. After Mimi passed, the family kept serving them in her memory. Today, they’re a favorite with Kelce’s own daughters. “HoneyBaked has been part of my family’s holiday traditions for years, so creating this campaign with a brand I genuinely love was really special,” said Kelce. “The Bone-in Ham is always a centerpiece at our house, and there are certain things you have to have around it: the Double Cheddar Mac & Cheese, the Maple Sweet Potato Souffle, the Rolls, and, of course, the Cinnamon Apples. Those were my Mimi’s favorite, so after she passed, we kept serving them for her. Now all four of my girls love them, even though Wyatt was the only one who got to meet her. I love that something as simple as a favorite food can keep a piece of someone, and a family tradition, going.” As brand ambassador, Kelce brings her real-life take on family, food, and hosting to HoneyBaked. She shows how a new generation is holding onto the traditions it grew up with while creating new ones that fit how families gather today. “We’re incredibly excited to partner with Kylie as our brand ambassador this holiday season and begin this next chapter for HoneyBaked together. Kylie is a natural fit for HoneyBaked. Her connection to our brand is authentic, and she brings a fresh, relatable perspective on how families host and gather today,” said Maegan Markee, Chief Commercial Officer at The Honey Baked Ham Company. “She represents a generation that’s taking the traditions they grew up with and making them their own, which is exactly the spirit of ‘Traditions That Bring Us Home.’ This holiday also marks the start of a broader marketing transformation for HoneyBaked, one that honors our heritage and celebrates our loyalists while finding new ways to connect with the next generation of HoneyBaked customers.” “The best holiday meals aren’t about spending all day in the kitchen, they’re about getting everyone around the table,” said Chef Tim Ziga, Culinary Director at The Honey Baked Ham Company. “HoneyBaked has always made that part easier. Whether it’s a big holiday dinner or a busy night with the family, we want to give people great food and more time to actually enjoy the moment.” HoneyBaked’s holiday menu includes its signature Honey Baked Ham, smoked for up to 24 hours and individually hand-glazed with its sweet and crunchy glaze, along with premium turkey breasts, heat-and-serve sides and desserts. Guests can plan ahead by ordering now at HoneyBaked.com and scheduling in-store pickup closer to Thanksgiving or the holidays. The full menu is available at participating locations nationwide and through HoneyBaked.com. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Lou Malnati’s Pizzeria announced today that its highly anticipated St. Charles restaurant will officially open Tuesday, October 27 at 3050 E. Main St., further expanding the family-owned company’s presence in the Chicagoland area. The restaurant marks Lou Malnati’s 70th location and will employ approximately 100 team members. The 6,200-square-foot space features a full-service dining room and bar, private dining room, carryout, delivery and catering services. “The St. Charles restaurant represents an exciting milestone in our continued Chicagoland growth,” said Julie Younglove-Webb, CEO of Lou Malnati’s. “Since 1971, we’ve been focused on bringing people together over our handmade deep dish, and we look forward to putting down roots in St. Charles, building lasting relationships and becoming a trusted part of the community for years to come.” “We’re thrilled to welcome Lou Malnati’s to Fox Haven Square and see this highly anticipated addition open its doors,” said Pat Greco, president of G Ninety Family Partners. “Lou’s is an iconic Chicago brand, and we believe the restaurant will be a tremendous addition to both the development and the St. Charles community.” Guests can enjoy the full Lou Malnati’s menu, including its legendary Chicago-style deep dish pizza made with its signature flaky buttercrust, Wisconsin mozzarella cheese and vine-ripened tomato sauce, as well as thin crust pizza, gluten-free options, appetizers, salads, pastas and desserts. The St. Charles restaurant will also be the first Lou Malnati’s location to showcase elements of the company’s refreshed brand experience. Updated visual elements, menu design and interior finishes blend the rich history of the Malnati family with a modern, welcoming atmosphere. To create a restaurant that reflects its new hometown, Lou Malnati’s worked with the St. Charles History Museum to incorporate historic photographs and local storytelling throughout the space. The restaurant design also features family photographs, pizza-pan-inspired décor and subtle nods to the Malnati family’s legacy and Chicago roots. As Lou Malnati’s continues to expand throughout the Chicagoland area, the company remains committed to being more than a restaurant in the communities it serves. Through local partnerships, charitable involvement and genuine hospitality, Lou Malnati’s looks forward to supporting local organizations and becoming an active member of the St. Charles community for generations to come. The restaurant is located in the Fox Haven Square development near the northeast corner of Kirk Road and East Main Street. For more information, please visit loumalnatis.com. articles.title: The Kolache Factory Makes Birria Kolache Permanent Menu Item
articles.titleKo: The Kolache Factory Makes Birria Kolache Permanent Menu Item
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Birria Kolache is filled with slow-braised birria beef, onions, cilantro, lime and a flavorful consommé, all wrapped in Kolache Factory’s signature dough. The Kolache Factory, the Katy-based bakery-café franchise known for its fresh-baked kolaches, is giving customers what they asked for. After a record-breaking limited-time run, the brand’s Birria Kolache has officially earned a permanent spot on the menu at all Kolache Factory locations. The Birria Kolache was inspired by Erin Hargett of Greenville, South Carolina, who submitted the idea as part of Kolache Factory’s annual Create a Kolache Contest. The customer-created flavor was introduced systemwide as the brand’s April 2026 Flavor of the Month and quickly became Kolache Factory’s No. 1 Flavor of the Month by sales. During its 30-day limited-time run, the Birria Kolache delivered strong systemwide results, including: 43,523 Birria Kolaches sold across all 60 stores 1.8 times the average Flavor of the Month sales per store per day More than 10,000 Birria Kolaches sold per week on average The results made the Birria Kolache Kolache Factory’s No. 1 Flavor of the Month by sales and helped drive the decision to add it to the permanent menu. “The Birria Kolache is exactly what our Create a Kolache Contest is all about,” said Dawn Nielsen, COO of Kolache Factory. “A customer brought us a bold idea and our team brought it to life, and guests responded in a big way. When a limited-time flavor performs like this and customers keep asking for it, we listen.” Priced at $4.98*, the Birria Kolache is filled with slow-braised birria beef, onions, cilantro, lime and a flavorful consommé, all wrapped in Kolache Factory’s signature dough. Unlike traditional birria dishes that are often served with consommé on the side for dipping, Kolache Factory bakes the consommé inside the kolache, creating a portable, flavor-packed version of the popular dish. The permanent menu addition reflects Kolache Factory’s approach to menu innovation, blending global flavors with the brand’s Czech-inspired roots while staying close to what customers want. The brand’s annual Create a Kolache Contest, now in its 8 th year, invites fans to submit original flavor ideas, giving customers a direct role in shaping future menu items. Winning submissions usually get a place on the menu as a limited-time offering. This is the first time a submission has been added to the permanent menu. “Kolache Factory has always been built around approachable, craveable flavors that fit into everyday routines,” Nielsen said. “The Birria Kolache brings something bold and unexpected to the menu, while still staying true to what people love about our kolaches.” The Birria Kolache is now available at all Kolache Factory locations. To learn more or find a location, visit www.kolachefactory.com. *Prices may vary in certain states. The post The Kolache Factory Makes Birria Kolache Permanent Menu Item appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: SIGEP World Heads to Warsaw Ahead of 2027 Trade Show
articles.titleKo: SIGEP World Heads to Warsaw Ahead of 2027 Trade Show
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Data provided by the Italian Trade Agency highlight growing demand in Poland for several food categories of interest to Italian companies. The international journey of SIGEP Meets the World, the Italian Exhibition Group (IEG) roadshow organised in collaboration with the Italian Trade Agency (ITA), continues. Today, 19 October, the initiative stops in Poland at the Embassy of Italy in Warsaw, aiming to strengthen dialogue with the Polish market and create new opportunities for Italian foodservice companies to meet local industry professionals. POLAND: A MARKET OF OPPORTUNITY FOR MADE IN ITALY Data provided by the Italian Trade Agency highlight growing demand in Poland for several food categories of interest to Italian companies: coffee, bread and bakery products, pastry products, chocolate, gelato and other food preparations. In 2025, Polish imports of these products reached €8.22 billion, an increase of 26.1% on the previous year. Over the same period, imports from Italy in these same categories rose to €865.3 million, recording growth of 25.3%. Polish imports of machinery and equipment for food preparation and production also showed a positive trend, pointing to further opportunities for Italian companies specialising in technologies for the sector. WARSAW: THE ROAD TO SIGEP WORLD 2027 The event on 19 October, hosted at the Embassy of Italy in Warsaw and aimed at industry professionals, will provide an opportunity to present SIGEP World 2027, highlighting its main new features, business opportunities and services for international operators. The programme will also feature a roundtable discussion on the outlook and opportunities for foodservice in the Polish market. Moderated by Natalia Aurora Urbanek, editor-in-chief of the trade magazine Mistrz Branży, the discussion will bring together entrepreneurs and experts from the gelato, pastry and Ho.Re.Ca. sectors to explore consumer trends, market developments and the needs of local operators. The meeting will conclude with a networking session, accompanied by a live demonstration and gelato tasting led by Polish master gelato maker Tomasz Szypuła. The Polish stop is therefore offering an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of market dynamics, engage with local operators and showcase the expertise of Italian companies. The event is part of the journey towards SIGEP World 2027 – The World Expo for Foodservice Excellence, scheduled to take place at Rimini Expo Centre from 23 to 27 January 2027. The 48th edition of the exhibition will bring together the pizza, coffee, bread, pastry, chocolate and gelato supply chains, along with the technologies and services driving the sector’s evolution. “Italian gastronomy tells the story of our regions, artisanal know-how and a culture of hospitality that is part of our identity,” says Luca Franchetti Pardo, Italian Ambassador to Poland. “Gelato is one of the most familiar expressions of this heritage, which continues to evolve through creativity and a commitment to quality. We are delighted to welcome SIGEP Meets the World to the Embassy and to share this tradition with Polish professionals, whose talent and experience enrich today’s gathering. A shared passion such as this also deepens mutual understanding and strengthens the economic ties and bonds of friendship between Italy and Poland.” “The Polish market is showing growing interest in Italian foodservice products and solutions, with positive import trends confirming opportunities for our companies, including in professional technologies and equipment,” says Roberto Cafiero, Director of the Italian Trade Agency’s Warsaw Office. “The Warsaw event forms part of the broader collaboration between the Italian Trade Agency and Italian Exhibition Group, aimed at strengthening the international reach of Italian trade fairs and enhancing their role as global platforms for

Captain D’s, the leading fast-casual seafood franchise in the United States, is building momentum for international growth as interest from prospective franchise partners expands across Europe. Following a successful international development trip earlier this year, Senior Vice President of International Operations and Development Hair Parra will return to Europe in October to meet with prospective franchisees and explore opportunities in additional markets. The trip is tentatively planned for the second week of October and is expected to include Italy, Spain and the United Kingdom, with additional markets potentially added. Interest in Italy has been particularly active, with Captain D’s currently in conversations with prospective partners. The company is also exploring opportunities in Spain, including Madrid and Valencia, while Poland and France remain markets of interest. “Every time we travel internationally, we come home with more conversations and more new relationships,” said Parra. “It’s exciting to get meaningful interest from experienced operators who recognize the opportunity in bringing a proven American seafood brand to their markets.” The international momentum comes as Captain D’s enters a new phase of U.S. growth, highlighted by the September unveiling of its new restaurant design in San Antonio, Texas. The location is the first U.S. showcase for a refreshed experience, featuring a contemporary design and more inviting guest environment while maintaining the brand’s familiar identity. Captain D’s plans to introduce the new design in additional U.S. markets, including Florida, Ohio and Oklahoma, while continuing to pursue qualified international partners. “Our growth story is bigger than opening individual restaurants,” said Brad Reed, Chief Development Officer for Captain D’s. “We’re evolving the Captain D’s experience while staying true to what has made the brand successful for more than five decades. That combination is creating interest from operators who want to be part of the next chapter of Captain D’s, both here in the U.S. and internationally.” Captain D’s is seeking experienced restaurant operators, multi-unit franchisees and master franchise partners interested in developing multiple locations internationally. TGI Fridays, where the world goes to celebrate, brought together eight of the brand’s best bartenders from across the world to compete in the 29 th World Bartender Championship (WBC), a flagship event at its Global Business Conference in Orlando. During a week focused on global brand momentum, the friendly competition between TGI Fridays’ most skilled bartenders really brought the spirit of the brand to life. Bartenders representing Japan, Greece, the UK, USA, Peru, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, and the Philippines showcased their bottle-spinning skills, with the crown going to Roniel Lopez from TGI Fridays, Manila. The contestants were judged by an expert panel on a combination of technical precision, brand knowledge, speed, and showmanship, while displaying the freestyle flair, personality, and lively personality that is synonymous with TGI Fridays. “It was a privilege to enjoy the skills and technical craft shown by the finalists, and I couldn’t be prouder of the eight experts who competed. Congratulations to Roniel on an impressive performance, and we hope visitors to our Manila restaurant enjoy seeing him in action” said Ray Blanchette, CEO, TGI Fridays. “The Global Business Conference was the perfect setting to bring the WBC back and give attendees an opportunity to show their support for colleagues and enjoy such an integral part of Fridays history.” TGI Fridays Global Business Conference saw brand leaders, franchisees and team members from more than 40 countries come together to discuss the global momentum of Fridays “1-2-3 Strategic Vision,” a growth plan to surpass 1,000 units and $2 billion in annual revenue by 2030. Under the theme “Fridays United,” the conference celebrated the company’s ongoing domestic and international resurgence. Fridays leaders took part in educational sessions and an interactive peer-driven Q&A panel on how regions tailor local strategies while staying true to global brand standards. They also heard from the teams behind several notable 2026 milestones, including the company’s first U.S. development agreement in more than a decade and entry into new territories that includes Pakistan, the Balkans, and Sub-Saharan Africa. “Working in the hospitality industry opens a world of opportunities, and TGI Fridays believes it is the responsibility of every team member to demonstrate their commitment to improving how we show hospitality to our guests,” said Phil Broad, Global President, TGI Fridays International. “Fridays United is an ethos that reflects the culture and mindset we are embracing globally across the brand, centered on collaboration, continuous improvement, and a commitment to making TGI Fridays our guests’ favorite choice. That spirit was on full display at our Global Business Conference that saw our leaders come together to share ideas, learn, and celebrate the future of the brand.” To learn more about TGI Fridays franchise opportunities, please visit www. tgifridays.com/franchise/. Baccarat Hotel New York , the Forbes Five Star AAA and Five Diamond hotel, announces the appointment of two food and beverage team leaders at the award-winning property. Chef Isaac Olivo has been named the Executive Chef, and In this role, he will collaborate with Chef Gabriel Kreuther, the hotel’s Two Michelin-starred Culinary Director in overseeing all food and beverage operations. This includes the Grand Salon, The Bar and Le Jardin, private events, and in-room dining. Beata Parzych is the new Head Sommelier, where she will oversee the entire wine program at the flagship property which includes the Grand Salon, The Bar, in-room dining, private bar service, and catered events. Chef Olivo brings nearly 20 years of culinary experience to this new position, having worked at world-renowned kitchens around the country and under acclaimed chefs. His previous work experience includes Executive Chef roles at two esteemed Relais & Châteaux establishments; Cuvee Restaurant at The Chatham Inn in Chatham, MA, and the Mayflower Inn & Spa in Washington, CT. Chef Olivo also held culinary leadership positions at Amorette Restaurant in Lancaster, PA, and Restaurant Clement in The Peninsula, New York. He began his career as a Sous Chef at Bourbon Steak by Michael Mina in Miami, FL, and his work experience includes tenure at SHO by Sean Hergatt in NYC, The Villa by Barton G in Miami Beach, and Jean Georges in NYC. A New York City native of Dominican heritage, Chef Olivo earned a Culinary Arts Diploma from Le Cordon Bleu and brings passion, creativity, and refined technique to the kitchen. Inspired by his father and grandmother, he discovered his love for cooking at an early age. Known for his seasonal, sustainable approach, Chef Olivo blends French technique with contemporary American flavors while honoring craftsmanship, culture and mentorship. He has also represented Relais & Châteaux at international events such as World Oceans Day, advocating for sustainability and ocean conservation. “I am thrilled to be part of something shaped by a pedigree rooted in centuries of excellence, craftsmanship, and an appreciation for the art of living well, and my goal is to bring this spirit to the table,” says Chef Olivo. “Baccarat Hotel New York is a celebration of joie de vivre which honors tradition while also embracing the inventiveness of today’s modern culinary landscape and for me it is all about creating cuisine that feels both timeless and contemporary at this sparkling property,” he adds. With nearly 20 years of experience in fine dining and luxury hospitality, Beata’s brings her expertise in wine, exceptional service, and the art of creating memorable guest experiences to her new role. Prior to joining the hotel, she worked at a variety of premier Michelin-starred establishments in New York City, including Le Bernardin, and Le Cirque and Circo Restaurants. Beata also held beverage leadership and sommelier positions at BLT Restaurant Group, STK Saint Urban, Rhubard Hospitality Collection, STK, and Zuma, all in the city. “In my new role I am excited to bring together my passion for continually evolving within the world of wine and hospitality, with a thoughtful, guest-focused approach to leadership, “ says Beata. “My focus is on maintaining high standards while building a collaborative team culture, while ensuring that knowledge, consistency, and genuine hospitality come together in every guest interaction,” she adds. All three locations will be owned and operated by the McClave family: John McClave, a real estate professional; his wife, Nam; their son, Egan; and Nam’s brother, Huy. “We spent a lot of time researching different franchise models and comparing what each one offered,” McClave said. “Bun Mee stood out because Denise and her team brought a level of professionalism and warmth that made the opportunity feel both promising and personal. The renewed domestic expansion effort is part of TGI Fridays' 1-2-3 Strategic Vision, which calls for more than 1,000 restaurants and $2 billion in annual revenue by 2030. TGI Fridays’ first domestic development agreement in more than a decade might be just the beginning. The casual-dining chain signed a deal with Bliss Bites LLC —led by led by owner and managing director Vinod Chand—to open five restaurants across New York State over the next three years. The franchisee also acquired an existing TGI Fridays in Central Islip, bringing his planned portfolio to six locations. But COO Ashley Kirkley says the company has already approved additional franchise partners and is negotiating agreements across several states. The goal is to establish a pipeline of multiunit operators capable of bringing the brand back to markets where its presence has diminished. “We have multiple opportunities in six to seven states that look very similar to Vinod’s deal,” Kirkley says. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Five Guys Games started in 2013. Five Guys, Connor Schell’s Full Day Productions, a Words + Pictures company, and Lost Tribe Creative, today released a five-episode docuseries entitled On The Line: The World Burger Games on Prime Video. Produced by Full Day Productions, a premium sports and entertainment studio, in collaboration with Lost Tribe Creative, On The Line takes viewers from local qualifying rounds around the world to the ultimate Five Guys Games championship, capturing the personalities and pressure behind one of the brand’s most celebrated traditions. The series is showrun by Collin Orcutt ( Any Given Saturday, Omnivore ). The finale was hosted by Charissa Thompson, who interviewed competitors before and after each event. The Five Guys Games started in 2013, as a Murrell family idea to celebrate hardworking Five Guys crew members. This year, the games drew participants from stores around the world competing in three events – the potato race, cheese race and dressing/QC race, with each contest demanding a level up on the skills that go into every Five Guys order. “The games began as a thank you to the people who make Five Guys what it is,” Five Guys Founder Jerry Murrell said. “Now, I’m watching crews from across the world compete on a brand new stage. I honestly don’t have words for it.” “With On The Line: The World Burger Games , we saw an opportunity to tell a story that goes far beyond competition,” Full Day Productions President David Chamberlin said. “At its heart, this series is about the people who bring Five Guys to life every day; their pride, dedication, camaraderie and the incredible culture they’ve built across the globe. We’re proud to partner with Five Guys and Lost Tribe Creative on this intimate, character-driven look at a tradition that celebrates the people behind the brand in an authentic and entertaining way.” Spoiler Alert: We Have a Winner, Folks The 2026 Five Guys Games concluded May 13 at The Theater at MGM National Harbor in Maryland, where Jonathan Martinez, of Poughkeepsie, New York – known to fans as “The Terminator” – defeated past champions to claim the title and championship belt. On The Line: The World Burger Games captures the sweat and sacrifice of crew members as they chase a shot at the grand prize – a $100,000 check. Lost Tribe CEO Jason Saffran said being a part of the evolution of the Five Guys Games, from a small contest on a trade show floor to today’s global competition, has been inspiring. “We have always been inspired by the level of intensity and pride each competitor brings,” Saffran said. “The opportunity to share these crew members’ journeys from their homes around the world to the big stage has been as profound and electrifying as the games themselves.” The Five Guys Games are open to any Five Guys employee. Media Watch Parties Members of the media, who wish to attend one of three watch parties around the country to celebrate our local finalists, are welcome to come out. The parties are taking place at a Five Guys store in the following locations: October 16, 7pm-9pm, American Dream, East Rutherford, New Jersey October 19, 2pm-5pm, Albuquerque, New Mexico October 20, 6pm-9pm, Kingsport, Tennessee Space is limited. To RSVP, reach out to Christine Cube, ccube@fiveguys.com. The post Five Guys Brings its World Burger Games to Prime Video appeared first on QSR Magazine .

On a warm fall morning in October, Freddy’s leadership whipped out big red scissors and a long piece of ribbon to mark the opening of the brand’s first location in Beaufort, South Carolina. But in the background of this moment, with staff members and C-suite executives gathered together, there were three golden balloons shaped as numerals to showcase an important milestone—Freddy’s has reached 600 units systemwide. It marks a significant achievement for a brand that began in Wichita, Kansas, in 2002. But the new restaurant represents more than another addition to the chain’s national footprint. It offers a glimpse into how Freddy’s plans to accelerate expansion as development becomes more expensive and operators face continued pressure on profitability. The unit introduces a 2,300-square-foot endcap format without a drive-thru. Operated by longtime franchisee Charleston Custard, the location seats 65 guests and includes an outdoor patio. The format is part of a change in Freddy’s real estate strategy. Historically, opening a restaurant typically required purchasing land and constructing a freestanding building. The company is now giving franchisees more opportunities to lease existing spaces, reducing upfront costs and opening markets that previously would have been difficult to develop. “Six years ago, Freddy’s was a franchise opportunity for folks who could afford to buy an acre of land and build a building, and that’s a very meaningful investment,” CEO Chris Dull says. “Whereas, today, with a format like this restaurant, you don’t have to buy an acre of land, you don’t have to build a building. You have to finish out an interior, bringing that investment level meaningfully down.” The prototype is smaller, but still maintains Freddy’s historical branding. Freddy’s places a major emphasis on hospitality at the counter. The strategy is already changing Freddy’s development pipeline. Chief development officer Andrew Thengvall says approximately half of the company’s current pipeline consists of endcap, inline, or second-generation restaurant spaces. Just a year ago, those formats represented approximately 10–15 percent. The company has also identified savings through changes to restaurant construction and equipment procurement. Thengvall says recent projects have eliminated $200,000–$300,000 in building costs without materially changing the customer experience. “It’s quicker to open. It’s a lower investment, and frankly, it’s easier to operate,” Thengvall says. Freddy’s has been testing smaller formats for several years. Of the approximately 40 corporate restaurants it operates, the six most recently developed locations have used non-ground-up formats. The company also has more than 50 franchised restaurants in non-freestanding buildings. The smaller restaurants also create opportunities in denser trade areas. Freddy’s historically developed many locations on the outskirts of growing communities, where land was more affordable. Leasing existing retail space allows the brand to pursue established urban and suburban locations without purchasing expensive parcels. “The landscape of opportunities for us is 10x what it was just a few years ago,” Dull says. Big Development Pipeline Freddy’s is the 14th-largest burger chain in America, earning $1.04 billion in U.S. systemwide sales last year. It opened a net of 124 restaurants across 2023, 2024, and 2025. The chain expects to open approximately 60 restaurants in 2026, continuing a steady pace of annual expansion. The company has more than 450 restaurant commitments in its development backlog and approximately 80 franchise operating groups. Its pipeline spans the country, with activity in Washington, California, Florida, South Carolina, and the Philadelphia area, among other markets. articles.title: Perkins Griddle & Go to Open First U.S. Location in New Jersey
articles.titleKo: Perkins Griddle & Go to Open First U.S. Location in New Jersey
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . A new chapter in Perkins history begins Oct. 19, when Perkins Griddle & Go opens its first U.S. location in Flemington, New Jersey. The milestone marks the highly anticipated U.S. debut of Perkins next-generation fast-casual concept and the brand’s return to the Garden State, led by local franchisees Giuseppe and Nicole Lahara. Blending more than 65 years of Perkins heritage with a modern approach to convenience, Perkins Griddle & Go brings the familiar flavors guests know and love into a fast casual experience designed for today’s busy lifestyles. From breakfast on the way to work to a satisfying lunch, dinner or an afternoon bakery treat, the new concept makes it easier than ever for guests to enjoy Perkins throughout the day. “Bringing Perkins Griddle & Go to New Jersey is an incredibly exciting milestone for our company,” said Matt Carpenter, President of Perkins Restaurant and Bakery. “We’re taking everything people have loved about Perkins for generations and bringing it to life in a completely new way. Flemington is where this next chapter begins, and we’re excited to welcome guests back to Perkins while introducing a new generation to the brand.” For the Laharas, the opening represents more than a new business venture. Longtime Perkins fans and New Jersey residents, the couple is bringing a brand they have loved for years back to their home state while building a family business they hope will become a lasting legacy for their four children. The Flemington café is the first of 16 Perkins Griddle & Go locations the Laharas have committed to developing across New Jersey, following the expansion of their original 10-unit franchise agreement to include additional locations in Monmouth and Ocean counties. “Nicole and I have always loved Perkins, so the opportunity to bring the brand back to New Jersey and be part of its next chapter means a great deal to our family,” said Giuseppe Lahara, franchisee of Perkins Griddle & Go. “We’re building something our children can one day grow into and carry forward as part of our legacy.” A Fresh Take on a Perkins Favorite Designed to meet the needs of today’s consumers without losing the comfort and hospitality that have defined Perkins for decades, Griddle & Go offers a streamlined, fast-casual experience with the flexibility to fit any occasion. After placing their order at the counter or self-service kiosks, guests can grab a quick bite or settle into the café-style dining room for a more leisurely visit. The concept brings together the best of Perkins signature menu with new offerings created specifically for the fast-casual format, including a Pork Roll sandwich and breakfast burrito. Guests can look forward to classic breakfast favorites, alongside specialty Griddle Greats, made-to-order breakfast sandwiches, lighter fare, burgers and sandwiches. The menu also features the bakery treats that have made Perkins a household name, including its iconic Mammoth Muffins, cinnamon rolls, cookies, brownies and signature pies. With breakfast, lunch and dinner options available throughout the day, Griddle & Go delivers the variety and value of Perkins in a convenient new format. Its modern design, compact footprint and flexible service model make it an exciting addition to the brand’s portfolio, creating new opportunities to bring Perkins to more communities.
