Matthew Keiser and Brad Paxton didn’t come to Taco John’s through the traditional restaurant career path. They came from medical sales, looking for a business that could diversify their income. Nearly a decade later, that side venture has become their full-time business, spanning 22 Taco John’s restaurants across eight states and giving the longtime business partners a platform for further expansion. Keiser grew up in western Nebraska, part of Taco John’s core Upper Midwest territory. Paxton came from Paducah, Kentucky, another longtime market for the brand. Their familiarity with the chain eventually turned into a business idea. “We kind of started talking about it, saying like, ‘Man, we loved it. We miss it.’ And we were like, let’s see if we can add more Taco John’s to the world and bring them out further than where they’ve been,” Keiser says. They began operating two restaurants in central Kentucky and quickly discovered restaurant ownership demanded more attention than a secondary venture could receive. The partners eventually sold their medical sales business and committed full time to restaurants. Their expansion since then has come primarily through acquisitions. Of the 22 Taco John’s restaurants in their portfolio, Keiser and Paxton built two and acquired the rest. Taco John’s long history has created a pipeline of longtime franchisees reaching retirement or seeking an exit, giving the pair opportunities to acquire established restaurants with proven sales and experienced teams. The partners look for acquisitions where they can preserve what an existing operator built and identify areas for improvement. AUV and the strength of the restaurant’s general manager are two major considerations. New development is evaluated partly on whether another restaurant can fill geographic gaps and make existing operations easier to support. Managing such a scattered footprint required Keiser and Paxton to change how they operated. Early in their restaurant careers, they handled everything from cleaning stores to local marketing. As the portfolio grew, they promoted experienced Taco John’s employees into multi-unit roles and gave general managers additional responsibility. Technology also helps connect restaurants separated by hundreds of miles. Stores communicate through back-office platforms, participate in speed-of-service competitions, share ideas, and recognize wins across the organization. “Even though you’re hundreds of miles away, it doesn’t really feel that way with our organization because they’re so tight knit,” Paxton says. Their learning curve stretched far past geography. Moving from medical sales into restaurants introduced them to a business where small changes in food and labor costs could carry significant consequences. Paxton says their existing back-office operation helped with the transition, but experienced employees taught them how to monitor controllables, labor, and food costs. Their first opening supplied another lesson. Sales initially struggled, forcing the partners to find unconventional ways to create awareness. Keiser recalls cleaning the restaurant relentlessly and canvassing the community. Paxton was asked to leave a Walmart after handing out coupons. articles.title: The Hidden Cost of Losing Your Cool as a Restaurant Leader
articles.titleKo: The Hidden Cost of Losing Your Cool as a Restaurant Leader
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Poised leaders recognize when they have become fragmented. They acknowledge the effect of their behavior. During my years as a multi-unit Cold Stone Creamery franchisee, I learned that some of the most important leadership lessons do not arrive in classrooms, conference rooms, or carefully planned training sessions. Sometimes, they explode in a parking lot. My wife and I were operating multiple Cold Stone Creamery locations, and the demands of restaurant ownership followed us everywhere. Operations, payroll, employee training, customer complaints, inventory, staffing, and the countless unexpected problems of running restaurants all competed for our attention. After an especially busy Friday night, I arrived at the store Saturday morning already tired and overwhelmed. The crew was moving quickly to prepare for the day—making ice cream, filling the mix-ins, baking waffle cones, and getting ready for customers. My wife arrived in our SUV with supplies for the store. Several employees and I went out to help unload. When the rear hatch opened, a gallon of milk fell from the vehicle. It hit the pavement, burst open, and splashed milk across the asphalt, our shoes, and everyone’s legs. I lost my composure. Instead of accepting the accident and helping address it, I kicked what remained of the first gallon across the asphalt. I then reached into the SUV, grabbed the second gallon of milk, and threw it across the parking lot. Then everything became quiet. No one said a word. My employees stared at me in disbelief. Their expressions communicated what they did not need to say: What just happened? Is this really our leader? In that silence, I saw myself through the eyes of the people I was supposed to be leading. The first gallon was an accident. I could not stop it from falling. But I could have prevented the second. That distinction has stayed with me because it captures one of the most important challenges in restaurant leadership. We cannot prevent every disruption. We cannot control every callout, late delivery, equipment failure, guest complaint, employee mistake, or gallon of milk that falls from a vehicle. However, we are responsible for what we add to the moment. The first gallon created a mess in the parking lot. My reaction created a second mess in the culture. The Human Moments Behind Restaurant Performance Restaurant managers deal with staffing shortages, narrow margins, variable demand, guest expectations, technology disruptions, and time constraints. They make decisions rapidly, repeatedly, and visibly. Most restaurant organizations prepare managers to execute procedures. They teach food safety, labor management, inventory control, guest recovery, cash handling, and operating standards. Those systems are essential. But procedures cannot anticipate every human moment. A procedure cannot determine the tone a manager uses when an employee makes a mistake. It cannot prevent frustration from becoming intimidation. It cannot decide whether a manager responds to a callout with curiosity or condemnation. It cannot repair trust after a leader’s reaction damages it. Those moments require something beyond operational competence. They require leadership alignment. I knew how I wanted to lead. I understood the importance of treating employees with respect, maintaining composure, and setting the emotional tone for the operation. My problem was not a lack of knowledge. It was a lack of alignment. What I believed, how I wanted to relate to my employees, and how I actually behaved had pulled apart. The leader I intended to be and the leader my employees experienced were not the same person. That is fragmentation, which is the gap between intention and behavior. Pressure did not create that fragmentation. It exposed it. Leaders Transmit More Than Instructions A manager’s emotional state rarely remains contained within the

articles.title: Longtime Captain D’s Guest Wins Cruise Trip to Alaska
articles.titleKo: Longtime Captain D’s Guest Wins Cruise Trip to Alaska
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Sandra Elmore has been going to Captain D’s since the Scottsboro store opened in the late 1970s. Captain D’s , the nation’s leading fast-casual seafood restaurant, has surprised a Scottsboro, Alabama, woman with the trip of a lifetime – a family cruise to Alaska! Sandra Elmore has been going to Captain D’s since the Scottsboro store opened in the late 1970s. This summer while she was there for her favorite fish dinner, she noticed a promotional sign for the “Captain D’s and PepsiCo Alaska Family Cruise Sweepstakes,” promoting the chain’s wild caught fish from Alaska. She scanned the QR code, submitted her receipt and forgot all about it. Weeks later when she received an email saying she was the winner, she was skeptical until she received the paperwork and a 32-pound box of cruise-themed merchandise from Captain D’s. They sent six sets of spa robes and slippers, binoculars, beach towels, loads of Captain D’s swag, and of course, Captain D’s gift cards. “We are just astonished and grateful,” Elmore said. “We have always loved Captain D’s, but this is just so over and above. Words fail me. I never expected it, but we’re very excited!” More than 5,000 Captain D’s fans entered the five-week promotion before a winner and five guests were selected to win a seven-night Alaska cruise, three ocean-view rooms, roundtrip airfare to Seattle, two nights of hotel accommodations in Seattle and a $3,000 travel stipend. Captain D’s launched its Wild Caught Batter Dipped Fish from Alaska nationwide in June as part of the brand’s continued focus on high quality seafood sourced from the United States. The fish comes from the cold waters of Alaska and is hand-battered fresh daily in Captain D’s restaurants. The Alaska cruise was a way to give guests the opportunity to experience the place where the brand’s fish is sourced. “The Alaska Family Cruise Sweepstakes was a natural extension of what makes Captain D’s special, which is bringing people together over great seafood and creating experiences that families can share,” said Phil Greifeld, CEO of Captain D’s. “Sandra’s story is exactly the kind of connection we hoped this promotion would create. She has been a Captain D’s guest for generations, and now she gets to experience Alaska with the people she loves most. We couldn’t be happier for her and her family.” The timing was especially meaningful for Elmore, just before she found out she won, Elmore was telling her husband how much she wanted to plan a family vacation with their two daughters and sons-in-law, but it was so difficult being in different states on different schedules. “Then the next week, I found out I’d won an Alaska cruise from Captain D’s,” Elmore exclaimed. “It was like my wish came true! It was truly amazing! Everyone is so excited!” That longtime connection made the news of her win even more special. For Elmore, Captain D’s has long been a wholesome family meal and a source of familiar favorites, including the restaurant’s classic fish and fries, fish tenders, green beans and baked potatoes. “It is hard to beat just the original fish and fries,” she said. “That’s kind of my comfort food of just a fun thing to grab.” For Elmore, the trip will be a first. She has never visited Alaska and has never taken a cruise. The family is now looking toward next summer for their Alaska adventure, with Elmore particularly excited about seeing the Inside Passage and glaciers. The Captain will be waiting when she returns, with fresh wild caught fish from Alaska. The post Longtime Captain D’s Guest Wins Cruise Trip to Alaska appeared first on QSR Magazine .

Starbird is bringing its Positively Delicious Chicken to the Midwest with plans to open its first Chicago-area restaurant in St. Charles, Illinois. The upcoming opening marks a major milestone in the fast-growing chicken brand’s expansion into the Midwest and the first of five planned locations in partnership with Keystone Management Group. Known for its bold, globally inspired flavors and culinary-forward approach to fast-casual dining, Starbird brings a fresh, flavorful approach with high-quality ingredients and made-from-scratch preparation. Tenders are antibiotic-free and hand-breaded daily, vegetables are freshly chopped, beverages are made in-house, and sauces are prepared from scratch, including Starbird’s signature Star Sauce. Guests can look forward to a diverse menu of crispy chicken sandwiches, tenders, wings, wraps, salads, nuggets and more. The brand’s innovative take on classic chicken favorites continues to drive its expansion into new markets nationwide. The first restaurant will open on Oct. 19 at 845 S. Randall Rd. in St. Charles, Illinois, with additional locations throughout the Chicago area expected to follow under the multi-unit agreement. Development will be led by Keystone Management Group, whose industry experience aligns with Starbird’s strategy of partnering with established operators in high-growth markets. “We’re incredibly excited to open the doors and introduce Starbird to the St. Charles community,” said Melanie Bowling with Keystone Management Group. “From the beginning, we wanted this opening to be about more than bringing a new restaurant to the area. St. Charles and the surrounding communities have such a strong sense of local pride, and we’re looking forward to celebrating alongside our guests while finding a fun way to give back to the schools and students who make this community special.” Starbird identified Chicago as a strategic next step in its national expansion due to the market’s scale, strong food culture and long term growth potential. With nearly 10 million consumers in the nation’s third-largest DMA, the market offers an opportunity to build brand awareness in one of the country’s most influential dining destinations as the brand expands its footprint. The expansion also allows Starbird to establish a local presence in the community and build lasting connections with guests through its commitment to quality and hospitality. “Expanding into Chicago is an important milestone for the brand and another example of our disciplined approach to growth,” said Greg Levin, CEO of Starbird. “We’re focused on entering markets where we see long-term opportunity and partnering with operators who can help us grow while preserving the guest experience and operational standards that define Starbird.” The Chicago announcement follows Starbird’s recent expansion into Washington state, where the brand opened its first location in Seattle. As the company continues to grow, Starbird said it remains focused on strategic market selection, local community engagement and sustainable long-term expansion. Taco Cabana, a celebrated fast casual Mexican-inspired dining chain, is closing out an exciting year of menu innovation with the launch of its new Chicken Poblano lineup, featuring four limited-time creations that put a fresh spin on familiar favorites. Available starting October 21, the launch also introduces Loaded Elotes, a new menu platform inspired by Mexican street corn, and Lime Margarita Cheesecake, a citrus-forward addition to the dessert menu. Announced by Ulyses Camacho, President and Chief Operating Officer of Taco Cabana, the new lineup centers on tender shredded chicken seasoned with poblano peppers and fresh cilantro, bringing bold flavor to four distinct creations: Chicken Poblano Quesabirrias with Consommé, Chicken Poblano Double Crunch Pizza, Chicken Poblano Loaded Elote and Chicken Poblano Folded Quesadilla. “2026 has been an incredible year for Taco Cabana, and we wanted to close it out with a launch that brings something fresh and exciting to our guests,” said Ulyses Camacho, President and Chief Operating Officer of Taco Cabana. “Chicken Poblano gave us the opportunity to take one standout flavor and create four distinct experiences around it. I’m especially excited about the quesabirrias, which put a new spin on a familiar favorite and reflect the kind of menu innovation we strive for at Taco Cabana.” Leading the lineup, Chicken Poblano Quesabirrias with Consommé reimagines a popular Mexican favorite with tender Chicken Poblano, melted quesadilla cheese and three corn tortillas served with a rich, green consommé infused with the aromatic flavors of poblano peppers and fresh cilantro. The vibrant, savory broth adds an herbaceous dimension to every dip, creating a distinctive twist on the quesabirria experience. Taco Cabana is also giving its Double Crunch Pizza a fresh makeover. The Chicken Poblano Double Crunch Pizza features two layers of golden, crunchy tortillas filled with creamy refried beans and topped with Chicken Poblano, sour cream, shredded cheese and diced tomatoes. The launch also marks the debut of Loaded Elotes, a new platform inspired by the bold, craveable flavors of Mexican street corn. The first creation, Chicken Poblano Loaded Elote, layers sweet corn with Chicken Poblano, creamy street corn sauce and sour cream for a savory, satisfying combination. The new platform creates opportunities for future street corn-inspired menu innovations. Rounding out the Chicken Poblano lineup, the Folded Quesadilla pairs Chicken Poblano and melted shredded cheese inside a warm flour tortilla for a flavorful, handheld option. Guests can also finish their meal with Lime Margarita Cheesecake, featuring creamy cheesecake, a citrusy lime glaze swirl and a graham cracker crust. Throughout 2026, Taco Cabana has continued to explore new flavor combinations and fresh interpretations of Mexican-inspired favorites. The latest launch builds on that momentum while establishing Loaded Elotes as a platform for future menu creations. “Our team continues to challenge itself to bring fresh ideas and bold flavors to life, and this launch is a great example of that creativity,” Camacho added. “From reimagining a fan favorite to introducing an entirely new menu platform, we’re continuing to find new ways to excite our guests and give them more reasons to come back. We’re finishing the year with great momentum, and we’re just getting started.” The Chicken Poblano lineup, Loaded Elotes and Lime Margarita Cheesecake launch October 21, 2026, at participating Taco Cabana locations for a limited time. articles.title: Teriyaki Madness Announces Partnership with Zipline’s Drone Delivery Service
articles.titleKo: Teriyaki Madness Announces Partnership with Zipline’s Drone Delivery Service
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Teriyaki bowls incoming! Beginning Thursday, Oct. 15, Teriyaki Madness (TMAD) is teaming up with Zipline , the world’s largest autonomous delivery service, to fly orders straight to customers across the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex and Houston later this year. No traffic. No detours. Just huge bowls of awesomeness, taking the express route from wok to sky to doorstep. Zipline’s all electric drones are entirely autonomous and have zero-emissions, meaning fanatics can get their teriyaki fix faster while putting a little less pressure on the planet. Most orders arrive in less than five minutes. This certainly isn’t Zipline’s first flight. Since 2014, the company has flown more than 140 million autonomous miles and now completes a delivery somewhere in the world every 20 seconds. Its network was built to transport blood, medicine, and critical medical supplies to more than 5,000 hospitals and health centers — work that continues across Africa today. Zipline brought its precision, home-delivery technology to the United States in 2025, and now serves dozens of communities through partnerships including retailers like Walmart and a growing roster of restaurant brands. “Getting bowls to people faster has always been the mission, and at some point you run out of shortcuts on the ground,” said Jodi Boyce, chief marketing officer of Teriyaki Madness. “Zipline has more flight experience than anyone out there, so we knew our bowls were in good hands — or, really, in good drones.” The launch caps a busy year for a brand that has spent 2026 doubling down on what fanatics want most: bigger value, bolder flavors, and fewer reasons to settle. And now, there’s one less reason to wait. Whether it arrives by air or by hand, every TMAD bowl is still cooked to order with fresh ingredients, crave-worthy proteins, signature sauces, and portions that prove everything really is bigger in Texas. “Zipline brings customers the food they’re craving the fastest way possible,” said Emily Snyder, vice president of restaurant sales at Zipline. “With Teriyaki Madness’s focus on fresh, premium ingredients, Zipline can make sure those quality meals are delivered exactly as the restaurant intended.” Zipline delivery will be available to TMAD customers starting at the Denton location and quickly expanding to additional shops across the Lone Star State. The delivery process is fast and simple: a customer places an order in the Zipline app. Once the order is ready, Zipline’s drones autonomously retrieve it, and quietly fly it to the delivery destination. Upon arrival, the drone stays up to 300 feet in the air while a smaller pod containing the order descends to the ground on a tether. The pod gently places the order on the ground with precision, and can even deliver in high winds and bad weather conditions. After delivery, the drone flies back to charge for its next order. For more information, visit teriyakimadness.com. The post Teriyaki Madness Announces Partnership with Zipline’s Drone Delivery Service appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Salad and Go’s CoFounder is Bringing the Bankrupt Chain Back to Life
articles.titleKo: Salad and Go’s CoFounder is Bringing the Bankrupt Chain Back to Life
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Salad and Go once had nearly 150 locations. Salad and Go may not be finished after all. Two months after filing for bankruptcy and shutting down its remaining 70 restaurants, the once-promising drive-thru salad chain is preparing for a comeback under the direction of one of its original creators. Daniel Patiño, the brand’s cofounder and longtime executive chef, has partnered with Arizona restaurateurs Mike Myers and Tom Misitano, cofounders of Hospitality First Concepts, to acquire Salad and Go’s intellectual property and begin rebuilding the business. The group has plans to reopen restaurants in Arizona and eventually pursue franchising. The transaction gives Patiño an opportunity to restore a concept that grew from a single Gilbert, Arizona, restaurant in 2013 to nearly 150 locations before an aggressive expansion strategy, mounting financial losses, and widespread closures brought the business to an abrupt end. “I just felt like, you know, it can’t end this way, like I have to find a way to keep this going,” Patiño told FOX 10 Phoenix . The new ownership group, operating through Beyond Salt and Pepper LLC, acquired Salad and Go’s name, trademarks, and recipes for $180,000, according to bankruptcy court documents reported by local TV stations Arizona’s Family and KTAR News . The group also secured a former Salad and Go restaurant in Gilbert for $1 and is pursuing another location in Mesa. READ MORE : Salad and Go Files for Bankruptcy, to Close All Restaurants Dutch Bros and 7 Brew to Battle for Salad and Go Locations 7 Brew Wins Auction for 73 Salad and Go Sites in $143 Million Deal Patiño told Arizona’s Family that he hopes to reopen the first restaurant within six weeks of approval. The partners plan to operate company-owned restaurants and eventually make franchises available nationwide, according to KTAR. Hospitality First Concepts already operates several Arizona restaurant and hospitality businesses, including The Hub Grill and Bar and Rusty Buckle Saloon. The comeback won’t necessarily recreate Salad and Go’s previous operating model. Patiño told Arizona’s Family that the new restaurants will prepare food on-site, marking a significant departure from the centralized production strategy that supported the chain’s earlier expansion. “Not happy with the chicken that we had before, transparently, right? But we’re going to be making everything in each location,” Patiño told the television station. The team is also considering the return of popular proteins, including steak and shrimp, and has confirmed that the brand’s lemonades will return. Patiño indicated that the initial focus will be on getting the menu and existing locations operating successfully before pursuing additional growth. The planned revival comes after one of the more dramatic collapses in recent quick-service history. Salad and Go built its reputation around compact, drive-thru-only restaurants serving affordable salads, wraps, breakfast burritos, and other nutritious meals. The concept attracted attention for its ability to offer freshly prepared food at prices competitive with traditional fast-food chains. But the company’s expansion into Texas and Oklahoma proved difficult. Salad and Go invested in a large commissary kitchen in Garland, Texas, capable of supplying as many as 500 restaurants within a 12-hour drive. Problems involving site selection, brand awareness, and its centralized production model contributed to financial pressure as the chain expanded. The company began closing restaurants in September 2025, announcing 41 closures across Texas and other markets. Another 32 followed in January 2026 as Salad and Go abandoned Texas and Oklahoma entirely. Those cuts left 70 restaurants in Arizona and Nevada, down from more than 140 in May 2025. The partnership marks another significant milestone in KFC's broader Kentucky Fried Comeback. KFC U.S. on Thursday announced a new partnership with The Coca-Cola Company, another step in the brand’s ongoing effort to refresh its menu and beverage platform and create more reasons for customers to visit. Beginning in January 2027, KFC will transition its U.S. beverage partnership to The Coca-Cola Company, with Coca-Cola products expected to be served in all U.S. restaurants by spring 2027. “I’m incredibly excited to bring KFC and Coca-Cola together. These are two originals, with deep consumer love” said Catherine Tan-Gillespie, President of KFC U.S. “This partnership is about more than what’s in the cup. It is another step in our work to evolve KFC, strengthen our restaurants, menu offerings and create a more relevant experience for today’s customers. Coca-Cola shares our ambition for the future of this brand, and I’m excited about what we can create together.” “This exciting new partnership brings Coca-Cola and KFC together across the U.S. for the first time,” said Dagmar Boggs, President of Foodservice & On-Premise, North America, The Coca-Cola Company. “By pairing KFC’s iconic food and flavors with the breadth of Coca-Cola’s beverage portfolio and innovation capabilities, we have an incredible opportunity to make every visit more refreshing, create memorable consumer experiences and unlock new growth possibilities together.” The partnership will bring together KFC’s signature food and Coca-Cola’s broad beverage portfolio to create compelling food-and-drink pairings, expand choice and explore new ways to make the KFC experience more complete. Together, the two brands see an opportunity to serve customers across more occasions, whether they are gathering over a family meal, stopping in for a snack or looking for something refreshing on its own. Coca-Cola’s extensive system capabilities will also support KFC restaurants across the U.S. The announcement comes as KFC continues to evolve its beverage platform through new drink offerings, expanded daypart occasions and innovation already underway across several global markets. Recent examples include the new drink lineup introduced at Open House, the brand’s new innovation restaurant in McKinney, Texas, featuring iced coffees, boba, shakes and other craveable creations designed to give fans more flavor and more reasons to visit. Together, the new Coca-Cola partnership and KFC’s continued expansion of beverages mark the next step in KFC’s plan to meet changing consumer preferences and create a more relevant customer experience. The partnership brings two iconic originals together as part of the broader Kentucky Fried Comeback, with a shared ambition to build memorable experiences around great food and beverages. articles.title: Inspire Brands Names Jenna Bromberg Chief Marketing Officer of Arby’s
articles.titleKo: Inspire Brands Names Jenna Bromberg Chief Marketing Officer of Arby’s
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Bromberg will lead all marketing efforts, focused on accelerating top-line profitability through innovation and value, expanding guest engagement, and bringing the Arby’s brand to life through distinctive culinary storytelling and highly personalized digital experiences. Inspire Brands announced the appointment of Jenna Bromberg as Arby’s Chief Marketing Officer, effective November 2. Bromberg is an accomplished marketing leader with deep experience across the restaurant, retail, and hospitality industries. Most recently, she served as Chief Marketing Officer at Papa Johns, where she led marketing, product, and commercial strategy for the North America business. Her previous leadership experience includes senior marketing roles at Yum! Brands, Carter’s, and Hilton, providing broad expertise across brand strategy, creative development, digital marketing, loyalty, consumer insights, and product innovation. “Jenna brings a powerful blend of creative brand-building and commercial leadership,” said David Graves, Arby’s Brand President. “She has a strong track record of driving growth, building meaningful consumer connections, and developing culturally relevant marketing that delivers results. We’re excited to welcome Jenna to Arby’s and look forward to the impact she’ll have as we continue building momentum for the brand.” Bromberg will lead all marketing efforts, focused on accelerating top-line profitability through innovation and value, expanding guest engagement, and bringing the Arby’s brand to life through distinctive culinary storytelling and highly personalized digital experiences. “I’m thrilled to join Arby’s, a truly iconic brand with a rich heritage, a distinctive voice, and an incredibly loyal fan base,” said Bromberg. “Arby’s has never been afraid to stand out, and that’s what makes this opportunity so exciting. I look forward to working with the talented teams at Inspire and across the brand to build on that momentum and unlock new opportunities for growth.” In addition to welcoming Bromberg, Inspire announced that Jeff Baker will transition into the role of Arby’s Vice President, Category Management and Culinary Innovation. Baker has played an instrumental role in shaping the Arby’s brand, leading the marketing organization through a period of strong growth and innovation. In his new role, he will focus on culinary, innovation, and menu strategy. The post Inspire Brands Names Jenna Bromberg Chief Marketing Officer of Arby’s appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Smalls Sliders Signs Multi-Unit Deal to Open Along Florida’s Atlantic Coast
articles.titleKo: Smalls Sliders Signs Multi-Unit Deal to Open Along Florida’s Atlantic Coast
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Smalls Sliders, the industry-disrupting cheeseburger slider brand, has signed a multi-unit development agreement to bring four Cans to Florida’s Atlantic Coast, further expanding the brand’s footprint across high-growth markets in the state. Seasoned entrepreneurs Joe Sloboda and Stanley Tsung of Stacked Hospitality will lead the development. Sloboda and Tsung bring decades of combined experience developing and operating multi-unit restaurant concepts across Florida and internationally. The duo has successfully grown franchise brands throughout Florida, Brazil, and Taiwan, building a strong track record of identifying high-potential concepts and introducing them to new markets. Smalls Sliders will become the fourth concept they have brought to South Florida. The group plans to develop four Cans across a territory spanning Florida’s Space Coast to as far south as Jensen Beach and throughout the Treasure Coast. Sloboda and Tsung expect to open their first Can in Port St. Lucie, marking Smalls Sliders’ debut in the region. “South Florida is a dynamic market with communities that embrace convenient, high-quality dining concepts, making it a strong fit for Smalls Sliders,” said Sloboda. “We see tremendous potential to build a meaningful presence here and introduce more guests to the brand’s unique experience. As we grow, our focus will be on becoming part of the communities we serve and creating Cans that people are eager to visit again and again.” Sloboda has called South Florida home since the early 1980s, while Tsung established roots in the region after immigrating from Brazil to Fort Lauderdale in 2014. Together, their ties to the area give them a strong connection to the communities where they plan to grow. The Stacked Hospitality partners will take an active role in developing and operating each Can, pairing their local market knowledge with Smalls Sliders’ craveable menu and streamlined operating model. Together, they aim to establish Smalls Sliders as a go-to burger destination along Florida’s Atlantic Coast. “Florida continues to play an important role in Smalls Sliders’ growth story, and expanding along the Atlantic Coast is a natural next step for the brand,” said Richard Leveille, Vice President of Franchise Development for Smalls Sliders. “Joe and Stanley bring extensive operating experience and a strong understanding of the communities they plan to serve. Their agreement allows us to introduce the Smalls experience to a new part of the state while building on the momentum we’ve already established across Florida.” The agreement builds on Smalls Sliders’ growing presence throughout Florida, where the brand has recently opened Cans in markets including Ocala and Pensacola. Sloboda and Tsung are actively scouting sites for their first locations along the Atlantic Coast. Smalls Sliders serves fresh, cooked-to-order cheeseburger sliders, seasoned waffle fries and hand-spun milkshakes from its signature Smorange™-colored shipping containers, known as “Cans.” The brand’s deliberately simple menu prioritizes quality and speed. Since opening its first location in 2019, Smalls Sliders has grown to more than 50 open Cans, with hundreds more in development across 30 states, attracting experienced multi-brand franchisees nationwide. As Smalls Sliders continues its expansion in the region, the brand is actively seeking real estate opportunities throughout the market. The team is evaluating sites for future Cans and encourages those interested in connecting with the brand to contact realestate@smallssliders.com and Nate Minnis at nate.minnis@smallssliders.com . For more information on Smalls Sliders, slide thru to www.smallssliders.com or visit https://smallsslidersfranchising.com to learn more about franchising opportunities. articles.title: Mexican Steakhouse Hacienda Tulum Opens in Long Beach, California
articles.titleKo: Mexican Steakhouse Hacienda Tulum Opens in Long Beach, California
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Hacienda Tulum, a new Mexican fine dining steakhouse from longtime friends and restaurateurs Nicolas Geeraerts and Tommy Mitsios, the owners of Tulum Tacos & Tequila, officially opens its doors on the Long Beach boardwalk. Located at 180 Boardwalk with ocean views and direct beach access, Hacienda Tulum is a year-round restaurant built around the concept of presenting the “flavors of Long Island through a Mexican lens.” The restaurant brings together the depth, tradition, and creativity of Mexican cuisine with premium steaks and seafood, seasonal Long Island ingredients, and the character of its waterfront setting. For Geeraerts and Mitsios, Hacienda Tulum represents the evolution of the Tulum Tacos & Tequila concept they began on Long Island. What started with a focus on modern Mexican cuisine has grown into a more ambitious dining experience designed to celebrate Mexican culinary traditions while embracing the place the restaurant calls home. “The Long Beach community is absolutely amazing,” Geeraerts said. “It’s a whole different level than anywhere else. I get goosebumps just thinking about it. For us to be a part of it, I’m super excited.” Leading Hacienda Tulum’s culinary program is Culinary Director Eduardo Salgado, chef of ’Emat in Mexico’s Valle de Guadalupe and a graduate of the Culinary Institute of America. Salgado has developed a menu that explores the breadth of Mexican cooking through premium steaks, whole fish, ceviches, aguachiles, oysters, composed dishes and complex moles. The kitchen pairs traditional Mexican ingredients and techniques with seasonal Long Island produce, locally sourced seafood and premium meats, including selections from Pat LaFrieda’s Prime 850 Club. The menu is intended to introduce guests to Mexican flavors and preparations that extend beyond more familiar interpretations of the cuisine. Signature offerings include Pat LaFrieda sliced rib-eye tacos with an Oaxaca cheese crust, pickled onions and salsa macha, along with chochoyotes, a masa-based preparation served with pistachio, pumpkin seed and cilantro pesto. The raw bar features East and West Coast oysters and other fresh seafood selections. Hacienda Tulum’s beverage program is similarly rooted in Mexican flavors and ingredients, with an extensive selection of tequila and mezcal alongside wine and specialty cocktails. Cocktails include the Piloncillo Passionfruit Mezcalita and Prickly Pear Champagne Margarita. The restaurant was designed to complement its Long Beach setting, with indoor and outdoor dining overlooking the ocean, furnishings imported from Mexico and an atmosphere that combines the warmth of a Mexican hacienda with the relaxed character of the waterfront. A private dining room and patio are also available for private events, corporate gatherings, and celebrations. Guests will also have access to an attached parking garage located beneath the restaurant, with private elevator access directly into Hacienda Tulum, as well as valet parking for added convenience. The Long Beach property offers additional ways to experience the Tulum brand. The boardwalk-facing Tulum Taco Stand provides a casual option for beachgoers, while the forthcoming Cemelle will introduce an intimate 24-seat agave bar within Hacienda Tulum. Geeraerts brings decades of hospitality experience to the project. After beginning his career at his family’s restaurant in Belgium, he went on to work with prominent chefs and hospitality groups including Patina Group, Jean-Georges, Todd English, Delmonico’s Restaurant Group and JF Restaurants. He later launched Tulum Tacos & Tequila on Long Island, growing the brand from Mineola to Baldwin and now Long Beach. For us to be a part of it, I’m super excited.” Leading Hacienda Tulum’s culinary program is Culinary Director Eduardo Salgado, chef of ’Emat in Mexico’s Valle de Guadalupe and a graduate of the Culinary Institute of America. Salgado has developed a menu that explores the breadth of Mexican cooking through premium steaks, whole fish, ceviches, aguachiles, oysters, composed dishes and complex moles. The kitchen pairs traditional Mexican ingredients and techniques with seasonal Long Island produce, locally sourced seafood and premium meats, including selections from Pat LaFrieda’s Prime 850 Club. The menu is intended to introduce guests to Mexican flavors and preparations that extend beyond more familiar interpretations of the cuisine. Signature offerings include Pat LaFrieda sliced rib-eye tacos with an Oaxaca cheese crust, pickled onions and salsa macha, along with chochoyotes, a masa-based preparation served with pistachio, pumpkin seed and cilantro pesto. The raw bar features East and West Coast oysters and other fresh seafood selections. Hacienda Tulum’s beverage program is similarly rooted in Mexican flavors and ingredients, with an extensive selection of tequila and mezcal alongside wine and specialty cocktails. Cocktails include the Piloncillo Passionfruit Mezcalita and Prickly Pear Champagne Margarita. The restaurant was designed to complement its Long Beach setting, with indoor and outdoor dining overlooking the ocean, furnishings imported from Mexico and an atmosphere that combines the warmth of a Mexican hacienda with the relaxed character of the waterfront. A private dining room and patio are also available for private events, corporate gatherings, and celebrations. Guests will also have access to an attached parking garage located beneath the restaurant, with private elevator access directly into Hacienda Tulum, as well as valet parking for added convenience. The Long Beach property offers additional ways to experience the Tulum brand. The boardwalk-facing Tulum Taco Stand provides a casual option for beachgoers, while the forthcoming Cemelle will introduce an intimate 24-seat agave bar within Hacienda Tulum. Geeraerts brings decades of hospitality experience to the project. After beginning his career at his family’s restaurant in Belgium, he went on to work with prominent chefs and hospitality groups including Patina Group, Jean-Georges, Todd English, Delmonico’s Restaurant Group and JF Restaurants. He later launched Tulum Tacos & Tequila on Long Island, growing the brand from Mineola to Baldwin and now Long Beach. He now joins the growing Smalls Sliders system as a multi-unit franchise owner. articles.title: Slutty Vegan Announces First Operating Franchisee
articles.titleKo: Slutty Vegan Announces First Operating Franchisee
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Slutty Vegan, the world-famous, woman-owned plant-based burger brand founded by entrepreneur, author and reality-television star Pinky Cole Hayes, has named Destiny Correa its first-ever operating franchisee, officially converting the brand’s Fulton Street location in Brooklyn, New York into its first operating franchised restaurant. Correa spent nearly five years as General Manager of the Fulton Street location, helping build it into one of Slutty Vegan’s flagship restaurants. In recognition of that determination and loyalty, Founder and CEO Pinky Cole Hayes gifted her the store outright, and Slutty Vegan waived both the initial franchise fee and the recurring marketing fee typically required of new franchise partners, in recognition of her years-long commitment to the brand. “I walked into this store five years ago as a manager, and now I’m walking back in as the owner,” said Correa. “Most people in this industry never get told that ownership is possible for them. Pinky told me it was, and then she helped make it a reality.” The Fulton Street location is now operating under Correa’s ownership, building on the momentum of additional franchise deals the brand has already announced in other markets as it continues to expand nationally, including Washington, D.C., Detroit, Ohio and its home market of Atlanta. “Destiny helped get Slutty Vegan Brooklyn up and running and has managed it beautifully ever-since,” said Pinky Cole Hayes, Founder and CEO of Slutty Vegan. “She showed up every single day for five years and ran that store like it was already hers. Handing her the reins to own the store was a no-brainer and the right thing to do. She’s proof that if you put in the hard work, Slutty Vegan will help you own something real.” Since launching in Atlanta in 2018, Slutty Vegan has grown from a viral burger concept into a nationally recognized brand known for bold flavors, high-energy customer experiences, and community impact. The brand’s founder, Pinky Cole Hayes, is a best-selling author and philanthropist who built the brand from a single food truck into a cultural phenomenon. Cole Hayes has continued her rise to stardom this year as a cast member of Bravo’s The Real Housewives of Atlanta, bringing her boldness and business savvy to one of television’s most-watched franchises and introducing Slutty Vegan to millions of new fans. The company’s move into franchising marks growing demand for the brand across the country and a strategic focus on sustainable expansion in high-opportunity markets with experienced operators. articles.title: 100 Days In, Dakota Manchester Airport Established as a Stylish Destination For Travellers Both Near and Far
articles.titleKo: 100 Days In, Dakota Manchester Airport Established as a Stylish Destination For Travellers Both Near and Far
articles.originalSummary: The UK’s first luxury airport hotel at Manchester Airport has proven to be a hit with air travellers and local residents alike in its first 100 days. Dakota Hotel Group’s stylish, luxury hotel welcomed over 15,000 guests in the opening 100 days, including new guests experiencing the brand for the first time. Guests range from business travellers staying ahead of early morning domestic flights, alongside leisure guests heading to destinations across the globe. Recent guests have travelled on to New York, Los Angeles, Barbados, Singapore and Bangkok, as well as domestic and European routes. The hotel offers a luxury experience with ultimate comfort, to ensure travellers get a great night’s sleep before embarking on their journeys around the globe. Dakota Manchester Airport has seen strong demand throughout the week, with Thursdays and Fridays proving to be particularly busy as guests set off on long weekend breaks or prepare for early flights. The hotel’s parking packages have been extremely popular from the outset. Guests appreciate the convenience of leaving their vehicle at the hotel and being transferred directly to their airport terminal in comfort by Dakota’s concierge team. It also provides guests with the added reassurance of knowing their vehicle is parked in a secure hotel environment while they are away. It’s not just air travellers that are visiting Manchester Airport’s new luxury hotel, local residents and businesses have been enjoying the hotel’s stylish food and beverage offerings alongside hotel residents. At the heart of the hotel sits The Grill where the menu reflects true Dakota style, centering on bold, flavour-led dishes made with high-quality produce and generous portions. There are premium steaks, indulgent sides, and a carefully curated wine list, delivering a memorable dining experience. Steak has long been at the heart of the Dakota table, and the 28-day dry-aged fillet remains the best-selling dish across every Dakota restaurant, Manchester Airport included. Truffle Parmesan Fries and Tenderstem Broccoli sautéed in Garlic, Chilli and Soy are the most popular accompaniments, and Dakota’s signature Sticky Toffee Pudding, served in a rich butterscotch sauce with Madagascan Vanilla Ice Cream continues to be the dessert of choice. Many guests choose to start their holiday with a glass of Taittinger Champagne, making it a popular choice for celebrations and special occasions. In The Bar, the Hugo Spritz, Classic Margarita and a range of brunch-favourite cocktails continue to be among the best-selling drinks, helping guests relax and begin their travels in style. Matt Townley, Group Operations Director, said: “With Dakota Manchester Airport, we’re bringing something different to the airport market, combining the luxury, style and service that our guests know and trust with the convenience of an airport location. It’s also an exciting milestone as our second hotel in Manchester, strengthening our presence in a city that continues to be incredibly important to us. “It’s been an incredibly busy and successful start, and we’ve loved seeing familiar faces from our other Dakota hotels alongside so many new guests experiencing the brand for the first time. “We’re welcoming travellers from around the world, corporate guests and local residents alike. As well as serving those passing through the airport, we’re focused on establishing The Grill and Bar as the neighbourhood destination of choice for the local community, whether for business meetings, celebrations or simply great food and drinks with friends and family.” The £54m development features 154 elegant bedrooms and stylish suites, each thoughtfully designed with the modern traveller in mind. Fueled by strong Live Más Café performance, the brand is kicking off the concept’s next chapter with new sips, new markets and more ways to explore what fans want to drink next. On October 15, Taco Bell will introduce four new horchata-inspired sips at Live Más Café locations, bringing its take on the beloved flavor to three distinct formats. From the creamy, frozen Purple Horchata Chiller to the coffee-forward Chocolate Horchata Cold Brew Float, and the fruity, refreshing Strawberry and Vanilla-Spiced Horchata Refrescas, the four-drink lineup offers something for every kind of beverage craving. At the same time, Live Más Café is growing alongside its menu. articles.title: The £95 Restaurant Ripple Effect: How Dining Out Drives Spending Beyond the Bill
articles.titleKo: The £95 Restaurant Ripple Effect: How Dining Out Drives Spending Beyond the Bill
articles.originalSummary: For more than 25 years, OpenTable has worked alongside restaurants to help them fill tables, connect with diners and grow their businesses. Its 2026 Restaurant Impact Report explores the vital role restaurants play in local economies, communities and everyday life, as well as how diners can help them thrive. The findings demonstrate that restaurants contribute far more than dining alone. They drive spending and footfall for surrounding businesses while creating spaces where people can come together and reconnect. The report explores the challenges restaurants face, including the impact of no-shows, and how small actions from diners can make a meaningful difference. Among the findings: Dining out has an economic ripple effect: 56% of UK diners spend at neighbouring businesses before or after their meal, spending an average of £95. Restaurants bring people together: 98% say local restaurants are important to their community, while 71% of Gen Z diners are likely to book a meal out to feel better or reconnect when they feel stressed or low. Supporting restaurants goes beyond the bill: Among Gen Z diners who made a restaurant reservation in the past year, 57% admit to having failed to show up at least once. A no-show for a table of two costs £55.70 on average, according to restaurant workers,² while 48% say understanding the financial impact of a no-show would make them more likely to honour or cancel a booking. “Restaurants are so much more than places to eat, they create jobs, bring people together and play an important role in the life of communities across the UK,” explains Sasha Shaker, Senior Director of Restaurant Sales and Service, OpenTable UK and Ireland . “This report showcases the industry’s wider impact and highlights why restaurants matter and why OpenTable is dedicated to advocating for their success.” Restaurants Fuel Employment and Local Economies More than half (56%) of UK restaurant diners said they spent money on other activities the last time they ate out locally.¹ Those who spent elsewhere alongside their meal spent £95.20 on average, rising to £126 among Gen Z and £118 among Millennials.¹ Restaurants see this impact first-hand, with 51% of hospitality workers saying their restaurant drives footfall or spending at nearby businesses. According to UKHospitality, hospitality is the UK’s third-largest employer, with restaurants employing 1.3 million people and contributing £44 billion to the economy annually. Restaurants Drive Community and Personal Wellbeing Restaurants provide spaces where people meet, celebrate and connect. More than half (56%) of UK diners are likely to book a meal out to feel better when stressed or low, rising to 71% among Gen Z diners.¹ If their favourite local restaurant disappeared tomorrow, 53% would miss the atmosphere and character it brings. Dr Martha Newson, Associate Professor of Psychology at the University of Greenwich , explains: “Sharing a meal at a restaurant is one of the oldest ways of bringing people together, because sitting around a table lets us focus on each other. Our research with over 10,000 people worldwide found face-to-face contact remains a strong predictor of wellbeing, as social bonds deepen through eye contact and shared experiences.” The Balancing Act for Restaurants While restaurants support their local areas, they are also navigating significant pressures. OpenTable’s research found that if VAT were reduced from 20% and restaurants passed the savings on through lower menu prices, 39% of diners would eat out more often, while a further 22% would spend more when they did. The report also explores how restaurants could use potential VAT savings. According to the research, 42% would primarily use a reduction to protect or increase staff wages and hours, 31% would lower menu prices for customers and 30% would reduce how often they need to raise prices. articles.originalSummary: Michelin-recommended contemporary Cantonese restaurant Cuisine Cuisine at The Mira , Tsim Sha Tsui, welcomes Lau Sze-yau as its new Executive Chef. An award-winning master of Cantonese cuisine whose distinguished career has seen him helm some of the city’s most respected Chinese dining establishments, Chef Lau brings a fresh perspective, two decades of experience and vibrant energy to the kitchen. Blending both innovation and tradition, his core culinary philosophy is grounded in three essential chapters – craft, heritage and memory – that unite to expand the possibilities and showcase the evolution of Cantonese cuisine. These fundamentals underpin a newly unveiled à la carte menu which retains signature classics for convivial celebrations, reimagines family favourites with nostalgic warmth, and introduces inventive creations that heighten the excitement of fine Chinese dining. Uniting Chef Lau’s culinary ingenuity with modern aesthetics in the restaurant’s elegant setting, the menu presents an exquisite feast designed to engage all the senses. With over two decades of culinary experience, Executive Chef Lau Sze-yau’s gastronomic journey was first sparked in childhood during family reunion dinners. Watching elders transform simple, fresh ingredients into a banquet of rich flavours – and seeing the joy it brought to loved ones – deeply moved him. This early realisation that delicious food brings happiness and nostalgia nourishes the soul ignited his lifelong passion for cooking. Chef Lau’s career in Cantonese gastronomy spans leading hospitality brands including The Hong Kong Bankers Club, Hong Kong Parkview and the Clearwater Bay Golf & Country Club. He honed his expertise at the Chinese Culinary Institute under the Vocational Training Council, completing advanced master classes and the Master Chef Course in Chinese Cuisine, where he was honoured as Outstanding Trainee of the 10th programme. His talent has earned widespread industry recognition, with consecutive gold and silver awards at the Vocational Training Council’s Asian Culinary Exchange from 2017 to 2019. Dedicated to promoting Cantonese culinary culture, he serves on the committees of the Asia Art of Cuisine Society and the Hong Kong Chinese Chefs Association, and was a judge at the 2019 Hong Kong International Culinary Classic. I am thrilled to join Cuisine Cuisine at The Mira and to share my contemporary vision of Cantonese cuisine, conceived through craft, heritage and memory, with multi-generational families of Hong Kong gourmands and guests from around the world,” says Executive Chef Lau Sze‑yau. “Grounded in authentic Cantonese flavours, my creations are elevated with modern touches in refined and often surprising presentations, ingredient pairings and culinary techniques. In harmony with the restaurant’s elegant concept, my goal is to curate memorable dining journeys that captivate through taste, aroma and visual beauty. Under the leadership of Chef Lau, Cuisine Cuisine at The Mira unveils nine new signature creations spanning appetisers, main courses and desserts – each testament to his versatility and creativity. This flavour journey unfolds across three chapters: infusing dynamic new life into traditional Cantonese frameworks, honouring time‑tested craftsmanship, and evoking cherished memories at the table. Guests are invited to immerse themselves in the chef’s storybook of tastes, savouring the heritage of Chinese culture while reconnecting with “the joy of memory” – nostalgic moments when flavour, love and happiness intertwined around the family table. articles.title: Delmonico’s Hospitality Group Opens Boogie Bakery & Bistro in New York City’s Washington Heights Neighborhood
articles.titleKo: Delmonico’s Hospitality Group Opens Boogie Bakery & Bistro in New York City’s Washington Heights Neighborhood
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Delmonico’s Hospitality Group (DHG), parent company of the historic Delmonico’s restaurant, today opened Boogie Bakery & Bistro, a new all-day bakery and bistro at 4015 Broadway in Washington Heights. The restaurant serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner six days a week, with sourdough baked fresh on site at the heart of the menu. Boogie Bakery & Bistro marks the U.S. restaurant debut of Boogie Lab, a well-known European sourdough brand. The space is built for the people who live and work nearby: a place to pick up a warm loaf in the morning, grab a sandwich at lunch, or sit down for dinner and a drink. Under the culinary direction of DHG’s Executive Chef Adam Plitt, the menu puts sourdough first, with fresh breads and focaccia, sandwiches, sourdough pasta, and other bakery and bistro dishes. Bread is baked by hand all day in the open kitchen, where guests can watch the team shape and bake each loaf from the counter. “We built Boogie to be a neighborhood restaurant first,” said Dennis Turcinovic, owner and executive culinary partner, Delmonico’s Hospitality Group. “You walk in, you smell the bread, and you know it was made here today. Real sourdough has always come down to flour, water, salt, and time. Time has always been the hard part. It’s what makes good sourdough slow to make and costly to buy. Our process removes that barrier without cutting corners, so we can bake fresh all day and keep prices fair. But hospitality is not just about the food, it’s about people. Our job is to give this neighborhood a place they want to come back to, with good bread and a team that gets to know them.” Every loaf starts with three things: flour, water, and salt. Boogie’s own patented fermentation method, developed in Europe, allows the team to make true sourdough in about three to four hours, with no commercial yeast or additives. The result is consistent: bread that tastes the same on a busy Saturday as it does on a quiet Tuesday, baked in small batches and always fresh off the rack. The opening is part of Boogie’s wider growth in the U.S. The company has entered the wholesale market and plans to open a New Jersey production plant this fall to supply bread at scale. The Washington Heights restaurant will continue to bake its bread by hand, on site, every day. Boogie Bakery & Bistro is located at 4015 Broadway, New York, NY 10032. The bakery is open daily from 6:45 a.m. to 7 p.m., while the bistro is open Monday through Saturday from 5 p.m. to 10 p.m. For more information, visit www.boogielabnyc.com. Clutch City Cluckers, the Houston-born concept known for its 100% halal Nashville-style hot chicken, is expanding with its 13th location in the Webster area at 1806 W Bay Area Blvd. The new location will celebrate its grand opening beginning Saturday, October 24 at 11 a.m. with a ribbon cutting, DJ, giveaways, and 50% off the entire menu throughout the two-day grand opening weekend. articles.title: How Founding Farmers’ Caitlin Mateo Turned a Fascination with People Into a Culinary Career
articles.titleKo: How Founding Farmers’ Caitlin Mateo Turned a Fascination with People Into a Culinary Career
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Mateo oversees all the brand's kitchens, which work through more than 200 items on the daily prep list. Caitlin Mateo is an anthropologist turned chef, though for her, the two are inextricably linked. In her teenage years, she was fascinated with world culture and people; she wanted to know what they believed in, how they ate, and how their geographical location influenced their culture. “When you study food, you look at what grows regionally, how it gets cooked, how it gets utilized. But this also tells you about the history of people, how they act, what their background is, and what motivates them,” Mateo says. “I think [anthropology and culinary] studies come together beautifully, if you are willing to learn and dine with people.” It’s an idea borne out in something as ordinary as a pecan. The only major nut tree native to North America, pecans became a high-density energy source for many Native American tribes in the winter, often traded or pounded into milk and stews. Today, they form the foundation of regional comfort foods, such as holiday pecan pie, praline candies, and butter pecan flavoring—a small but telling example of how a single regional crop can carry generations of resilience, season, and culture forward. It’s the kind of connection she’d go on to build a career around. Mateo was a natural cook. She catered for friends, parties and weddings, hand-producing hundreds of cookies and other naturally sourced goods. In college, she was introduced to a woman who owned a fine-dining French restaurant, and this first mentor taught her everything. Favorite spice at the moment: Aleppo pepper Secret comfort food: Mole What’s the last cookbook you bought? “Pulp” by Abra Berens If you weren’t a chef, what profession would you be in? Cultural studies / Anthropology The one food trend you wish would come back: Dessert/cheese carts “I took a part-time job working in the kitchen, and she showed me everything from running a dish room, to fabricating beef tenderloins and trimming lamb racks, and making the most delicious food,” Mateo says. “It inspired me to turn my studies and my career around.” Mateo enrolled in the restaurant school at Walnut Hill in Philadelphia, blending her curiosity and love for people and food into a career path she could grow into. After running her own culinary consulting firm for a few years, she found her footing at Founding Farmers, joining as an executive chef and working her way up to director of kitchen operations and development. Founding Farmers is majority-owned by more than 70,000 members of the North Dakota Farmers Union, as well as farmers across the Midwest. The first restaurant opened in 2008, just a few blocks from the White House, and has since expanded to three locations in Washington, D.C.; one in Maryland; one in Pennsylvania; and three in Virginia. Mateo oversees all the brand’s kitchens, which work through more than 200 items on the daily prep list. From bread to booze, everything is prepared from scratch across a multi-unit footprint. Each menu item can be tied back to an American farmer whom the restaurant buys from directly, running its own trucks to suppliers in North Dakota. Founding Farmers has a host of working relationships with independent and locally owned distributors, who help fill in the gaps with nearby family farms and fishermen. Because of this, menus are crafted to be location-specific and vary from season to season. “Our goal is to unbundle the supply chain. articles.title: QSR’s Next Battleground Isn’t Speed—It’s Feeling
articles.titleKo: QSR’s Next Battleground Isn’t Speed—It’s Feeling
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . According to Qualtrics' 2025 Consumer Trends Report, 66 percent of fast-food consumers reduce or stop spending after a single poor experience. QSR was built on efficiency, and it delivered on that promise for decades. Now, consumers want more than fast. They want fast and a good experience. Drive-thrus shaved to the second, digital ordering eliminating the queue, AI now rewriting the entire service model in real time. Speed has become table stakes. We said as much in our own research: efficiency alone no longer wins loyalty, consumers have come to expect it, which means it’s stopped being the thing that sets one brand apart from another. When every QSR is fast and highly digital, these things become the cost of doing business, not the source of competitive difference. And in chasing efficiency above all else, we’ve done something we didn’t intend. We’ve stripped time of any meaning. Fast is Table stakes. Felt is the Differentiator. Think back to a meal you can genuinely remember, one that made an impact on you. Did you note how quickly the food came out? Or was it the warmth of the person who served you? The smell when you walked in? The sound of a busy kitchen? That small, unexpected moment of human connection that you weren’t even expecting? Memory doesn’t form around speed. It forms around feeling. QSR’s are spending an enormous amount of energy to make things faster. But why aren’t they putting the same energy into making time well spent? The commercial stakes of getting this wrong are real. According to Qualtrics’ 2025 Consumer Trends Report, 66 percent of fast-food consumers reduce or stop spending after a single poor experience—more than any other sector. That’s a revenue problem. And it won’t be solved by shaving another ten seconds off the drive thru. How Do You Design “Time Well Spent?” The guest journey has four natural moments where brands can shift from transactional to memorable: Order, Wait, Pick-Up, and Return. Most brands invest heavily in the first, but the best ones invest intentionally across all four. ORDER : Make it Co-Creation, Not a Transaction Ordering is, by design, an act of cognitive efficiency. But there’s a more generous version, one that reduces overwhelm without stripping out warmth. Cava does this well. Their live, step-by-step build transforms ordering into something collaborative. Staff guide, suggest, build in front of you. The menu stops being a wall of decisions and becomes a conversation. You leave feeling like that meal was made for you. Because in a sense, it was. WAIT : Turn Awkward into Anticipated Where wait time can be cut, cut it. Where it can’t, transform it. Sweetgreen has understood this for years. Open kitchens and visible assembly do more than signal transparency, they signal craft. Watching your food being built stimulates appetite and makes the wait feel like part of the experience, not time stolen. Add sensory cues, smell, motion, sound, and impatience shifts into anticipation. People don’t mind waiting when they feel something worth waiting for is happening. PICK-UP : Not Confirmation of Completion, Confirmation of Care The pick-up moment is probably the most underrated touchpoint in the entire journey. It’s when the promise lands, and almost every brand treats it as an administrative handover. Number called. Bag passed. Done. Starbucks figured out something the rest of the industry hasn’t fully caught up with yet. Writing a name on a cup, adding a few words of encouragement like “you got this”‘” or “‘”have a great day,” shifts the entire feeling from transaction complete to this was made for you. A tiny thing with a disproportionate impact. RETURN : Give Them a Reason to Come Back Getting someone through the door once is a marketing challenge but getting them back is an experience challenge. Crumbl Cookies is the most interesting case study here. Their

articles.title: Pryze Launches Fully Redesigned Platform
articles.titleKo: Pryze Launches Fully Redesigned Platform
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Pryze helps companies like Burger King, Amazon, Paris Baguette, and Sky Zone. Pryze, the mobile app that rewards hourly employees for staying focused and completing goals during their shifts, announced the launch of a fully redesigned version of its platform. The update addresses growing demand for real-time insights into revenue, retention, productivity, and focus, giving operators a shift-by-shift view of how teams are performing. Pryze helps companies like Burger King, Amazon, Paris Baguette, and Sky Zone across quick service restaurants, hospitality, and the public sector turn their employees into a competitive advantage through rewards, recognition, and competition. “We are thrilled to give our customers an upgraded app that gamifies business goals and turns raw data into actionable behavior patterns.” said Natalia Micheletti, CEO and Co-Founder of Pryze. “Operators want focused teams and great customer experiences. Employees want to feel seen and rewarded. This will bridge the gap between what operators want and what employees actually do.” With Pryze, employees begin each shift by selecting goals set by management, such as upselling desserts or increasing the average ticket, and then “lock in” to a focus session. They earn points for time spent focused and for goals completed, and lose points when they check their phones. At the end of each shift, employees bank their points and can redeem them for real rewards. By combining its proprietary behavioral data with revenue metrics, Pryze shows managers what drives results and helps them change employee behavior in real time. To view a demo of the new app and management dashboard or to schedule a live walkthrough, visit www.pryzeapp.com. The post Pryze Launches Fully Redesigned Platform appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: Bar Prince Unveils Mythical Legends: A New Cocktail Menu Inspired By Scotland’s Most Enchanting Folklore
articles.titleKo: Bar Prince Unveils Mythical Legends: A New Cocktail Menu Inspired By Scotland’s Most Enchanting Folklore
articles.originalSummary: Following the success of last year’s Connected Icons , Bar Prince at The Balmoral invites guests into a world of myth, magic and storytelling with the launch of its newest cocktail menu, Mythical Legends . Launching this autumn, Mythical Legends draws inspiration from Scotland’s most enduring folklore, transforming legendary creatures and ancient tales into an immersive cocktail experience. From unicorns and selkies to witches, dragons and kelpies, the menu celebrates the stories that have captivated imaginations for generations. Overseen by Head Bartender Mattia Rovaris, each signature cocktail has been individually created by Bar Prince’s mixologists, with every serve inspired by a different Scottish legend. Guests are invited to discover the inspiration behind each creation, with every drink offering its own connection to Scotland’s rich mythical heritage. The theme extends beyond the cocktails themselves. Bespoke illustrations bring each character to life, transforming the menu into a contemporary storybook. Each copy has been meticulously handcrafted by Edinburgh’s Crawford Bookbinders, whose traditional techniques and attention to detail add another layer of craftsmanship, echoing Scotland’s long tradition of storytelling and artistry. Enhancing the experience further is a bespoke Mythical Legends Scent Mist, inspired by Scotland’s ancient forests, mist-covered lochs and legendary landscapes. Blending notes of cedarwood, chamomile and sandalwood with Scots pine, citrus and warming spice, it has been designed to transport guests into the world that inspired the cocktails. Capturing the spirit of Scotland’s wild landscapes and folklore through new techniques and evocative flavour combinations, highlights include The Untamed One , a shimmering tribute to Scotland’s national animal, the unicorn, blending Scottish vodka with coconut water, white chocolate, banana and lime leaf for an elegant serve. Double Identity , inspired by the selkie’s existence between land and sea, reimagines the whisky sour with coastal Scotch whisky, honey, citrus and warming spice. Meanwhile, Kingdom’s Cauldron draws on the tale of the Witch of Fife, combining whisky, botanicals, chocolate, vanilla and caramel into a rich and mysterious after-dark cocktail. Elsewhere, guests can discover the inspiration behind Messy-Nessie , a bright and herbaceous whisky highball inspired by Scotland’s most famous monster, or enjoy Fairy Queen , a decadent take on the Mai Tai featuring aged rum, roasted Brazil nuts and dark cacao. More than a cocktail menu, Mythical Legends is an invitation to explore Scotland’s legendary past through flavour, artistry and imagination. Continuing Bar Prince’s commitment to innovative cocktail storytelling, each drink reveals a new chapter in Scotland’s rich folklore. Mattia Rovaris, Head Bartender at Bar Prince, said: “Building on the success of Connected Icons, Mythical Legends gave our team the opportunity to tell a new chapter of Scotland’s story through the lens of folklore. Each cocktail has been created by a different member of the bar team, making the menu a true collective of ideas, creativity and personal interpretation. Paired with bespoke illustrations and scent, we’ve created an experience that invites guests to discover something new with every serve.” Discover the stories, flavours and aromas behind Scotland’s most captivating folklore at Bar Prince at The Balmoral. Mythical Legends launches this autumn. For more information or to reserve a table, visit: https://www.roccofortehotels.com/hotels-and-resorts/the-balmoral-hotel/dining/bar-prince/cocktail-menu/

articles.title: Walk-On’s Gives In-Depth Look at Newest Prototype
articles.titleKo: Walk-On’s Gives In-Depth Look at Newest Prototype
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Walk-On’s is offering a closer look at its next-generation restaurant prototype, a smaller, more flexible sports bar model aimed at reducing development costs and opening new real estate opportunities for franchisees. The company unveiled interior renderings of the prototype, which will range from 3,500 to 4,500 square feet, compared with the brand’s traditional restaurants of 7,000 to more than 8,000 square feet. The first location is scheduled to open in early 2027 on Perkins Road in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, measuring approximately 3,688 square feet with seating for 125 guests. Developed with Madrid-based restaurant firm Livit, the prototype uses a modular “kit of parts” that allows franchisees to customize certain features according to their market, available real estate, and operating preferences. The smaller footprint represents a significant departure from Walk-On’s traditional sports bar format, which has relied on expansive dining rooms and large gathering spaces. The company is seeking to preserve its full-service experience and sports-focused atmosphere within a restaurant that requires substantially less space. The prototype includes a redesigned kitchen equipped with clamshell grills and other equipment intended to simplify employee training, improve food consistency, and reduce ticket times. Despite the smaller kitchen, Walk-On’s plans to maintain its full menu. The restaurant will also feature a peninsula-style bar that can be adapted to different floor plans, a large television wall, and upgraded audiovisual equipment. A flexible lounge area will accommodate groups and game-day gatherings or provide additional dining capacity when needed. Off-premises business is another consideration. Dedicated pickup cubbies near the host stand will provide a designated area for DoorDash, Uber Eats, and other delivery orders, separating pickup traffic from the dining experience. Walk-On’s is also incorporating local sports memorabilia, including high school jerseys and athlete displays, to connect individual restaurants with their communities. Other features include an outdoor television wall and a host stand that doubles as a merchandise station. “We wanted to rethink what the Walk-On’s experience can look like without losing what makes us Walk-On’s,” CEO and cofounder Brandon Landry said in a statement. “The new design gives our franchisees more flexibility in where and how they build, while keeping the energy, hospitality and community connection our guests know and love.” The company previously announced that it was targeting development costs below $2 million for the new format, a key consideration as restaurant construction expenses continue to challenge franchise expansion. The prototype also draws on the performance of Walk-On’s approximately 3,700-square-foot restaurant at The Battery in Atlanta. According to the company, that location demonstrated the feasibility of operating its full menu and sports bar experience in a smaller, inline restaurant. For operators, this intelligence translates into faster-moving lines, contextual upsells, and reduced strain on front-of-house staff.
