articles.title: How Long Should a Menu Price Live?
articles.titleKo: How Long Should a Menu Price Live?
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . In 2024, Trader Joe’s raised the price of a banana from 19 cents to 23 cents . Normally, a four-cent price increase wouldn’t attract much attention. This one made national news. There was a reason. Trader Joe’s had sold bananas for 19 cents for more than two decades. The price had become familiar enough that changing it meant more than charging four additional cents for a piece of fruit. Nineteen cents had become part of what customers associated with Trader Joe’s value proposition. That raises an important question for quick-service restaurants. At a time when digital menu boards, apps, sophisticated analytics and AI make it increasingly easy to change prices, how do restaurants decide which prices should actually move? Pricing researcher Utpal Dholakia recently explored the idea that every price has a “life.” In “ What Decides the Life of a Price ?” he argues that some prices survive for years or decades while others disappear within hours, and that their appropriate lifespan depends on more than the technology or economics of changing them. It also depends on what those prices mean to customers. For QSRs, that distinction matters because not all menu prices play the same role. Some Prices Are More Memorable Than Others Consider the difference between the price of a Big Mac, a new limited-time product and a temporary offer in an app. All three are prices, but they occupy very different places in the customer’s mind. Someone who has bought Big Macs for years may not know the exact price at the restaurant down the street, but has had many opportunities to develop a sense of what a Big Mac should cost. A new product has no such history, while a temporary offer may be evaluated once and quickly forgotten. That suggests a continuum. Some prices are essentially forgettable. Others become reference prices, where customers may not remember the exact amount but develop expectations about what the product should cost. And a small number become iconic prices, where the price itself becomes part of what the brand represents. Costco’s $1.50 hot dog and soda combination, unchanged since 1985 , is perhaps the ultimate example. The further a price moves along that continuum, the more complicated changing it becomes. QSR Customers Have Long Memories Customer memory is especially important in QSR because of purchase frequency. A leisure traveler might stay at a particular hotel once or twice a year, encountering different dates, room types and market conditions each time. Hotel customers have also been trained for decades to expect prices to vary, so there may be no obvious answer to what a particular hotel room “should” cost. Now consider a customer who buys the same lunch from the same QSR two or three times a week. That customer has dozens of opportunities each year to observe the price of the same product. Over time, that familiar price becomes a reference point. A price increase can communicate more than the additional amount the customer has to pay. It can signal that the customer’s understanding of the brand’s value is no longer accurate. And when the price changes, the old price doesn’t simply disappear. Customers remember it, consciously or not, and compare the new price against it. The Value Wars Were Really About Reference Prices McDonald’s experienced this very publicly in 2024. After social media posts about an $18 Big Mac meal attracted widespread attention, McDonald’s USA President Joe Erlinger published an open letter addressing perceptions about the company’s prices . He reported that average menu prices had increased about 40 percent since 2019, while the average Big Mac had risen 21 percent, from $4.39 to $5.29. articles.title: KFC’s Confidence in Kwench’s Potential Continues to Grow
articles.titleKo: KFC’s Confidence in Kwench’s Potential Continues to Grow
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Dhiren Karnani noticed a guest behavior that’s become a common tale in QSR. Beverages are often now a price of entry. Yet how does that manifest at a legacy chain like KFC, as synonymous with its hero product (not drinks) as any retail operation in the country? Karnani, who elevated to the role of senior director, global head of food and experience at KFC Global in May, promoting from global director, next generation KFC and new concepts, says the aim started from the first observation and found its way to the second. Could KFC get customers to come for drinks and stay for chicken? Earlier in the year, the company began materially expanding “Kwench by KFC,” a specialty beverage extension that first ran across 38 stores. Success led to visions through the U.K. and Ireland over the summer and, as Yum! Brands shared in Q4, a 3,000 or so restaurant outlook by calendar-end 2026. Kwench appreciated a splashy “thirst-trap” Canadian launch in August, and, more recently, backed by a £38m investment from corporate, set course for Scotland. The Middle East and other global markets are lining up, too. Fueling Kwench are those same outset points. One, the market, from upstarts to drive-thru coffee concepts to large fast-food enterprises such as Taco Bell and McDonald’s, is responding to a surge of a specialty options capturing demand from energy to dirty sodas to refreshers. The other note is more than 90 percent of Kwench users in tests said they “loved” the new drinks and about half shared they’d visit KFC specifically for them. So, as Karnani and the brand hoped, customers came for Kwench, even if they weren’t, perhaps, showing up for chicken. That opened possibilities. “That’s actually what we’re seeing laid out,” says Karnani, who joined Yum! in 2017 as a senior brand manager for KFC U.K. and Ireland, “where this is definitely creating a halo and overall transaction growth. And that’s creating a lot more confidence to the system when it comes to Kwench. So, we’re really going deep on building this.” As Kwench matures, it’s broadening innovation. KFC added Matcha about a month ago, made with PerfectTed ceremonial grade tea and vanilla syrup, strawberry puree, and shortcake crumb. Karnani says matcha has become a category, like iced coffee was for younger consumers, needed by brands to signal you’re a beverage destination, especially later in the day. It’s evolved toward less of a menu alternative and more of a complement. Kwench, largely speaking, aims to “create the favorite version of the drink they already love,” Karnani says. With an item as buzzy as matcha, it meant partnering with a company like PerfectTed and delivering satisfaction on something familiar. “The reaction on social has been amazing,” he says. “People are like … ‘I can’t believe I am getting this matcha quality from KFC.’ And that’s exactly what we would want.” Karnani adds Kwench will keep tinkering with categories—today the brand has shakes, lattes, like an Iced Tiramisu, sparkling lemonades, and boba. A key, he explains, being to keep Kwench’s focus relatively narrow. “How do we really go deep in the categories where we have a clear right to play?” Karnani says. KFC developed Kwench so restaurants could move quickly as preferences do. Meanwhile, Kwench will create new news for categories people recognize. Currently, its Krunch Shake, caramel milkshake drizzled with caramel sauce, and topped with a krunchy speculoos crumb, is the brand’s top seller. Playing off a “Downright Dirty Meal” that arrived in the U.K. with “dirty items,” from loaded fries to a Louisiana burger, Kwench spun the item into a “Dirty Millionaire” version with chocolate cookie crumbs and chocolate and caramel sauces. “That’s another way we’re bringing new news into the platform, where it’s fully integrated into the menu concepts,” Karnani says. State of Play Hospitality will open its second Flight Club venue in Texas on Friday, Oct. 23, at Village on the Parkway in Addison, marking the Social Darts concept’s Dallas-Fort Worth debut. Known for reimagining the classic British game of darts into an interactive, tech-enabled social experience, Flight Club blends the thrill of friendly competition with craft cocktails, chef-driven cuisine and design-led hospitality to create a one-of-a-kind destination for dining, drinking and entertainment. Located at 5100 Belt Line Road, Suite 776, Addison, TX, the space spans approximately 8,000 square feet, accommodates up to 400 guests and features 12 semi-private playing areas known as oches and two patios. The venue introduces Flight Club’s unique approach to elevated hospitality to North Texas, offering a warm, lively setting for everything from casual nights out and date nights to celebrations, group gatherings and large-scale corporate events. “Addison always felt like an excellent fit for our first Flight Club in the Dallas-Fort Worth metro,” said Toby Harris, president and CEO of State of Play Hospitality, which operates Flight Club in North America under license. “Its central location, thriving dining and entertainment scene, and local corporate community made Addison a natural choice. We can’t wait to open the doors and share this beautiful new space with our guests.” At the heart of the experience is Flight Club’s proprietary Social Darts technology, which automatically scores every throw and powers a collection of fast-paced, multiplayer games designed for groups of all sizes and skill levels. The innovative system transforms the traditional pub pastime into an engaging social competition, allowing guests to focus on the fun rather than keeping score. Each of the venue’s 12 oches serves as a semi-private playing area for up to 12 guests, complete with a dartboard, dedicated seating and attentive tableside service, with larger groups able to reserve multiple oches. Individually decorated and thoughtfully designed, the oches give guests their own space to eat, drink, play and socialize while remaining connected to the energy of the broader venue. Food and beverage are equally central to the Flight Club experience. The chef-driven menu emphasizes dishes made for sharing between dart throws, including flatbreads, sliders and tacos. With options thoughtfully crafted to accommodate different dietary preferences, the menu makes group dining more seamless and encourages guests to focus on great company and playful competition. The Addison venue puts a local spin on Flight Club’s signature design aesthetic, drawing on the nostalgic charm of Victorian fairgrounds and the playful energy of traditional British pubs while incorporating eclectic artwork, richly layered interiors and unexpected nods to Dallas and Texas. articles.title: Jefferson’s Announces Annual ‘Coach of the Year’ Program
articles.titleKo: Jefferson’s Announces Annual ‘Coach of the Year’ Program
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Family-friendly wing spot Jefferson’s is bringing back its “Coach of the Year” program once more, launched in celebration of National Coaches Day on Oct. 6. Now in its fourth year, the program has, in the last few years, honored dozens of coaches across all five states where Jefferson’s has locations: Kansas, Missouri, Tennessee, Alabama, and Georgia, resulting in an outpouring of support for the many beloved local coaches in Jefferson’s communities. The Jefferson’s Coach of the Year program celebrates coaches from any sport who exemplify compassionate leadership, community spirit, and dedication to their players. Coaches can be nominated by athletes, parents and guardians, school officials, neighbors, or anyone who has witnessed their impact. This year, the program will also launch at several new Jefferson’s locations that opened their doors in the last year, including restaurants in Bellevue, Tenn., Hartselle, Ala., and Weiss Lake, Ala., giving even more communities an opportunity to recognize a coach who goes above and beyond. How It Works: The nomination period is open now and will close at 11:59 p.m. on Oct. 18. Coaches of any sport, working with athletes of all ages, are eligible for nomination. Winners from each location will receive a $500 Jefferson’s gift card and their names added to the “Jefferson’s Coach of the Year” plaque displayed prominently at their respective restaurant. “Coaches have an incredible ability to shape not only athletes, but the communities around them,” said Brandon Graham, president of Jefferson’s Restaurants. “We’re proud to bring the Coach of the Year and establish it as a Jefferson’s tradition—and expand it to our newer locations. As Jefferson’s continues to grow, it’s important that we continue building relationships with the people and organizations that make each of our communities special.” 2025 Recap: Last year’s winners were chosen from an incredible pool of community leaders . Winners can be found on the individual location’s page. If you know of a life-changing coach in a Jefferson’s community, you can submit a nomination through the official Jefferson’s website, active now through 11:59 p.m. CST on Oct. 18. Winners will be announced on Nov. 16. The post Jefferson’s Announces Annual ‘Coach of the Year’ Program appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: First-Party Platform Sauce Announces Strategic Partnership with Grubhub
articles.titleKo: First-Party Platform Sauce Announces Strategic Partnership with Grubhub
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Sauce, a leading first-party ordering, delivery and retention platform for restaurants, today announced a strategic partnership with Grubhub, a leading U.S. food-ordering and delivery marketplace. Through the partnership, Sauce will become a direct ordering and delivery partner available to Grubhub merchants, enabling restaurants to support direct sales while leveraging Grubhub’s nationwide delivery network for fulfillment. Together, Sauce and Grubhub will provide restaurants with a seamless solution that pairs Sauce’s high-converting direct ordering platform with Grubhub’s nationwide fulfillment network. This partnership enables merchants to drive direct orders and retain ownership of customer relationships, all while leveraging Grubhub’s reliable delivery infrastructure. The partnership comes as restaurants increasingly seek ways to build stronger direct channels while maintaining reliable delivery operations. Through this joint offering, Sauce powers the customer-facing ordering and data tools, while Grubhub connects merchants with drivers for reliable last-mile delivery fulfillment. “Restaurants deserve online order and delivery technology that grows their business, strengthens connections with their customers, and delivers a best-in-class ordering experience,” said Li-ran Navon, CEO and Co-Founder of Sauce. “We’re excited to partner with Grubhub to give restaurant operators a powerful direct ordering solution backed by one of the most trusted delivery networks in the industry. Together, we’re making it easier for restaurants to support direct sales while building lasting customer loyalty.” Through the partnership, eligible restaurants will gain access to: Sauce’s high-converting branded online ordering platform Direct ordering websites optimized for mobile and SEO Integrated loyalty, marketing and AI-powered customer engagement tools Ownership of customer data and relationships Seamless delivery fulfillment powered by Grubhub’s nationwide logistics network Exclusive promotional opportunities and onboarding incentives “We’re excited to partner with Sauce to bring together direct ordering technology and delivery capabilities in a seamless experience for restaurants,” said Rachel Winkelman, Vice President, Enterprise Partnerships at Grubhub. “This partnership reflects our shared commitment to helping restaurants support their business and better serve their customers. By combining Sauce’s direct ordering technology with Grubhub’s nationwide delivery network, we’re providing merchants with an end-to-end solution that helps drive sales, streamline operations, and deliver a great customer experience.” For more information, visit www.getsauce.com. articles.title: Sushi by Boū Celebrates Grand Opening at Trump National Doral Miami Golf Resort
articles.titleKo: Sushi by Boū Celebrates Grand Opening at Trump National Doral Miami Golf Resort
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Sushi by Boū, the largest omakase brand in the U.S., today celebrates the grand opening of its newest location at Trump National Doral Miami, the renowned Miami golf resort. The new restaurant features a 20-seat omakase counter, Sushi by Boū’s largest to date, as the company builds on its success at hospitality destinations and sets its sights on additional luxury golf properties nationwide. The opening builds on Sushi by Boū’s established history at Trump National Doral, where the brand previously hosted on-property activations, including serving guests surrounding the Cadillac Championship. That existing connection with the resort’s guests, members, and event community made Doral a natural home for Sushi by Boū’s most ambitious counter yet. A WINNING FORMULA, NOW ON A BIGGER STAGE Sushi by Boū’s small-footprint model has consistently found success by transforming underutilized spaces within hotels, resorts, and other premier properties into high-performing dining destinations. Golf resorts, in particular, have proven to be a natural fit: guests who spend the day on the course are looking for an experience that matches the caliber of their surroundings once the sun goes down, and Sushi by Boū’s chef-guided, high-energy omakase format delivers exactly that. The Trump National Doral location builds directly on that momentum. Featuring Sushi by Boū’s largest counter to date, the restaurant can accommodate larger groups, golf outings, and resort events as an amenity for the property while preserving the brand’s intimate, chef-led experience. “The arrival of Sushi by Boū marks an exciting new chapter in the culinary experience at Trump National Doral Miami,” said Mickael Damelincourt, Managing Director. “Its intimate, elevated take on omakase brings a fresh and dynamic dimension to our dining portfolio, complementing our exceptional collection of restaurants while giving guests, members and the local community yet another compelling reason to dine at the resort.” At the center of the space is an omakase counter crafted from Italian Calacatta Viola marble, whose burgundy and violet veining brings richness and movement to the interior. Overhead, a custom gold-leaf wallcovering, fabricated in France and adorned with hand-painted koi, complements the soft, dim lighting to create a warm, cinematic atmosphere. Together, the materials, lighting, and culinary performance capture the luxury and intrigue of a hidden speakeasy without feeling overly formal. “Trump National Doral is an iconic destination at the intersection of business, leisure, and world-class hospitality, making it a natural fit for Sushi by Boū and the elevated, high-energy dining experience we bring to every destination,” said Erika London, CEO of Sushi by Boū. “We’re excited to bring Sushi by Boū to more exceptional luxury properties like this where we can complement the guest experience with a distinctive dining amenity while also engaging the local community.” A STORIED HOME ON THE GREEN Trump National Doral is one of the most recognized names in golf, with a competitive history that includes hosting the Cadillac Championship, a fixture on the PGA Tour for decades. Sushi by Boū previously brought its signature hospitality to the property through past event activations on-site, giving the brand an established relationship with Doral’s guests, members, and event crews well before opening a permanent counter. With this opening, Sushi by Boū expands to four locations across South Florida, with the Trump National Doral restaurant becoming the largest in the brand’s entire portfolio. Sushi by Boū at Trump National Doral offers the brand’s full range of chef-guided tasting menus alongside handcrafted cocktails, premium sake and rare Japanese whiskies in a high-energy, speakeasy-style setting befitting one of golf’s most storied addresses. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The Red Robin Prime Rib Stack Burger delivers an over-the-top burger experience made for the meat lovers seeking bold, indulgent flavors. Red Robin Gourmet Burgers, Inc. is introducing the new, limited-time Prime Rib Stack Burger, a meat-on-meat masterpiece for guests looking for a premium burger experience. That’s not all, Red Robin is bringing back two fan-favorite burgers to the Big YUMMM Deals menu, delivering even more YUMMM and value. The new menu and returning items will be available at participating Red Robin locations nationwide starting Oct. 19. The Red Robin Prime Rib Stack Burger delivers an over-the-top burger experience made for the meat lovers seeking bold, indulgent flavors. The limited-time burger features a hand-pressed beef patty, tender sliced prime rib, Monterey Jack cheese, caramelized onion and garlic aioli on a black-and-white sesame seed brioche bun, served with a bottomless side. The burger goodness doesn’t stop there. Red Robin is also bringing back two fan-favorite burgers, the Bleu Ribbon Burger and Burnin’ Love Burger, to its Big YUMMM Deals menu, giving burger lovers even more craveable choices at a great value. The Bleu Ribbon Burger features HEINZ 57 Sauce, bleu cheese crumbles, crispy onion straws, lettuce, tomato and green chili aioli on a brioche bun, while the Burnin’ Love Burger returns with fried jalapeño coins, salsa, pepper jack cheese, lettuce, tomato and green chili aioli on a brioche bun, both served with a bottomless side and bottomless beverage. “Burgers are in our DNA, and we wanted to create a burger that brings a little extra indulgence to the table. The Prime Rib Stack Burger is piled high with all the good stuff – a juicy beef patty, tender sliced prime rib, melty cheese and plenty of flavor in every bite,” said Brian Sullivan, executive chef and vice president of Culinary & Beverage Innovation at Red Robin. “We’re carrying that same spirit into our beverages, with our new bottomless Refreshers, which tap into some of the most fun and current beverage trends our guests crave. From an over-the-top burger to bold, playful drinks, we can’t wait for guests to dig in and try all the delicious new items coming to Red Robin.” Red Robin isn’t done rolling out new flavors just yet! From appetizers to desserts, even more satisfying menu items are joining the lineup, including: Spinach Artichoke Dip: Cheesy spinach artichoke dip topped with grated Parmesan and served with warm tortilla chips. New Chicken Wing Flavors: Available in Lemon Pepper , which combines classic lemon pepper seasoning with a savory citrusy punch, and Lemon Pepper Buzz, which adds a spark with Red Robin’s signature Buffalo-style sauce for a tangy, spicy finish. Signature Grilled Chicken & Broccoli: Tender grilled chicken breast finished your way with a choice of ancho marinade, Whiskey River ® BBQ sauce, teriyaki or blackened. Cookie Dough Milkshake: Vanilla soft serve blended with cookie dough, topped with whipped cream, chocolate syrup and cookie dough. Also available in chocolate soft serve. Salted Caramel Brownie Milkshake: Vanilla soft serve blended with chocolate chip brownies, salted caramel and chocolate, topped with whipped cream and caramel sauce. To wash down all those mouthwatering flavors, Red Robin is launching a new line of Bottomless Refreshers. Guests can energize any Refresher flavor with Red Bull, giving them a colorful, refreshing option to sip alongside their favorite meal. The new beverage will be available in a variety of flavors including Tropical Dragon Fruit, Mango Passion Lemonade, Sunset Lemonade, Poppin’ Purple Lemonade and Raspberry Limeade. articles.title: CAVA Releases New Greek Goddess Dressing
articles.titleKo: CAVA Releases New Greek Goddess Dressing
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The new Greek Goddess dressing is CAVA’s Mediterranean twist on a classic green goddess dressing. CAVA is channeling Greek Goddess energy with a fresh lineup of offerings built around an all-new Greek Goddess dressing. The latest innovations pair fresh, herby Mediterranean flavors with wholesome ingredients, alongside a seasonal Pomegranate Apple drink. To celebrate the launch — and prove it’s no myth that big flavor and healthful choices go hand in hand — CAVA is taking inspiration from the ancient Greeks themselves, with a one-of-a-kind Greek Goddess arriving in New York City tomorrow. The center of the celebration? CAVA’s new Greek Goddess dressing, a tangy blend of rich Greek yogurt, lemon juice, garlic, herbs, and spices. The new dressing serves as the crowning touch on two new curated bowls, bringing a fresh twist to CAVA’s Mediterranean menu. Meet the Greek Goddess Lineup Greek Goddess Salmon Bowl: A colorful and satisfying bowl with a creamy green drizzle. CAVA’s Glazed Salmon is served over saffron rice and arugula with red pepper hummus, traditional hummus, pickled onions, fiery broccoli, sumac cabbage slaw, and the new Greek Goddess dressing. Greek Goddess Steak Salad: An epic mix of greens, grilled steak, and bold Mediterranean flavor. Grilled steak is served over Power Greens with traditional hummus and tzatziki, plus tomato + cucumber, sumac cabbage slaw, kalamata olives, feta, pita crisps, and Greek Goddess dressing. Pomegranate Apple Drink: Move over pumpkin, apple is the star flavor of fall 2026. This seasonal drink balances slightly sweet and tart flavors in a vibrant red sip that’s made for crisp fall days, peak foliage, and apple-picking adventures. The new Greek Goddess dressing is CAVA’s Mediterranean twist on a classic green goddess dressing, delivering a tangy, herby flavor that pairs deliciously with glazed salmon or grilled steak. CAVA superfans may even recognize the flavors from the brand’s Greek Goddess dip sold in grocery stores, which inspired this new format reimagined for bowls and pitas in restaurants across the country. “Our menu is inspired by the Mediterranean tradition of bringing together bold flavors, vibrant ingredients and food that leaves you feeling as good as it tastes. That balance may feel like a Greek myth, but its core to how I grew up, and the Mediterranean way has been proving it true for centuries,” said Ted Xenohristos, Co-Founder and Chief Concept Officer of CAVA. “Our new Greek Goddess dressing gives guests another way to enjoy the ingredients they already know and love.” A Taste of the Mediterranean, Set in Stone in NYC The Greek Goddess is also making her mark beyond the menu. Tomorrow, CAVA will transform Flatiron Plaza into a modern-day ode to ancient Greece with an activation that’s truly set in stone. Passersby can also get a taste of the new menu, sampling CAVA’s Greek Goddess dressing paired with fan-favorite pita chips and the seasonal Pomegranate Apple drink. The Greek Goddess may be holding court in Flatiron Plaza, but her reign extends far beyond NYC. A limited number of CAVA Rewards members across the U.S. who text a limited-time code to CAVA will score a complimentary entree reward to try the new Greek Goddess menu, bringing the Greek Goddess energy to CAVA fans from coast to coast. Join CAVA Rewards at cava.com/rewards ahead of time for a chance to be crowned with the reward. Be sure to keep an eye on @CAVA on socials for all the divine details. The new offerings are currently available for guests to enjoy at CAVA restaurants nationwide. Guests can taste the fall lineup by ordering in-restaurant, online, or through the CAVA app. For more information, visit CAVA.com and follow @CAVA on Instagram. articles.title: McAlister’s Franchisee Awards Nearly $20,000 in Classroom Grants
articles.titleKo: McAlister’s Franchisee Awards Nearly $20,000 in Classroom Grants
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Following the success of its first Together For Teachers campaign, TSG Restaurants is celebrating the meaningful impact the initiative has made in classrooms across Texas, Oklahoma, and Kansas. Created to recognize outstanding local educators while investing directly in the communities TSG Restaurants serves, the campaign invited teachers from communities surrounding its 79 McAlister’s Deli locations to share their stories and the difference they make in their classrooms every day. Local restaurant teams selected three Spotlight Teachers from each community, whose stories were featured on their local McAlister’s Deli Facebook pages as community members rallied behind them through social media engagement. One teacher from each participating location received a $250 classroom grant, resulting in $19,750 invested directly into local classrooms to help educators purchase supplies and educational resources ahead of the new school year. While the campaign generated exceptional engagement across social media, its greatest success can now be seen inside classrooms. Teachers used their grants to launch student-run vocational programs, purchase flexible seating, create more welcoming learning environments, provide school supplies for every student, expand music education programs, and invest in instructional resources that will benefit students throughout the school year. One recipient, Erika N., used the funds to help launch Leopard Brew, a student-run classroom coffee shop where students practice vocational and life skills including customer service, communication, money management, and following directions. “Leopard Brew will provide my students with hands-on opportunities to practice important vocational and life skills… giving our students a meaningful way to build confidence and independence while serving our school community.” Another recipient, Jennifer F., invested in podcasting equipment that will allow students to tell their stories, debate ideas, and strengthen communication and public-speaking skills. “This opportunity will help them build confidence, strengthen communication and public-speaking skills, and learn how to formulate and express their thoughts effectively.” For first-year teacher Paige T., the grant helped transform an empty classroom into a welcoming environment for students. “Starting the year with a classroom that feels like home not only for myself but all of my students… has been a huge blessing.” “At TSG Restaurants, serving our communities extends far beyond the four walls of our restaurants,” said Stephen Lee, President of TSG Restaurants. “Together For Teachers was created to celebrate educators and invest directly in the classrooms where future generations are shaped every day. Seeing how these teachers transformed a simple gift into opportunities that will benefit hundreds of students has been incredibly rewarding, and it reinforces our belief that supporting local communities is one of the most meaningful ways we can live out our purpose.” The Together For Teachers campaign reflects TSG Restaurants’ ongoing commitment to community involvement and keeping people at the heart of its mission. From supporting educators and nonprofits to partnering with local organizations and schools, the company continues to invest in initiatives that create lasting, meaningful impact in the neighborhoods its restaurants proudly serve. articles.title: How Lisa Dahl Turned Grief into a Sedona Culinary Empire
articles.titleKo: How Lisa Dahl Turned Grief into a Sedona Culinary Empire
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . There’s something about cooking with fire that grounds Lisa Dahl. The soft char of a wood-fired grill transforms a dish, and as she tends to the embers, she is reminded of how she, too, has reemerged from the ashes and allowed herself to be transformed. She moves effortlessly between being a self-taught chef, restaurateur, culinary visionary, and philanthropist. Over the past 30 years, her restaurants (Mariposa, Cucina Rustica, Dahl & Di Luca, Butterfly Burger, and Pisa Lisa) have transformed Arizona’s culinary landscape. She’s published multiple cookbooks, appeared on countless television specials, and told the story of her culinary rise time and time again. But it’s the story beneath the accolades—the one about grief, fire, and rebirth—that defines her most. No identity is more sacred to Dahl than that of being a mother. Even after the devastating loss of her son, Justin, in 1994, she never stopped being one. His death lit a flame inside her, one that has never gone out. Everything she did then, and continues to do today, carries Justin’s legacy forward. In 1995, she felt guided to Sedona, a desert town nestled in the northern Verde Valley of Arizona. She didn’t arrive to build a culinary empire; she came to escape her heartbreak. Immersed in the red-rock canyons, turquoise waterfalls, and the fiery glow of the desert sun, she began to heal. Decades later, that same sun would still find her standing over an open flame. “Sedona is indescribable. When I arrived, I started hiking every day. I was healing in nature because I was very raw and fearful, and I’ve never moved to a place where I didn’t know a soul,” Dahl says. “I asked myself, ‘What am I doing here? At the time, her partner was an Italian chef, and when an opportunity arose to take over a local restaurant that was failing, Dahl felt a tug at her soul. She had always loved cooking; her mother, grandmother, and nanny were all fantastic home cooks, and she would always cook with her son. When the doors of Dahl & Di Luca Ristorante Italiano opened later that year, something unlocked inside Dahl. It became an energizer for the town—Sedona had never seen a fine-dining restaurant of this caliber before. It was warmly welcomed by the community, and in that welcome, she found healing. “I was in the early stages of recovery from the loss of Justin when Dahl & Di Luca was born,” Dahl says. “Through the process of engaging with people, it became a community hub, and it was amazing because we could be charitable and immerse ourselves in this town as givers.” What would become her signature philosophy began to take form: “When you cook with love, you feed the soul.” As she opened more concepts throughout Sedona—from Mariposa’s Latin-inspired fine-dining grill to Pisa Lisa’s casual, artisanal wood-fired pizzas—her ability to serve others with love and intention was magnified. Even as a teenager developing her own recipes, she always wanted to bring out the essence of the food in its natural form, letting fire do what words could not. “If the food doesn’t speak, you have nothing,” Dahl adds. “You can have the most beautiful restaurants, but the food must touch the soul. Beginning this fall, guests will see elements of PDQ’s original visual identity return to restaurants and digital channels, refreshed for today’s guests. Fifteen years ago, PDQ set out to do chicken differently: buttermilk brined and hand-breaded to order, made with quality ingredients and served with a level of hospitality that made guests feel like regulars from their very first visit. The anniversary marks a new chapter for PDQ, but one that starts by looking back at what made the brand special in the first place. As PDQ looks forward, the quick-service brand is strengthening its leadership and operational foundation across every level of the organization, from restaurant operations and marketing to C-suite leadership and strategic collaboration across the business. This enhanced approach is designed to create greater alignment and a more consistent guest experience across every PDQ location. “PDQ has built its legacy behind the concept of people dedicated to quality, serving delicious food and making every guest feel welcome,” said Nina Franchina, Chief People Officer. “For 15 years, that commitment to quality has been at the heart of who we are, and as we celebrate where we’ve been, we’re excited to carry that same dedication forward as we build the next 15 years of PDQ.” Beginning this fall, guests will see elements of PDQ’s original visual identity return to restaurants and digital channels, refreshed for today’s guests. The rollout begins with the exterior of PDQ’s St. Petersburg restaurant this October, followed by a gradual systemwide rollout. Guest Favorites Are Back + $15 Tender Bucket Deal As PDQ looks back on its journey this anniversary season, the restaurant is especially thankful for the community that made it possible. To show its gratitude, PDQ is sharing a special anniversary offer: from October 19 through November 30 (while supplies last), guests can enjoy 15 hand-breaded chicken tenders and an 8-ounce dipping sauce for just $15, the perfect spread for gathering with family and friends this fall. PDQ’s anniversary fall menu brings back a fan-favorite original and introduces a lineup of flavors inspired by the best tastes of the season including: Apples & Toffee Dip: An original PDQ menu item makes its return, pairing fresh, crisp apples with rich, creamy toffee dip. Thanksgiving Sandwich: PDQ puts its own spin on a Thanksgiving favorite with a hand-breaded crispy chicken breast, savory herb mayo, fresh lettuce and cranberry sauce, served on a toasted brioche bun. Pumpkin Pie Shake: A hand-spun fall favorite made with spiced pumpkin purée and garnished with whipped cream, cinnamon and a cherry. Apple Pie Shake: A hand-spun shake featuring apple, graham cracker crumbles, cinnamon and nutmeg, finished with whipped cream and additional graham cracker crumbles. Sugar Cookie: A seasonal sweet treat that rounds out PDQ’s fall lineup. Eye Scream Shake for Halloween Weekend PDQ is also giving guests a special Halloween treat with the Eye Scream Shake, available October 30 through November 1. The limited-time shake is spun with Candy Corn Monin syrup and rich blackberry purée, then topped with whipped cream, Halloween sprinkles and candy eyes for a festive holiday weekend treat. The 15 for $15 Tender Bucket, fall limited-time offerings and Eye Scream Shake are available at participating PDQ locations through their respective promotional periods. articles.title: GEN Korean BBQ to Sell 47 Restaurants to Chubby Cattle in $100 Million Deal
articles.titleKo: GEN Korean BBQ to Sell 47 Restaurants to Chubby Cattle in $100 Million Deal
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Chubby Cattle will assume restaurant-level operating responsibilities and lease obligations as it takes over each location. GEN Korean BBQ has signed a binding letter of intent to sell operations at 47 U.S. restaurants to Chubby Cattle Group in a $100 million transaction that would effectively shift the publicly traded company away from restaurant operations and toward its growing CPG business. The agreement, unanimously approved by GEN’s board of directors, calls for Chubby Cattle to take over the restaurants in four phases over 12 months. The companies are working to finalize the transaction within the next 30 days. GEN will retain ownership of its Korean BBQ brand and its entire CPG business. The company also plans to keep approximately three restaurants, including its Cerritos, California, location, to support product development, training, and staffing. Chubby Cattle will assume restaurant-level operating responsibilities and lease obligations as it takes over each location. The company plans to introduce wagyu-focused menus and fund restaurant conversions and buildouts using its own capital. The announcement does not specify whether all 47 restaurants will be rebranded under Chubby Cattle’s existing concepts. READ MORE : Gen Korean BBQ Considers $100M Sale of Restaurant Business Gen Korean BBQ Sees $100 Million Retail Opportunity Beyond Restaurants The transaction could substantially reduce GEN’s financial obligations. The company currently carries approximately $160 million in restaurant lease liabilities, which it expects to decrease as leases transfer to Chubby Cattle. “Securing a binding LOI with Chubby is a major milestone for GEN as part of the Company’s continued evolution into a premier CPG brand,” GEN chairman and CEO David Kim said in a statement. “We know Chubby through a partnership that is already delivering operating progress. This transaction would substantially reduce our restaurant lease obligations while giving GEN the option to participate in Chubby’s growth. We are moving quickly toward closing and believe this is the right next step for GEN and our shareholders.” Founded in 2016, Chubby Cattle operates more than 70 restaurants across over 25 brands, including Chubby Cattle, NIKU X, Wagyu House, and The X Pot. Its business spans fine dining, casual dining, and fast casual. Chubby Cattle reported $233 million in revenue in 2025, more than 10 times its revenue in 2021. The company also recently completed a capital raise at a $500 million valuation and is targeting 100 operating restaurants and one million Chubby Club members in 2026. The acquisition would give Chubby Cattle access to an established restaurant network and existing customer base as it expands its national presence. “Acquiring these 47 restaurants gives Chubby an established, high-traffic platform to accelerate our national growth,” Chubby Cattle founder David Zhao said in a statement. “GEN has built one of the leading Korean BBQ brands in the U.S. As we take over operations, we will build on the Korean BBQ experience these guests know with a wagyu-forward menu, and we are committed to completing this acquisition and executing a disciplined, phased transition.” Under the proposed transaction with Chubby Cattle, GEN will remain publicly traded, and its corporate infrastructure will be restructured to support the retail business. Senior staff will focus on expanding the company’s branded products rather than operating a national restaurant system. The agreement builds on an existing relationship between the companies. Earlier this year, GEN formed a joint venture with Chubby Cattle involving five restaurants that would transition to the Chubby Cattle brand. Beloved Portland-based ice cream maker Salt & Straw debuts the Strawberry Pretzel Cheesecake Tacolate , a brand new flavor joining the team’s growing suite of nostalgic, artisan ice cream tacos. This release follows last fall’s launch of Salt & Straw’s Cinnamon Ancho Tacolate , which was crafted in collaboration with Taco Bell, and immediately went viral and sold out during its initial launch weekend last year. The Strawberry Pretzel Cheesecake Tacolate marks the first line extension of the Tacolate since its launch last year, and is available in the freezers, alongside the original Cinnamon Ancho Tacolate, of all Salt & Straw shops across the country (find your local shop here ) on Friday, October 16th. Both Tacolate flavors stand as elevated odes to everyone’s favorite childhood treat, and – in true Salt & Straw fashion – utilize innovative flavors and ingredients dreamed up by Co-Founder and Head Ice Cream Maker Tyler Malek . The new Strawberry Pretzel Cheesecake Tacolate is a twist on a classic and features a hand-pressed waffle cone taco shell, filled with strawberry ice cream made with ripe Pacific Northwest berries, dipped in a cream cheese white chocolate shell, and sprinkled with crushed pretzels. These sweet, salty, tangy tacos will be served alongside a silky, vanilla bean cheesecake sauce. “We’re obsessed with strawberry cheesecake in the Salt & Straw test kitchen, and the Strawberry Tacolate lets us take that combination to another level, ” said Tyler Malek, cofounder and head ice cream innovator of Salt & Straw ice cream. “We pair fresh Pacific Northwest strawberry ice cream with cream cheese, white chocolate, and a salty pretzel crumble, all finished with a liquid cheesecake drizzle. The contrast of textures and flavors makes this one of my favorite creations.” The origins for the overall concept of the Tacolate dates back to 2016, when Salt & Straw first launched their version of an ice cream taco at their soft serve concept, Wiz Bang Bar. In 2022, Salt & Straw brought back their Chocolate Tacolates in a limited-run that sold out in minutes, before going on to partner with Taco Bell® in 2025 for the Cinnamon Ancho Tacolate launch. That original, fan-favorite Tacolate remains available in all Salt & Straw shops and by way of nationwide shipping via Salt & Straw’s website. Additionally, Salt & Straw is running a “Tacolate Tuesday” promotion across the remaining Tuesdays in October, where guests can buy one Tacolate and enjoy the second one for free. For more information and to find your local shop, visit www.saltandstraw.com and follow @saltandstraw. articles.title: Noodles & Company Makes Ramen Permanent Menu Item
articles.titleKo: Noodles & Company Makes Ramen Permanent Menu Item
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The expanded ramen lineup follows the breakout success of Chili Garlic Ramen, one of the most successful menu launches in Noodles & Company history. No one knows noodles like Noodles & Company. After more than 30 years of serving noodle dishes inspired by flavors from around the world, Noodles & Company is putting its own spin on another beloved noodle: ramen. Starting today, ramen noodles officially earn a permanent place on the Noodles & Company menu, launching with three bold, brothless bowls designed to deliver distinctly different flavor experiences. Gochujang Carbonara Ramen Noodles brings together Korean heat and Italian comfort, Sweet Sesame Steak Ramen Noodles balances savory and sweet flavors, and Spicy Korean Steak Ramen Noodles reimagines one of the brand’s longtime favorites with ramen noodles. The launch marks the beginning of a new permanent ramen category for Noodles & Company, giving the brand another way to showcase its noodle expertise while continuing to explore new flavors, combinations, and ramen creations over time. The expanded ramen lineup follows the breakout success of Chili Garlic Ramen, one of the most successful menu launches in Noodles & Company history. The limited-time dish brought more than 150,000 new guests to the brand, reinforcing what Noodles has known for more than 30 years: There are endless ways to experience a great bowl of noodles. “We’ve spent more than 30 years exploring what’s possible with noodles, and ramen gives us another incredible canvas for flavor and creativity,” said Tina Massey, vice president of culinary R&D at Noodles & Company. “What I love about this lineup is that each bowl delivers a completely different experience. From the creamy heat of the Gochujang Carbonara Ramen Noodles to the savory sweetness of Sweet Sesame Steak Ramen Noodles and the familiar bold flavor of Spicy Korean Steak Ramen Noodles, we’re showing just how versatile ramen can be while giving each dish a distinctly Noodles spin.” Three Distinct Ways to Ramen The new lineup showcases the versatility of ramen noodles through three brothless bowls featuring globally inspired sauces, fresh vegetables, and satisfying proteins: Gochujang Carbonara Ramen Noodles : Korean heat meets Italian comfort in an unexpected fusion featuring ramen noodles sautéed in a creamy gochujang-Parmesan carbonara sauce with bacon, napa cabbage and red cabbage, finished with grated Parmesan, Asian spice blend, and parsley. Sweet Sesame Steak Ramen Noodles : Savory meets sweet with ramen noodles sautéed with marinated steak, carrots, and red peppers, then finished with sesame seeds and cilantro for a satisfying balance of flavor and texture. Spicy Korean Steak Ramen Noodles : A ramen twist on the longtime guest favorite Spicy Korean Steak Noodles, this brothless bowl pairs ramen noodles with marinated steak, napa cabbage, red cabbage, and spinach in a sweet and spicy Korean-style gochujang barbecue sauce, topped with cucumber, scallions, and cilantro. “The incredible response to Chili Garlic Ramen showed us that our guests are hungry to see what Noodles can do with ramen,” said Dwayne Chambers, interim chief marketing officer at Noodles & Company. “Ramen gives us an exciting new way to build on 30 years of noodle expertise, bringing guests the comfort they love while continuing to surprise them with bold flavors and unexpected twists. Making ramen a permanent part of our menu is just the beginning of what we can do with this incredibly versatile noodle.” Noodles & Company’s new ramen menu is available starting today at restaurants nationwide, through the Noodles Rewards app and online at noodles.com . Gochujang Carbonara Ramen Noodles and Sweet Sesame Steak Ramen Noodles are available for a limited time, while ramen will remain a permanent menu category with new creations continuing to evolve the lineup. articles.title: California Pizza Kitchen Announces Collection of Salad Kits and Single-Serve Salads
articles.titleKo: California Pizza Kitchen Announces Collection of Salad Kits and Single-Serve Salads
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The new CPK collection will feature restaurant-inspired recipes, elevated ingredients, and bold California flavors. California Pizza Kitchen (CPK), the iconic restaurant brand that revolutionized pizza, in partnership with FiveStar Gourmet Foods, North America’s largest producer of fresh single-serve foods, announced the launch of a premium collection of CPK-inspired salad kits and single-serve salads. The first CPK fresh retail products are expected to launch nationwide in 2027, with broader distribution and additional innovation planned as the partnership grows. The collaboration taps CPK’s long-standing legacy of culinary innovation in pizzas, pastas, and salads along with FiveStar’s expertise in premium fresh food to upgrade grocery’s refrigerated salads section, giving shoppers high-quality, exciting, and affordable options in fresh foods. “Salads have been a cornerstone of CPK since the beginning, from our BBQ Chicken Chopped to our Thai Crunch,” said Michael Beacham, President of California Pizza Kitchen Global. “Bringing that creativity, bold flavor and California approach to the fresh aisle is a natural next step, and FiveStar Gourmet Foods is the right partner to help us deliver the quality our guests expect, wherever they find us.” Restaurant Credibility Meets Retail Scale FiveStar Gourmet Foods, creator of Simply Fresh, brings nearly three decades of fresh-food expertise, national manufacturing capabilities, and large-scale retail execution to the partnership. “This category doesn’t need another ordinary salad,” said Tal Shoshan, Founder and CEO of FiveStar Gourmet Foods. “Retailers need products that give consumers a reason to come back with excitement and confidence. CPK brings something very different: a loved restaurant brand known for delicious, creative food.” “We started with the salads our guests already love and worked with FiveStar to translate them for the fresh aisle,” said Paul Pszybylski, Executive Chef and Vice President of Culinary Innovation at California Pizza Kitchen. “The goal is simple: when you open one at home, it should taste like something you’d order at our table.” The new CPK collection will feature restaurant-inspired recipes, elevated ingredients, and bold California flavors designed to differentiate at shelf and rebuild excitement in the fresh salad category. Products will be produced by FiveStar and feature the CPK brand alongside “Crafted by Simply Fresh.” Beyond Salads: A Platform for Growth While launching with salads, the partnership is designed for expansion. CPK and FiveStar plan to explore additional opportunities across refrigerated prepared foods, dressings and other categories as they build a broader retail platform together. The strategy complements CPK’s plan announced earlier this year to expand its frozen offerings beyond signature pizzas and into appetizers and entrees inspired by its restaurant menu. The brand is also expanding into non-traditional channels through the deployment of up to 1,000 automated retail kiosks nationwide over the next three years, expanding the brand into airports, universities, hospitals and other high-traffic locations. “When we began looking at the right strategic partner for CPK, FiveStar stood out for reasons that went well beyond manufacturing,” said Cory M. Baker, Founder and Managing Partner of Consortium Brand Partners. “Tal has built an organization with the infrastructure of a major national prepared foods company while retaining the speed, creativity, and entrepreneurial mindset that built the business. That combination is rare, and it gives us tremendous confidence in what we can build together.” For more information, visit www.cpk.com and follow @cpk on Instagram, @calpizzakitchen on TikTok or @calpizzakitchen on X. articles.title: BoomBozz Celebrates 28 Years with Special Offers and Free Pizza
articles.titleKo: BoomBozz Celebrates 28 Years with Special Offers and Free Pizza
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . What began as a 14-seat pizza restaurant in St. Matthews in 1998 has become one of Louisville’s recognizable homegrown restaurant brands. On Tuesday, October 20, BoomBozz will celebrate its 28th anniversary with free pizza, special offers, a Beat the Clock contest and the grand reopening of its remodeled Highlands restaurant. The anniversary theme is “28 YEARS. 28 SECONDS. FREE PIZZA FOR A YEAR.” At BoomBozz Highlands, 1448 Bardstown Road, dine-in guests can receive a free small one-topping pizza from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. The restaurant will also showcase its refreshed interior, bar and patio. From 3 p.m. to close, Highlands will offer $10 Medium Famous Pizza Pies. $2 Boom Brew beers and the Beat the Clock contest will be available throughout the day. Other participating Louisville-area BoomBozz locations will offer $10 Medium Famous Pizza Pies, $2 Boom Brew beers and Beat the Clock throughout their regular operating hours. A 28-Second Challenge with Pizza for a Year at Stake Each dine-in guest gets one attempt to start and stop a digital timer. Stop it at exactly 28.00 seconds and win Free Pizza for a Year – one small one-topping pizza each week for 52 weeks. Each participating location will award one grand prize. Guests who stop the timer at exactly 27.99 seconds win a $100 gift card; 27.98 seconds wins $50; and 27.97 seconds wins $25. There is no limit on the number of qualifying gift-card winners. Exact times are required, and each dine-in guest is limited to one attempt. A Louisville Original, 28 Years Later From its modest 14-seat beginnings, BoomBozz has built a following for award-winning pizzas, creative Famous Pizza Pies and a neighborhood sports-bar atmosphere. The anniversary recognizes the Louisville customers, employees and communities that have supported the brand across nearly three decades. The celebration also marks a new chapter for BoomBozz Highlands, which has undergone renovations to its dining room, bar and patio. The October 20 event is its official grand reopening. Anniversary Event at a Glance Tuesday, October 20, 2026 | BoomBozz Highlands, 1448 Bardstown Road, Louisville Highlands: Free small one-topping pizza, dine-in, 11 a.m.-3 p.m.; $10 Medium Famous Pizza Pies, dine-in, 3 p.m.-close; $2 Boom Brew and Beat the Clock all day. Other participating Louisville-area locations: $10 Medium Famous Pizza Pies, $2 Boom Brew and Beat the Clock during regular operating hours. The $10 Medium Famous Pizza Pie offer is dine-in only, limited to one per table/check, with no substitutions or combination with other discounts. Additional promotional rules apply. Alcohol is served only to guests 21 and older. The post BoomBozz Celebrates 28 Years with Special Offers and Free Pizza appeared first on FSR magazine .

The SOUR PATCH KIDS brought the SOUR THEN SWEET mischief, and Wingstop made it saucy. The result is the ultimate candy-meets-wings crossover, one of Wingstop’s wildest flavor creations yet. Created by Wingstop’s Flavor Experts, Wicked Punch features a mischievous SOUR THEN SWEET REDBERRY glaze finished with SOUR PATCH KIDS Bitz for a wickedly fun twist, available across all proteins. Halloween has a way of bringing unlikely duos together, and this year, Wingstop and the SOUR PATCH KIDS candy may be the most unexpected yet. It’s surprising, a little unhinged and exactly the kind of flavor experience only Wingstop could pull off – a mashup that is equal parts trick, treat and dare. “Candy on wings? We know exactly what you’re thinking. But no, seriously, it has no business being this good,” said Michael Skipworth, President and CEO of Wingstop. “SOUR PATCH KIDS Wicked Punch wings bring sour and sweet together in a way only Wingstop can. This year, the SOUR PATCH KIDS brand decided candy wasn’t enough,” said Lauryn McDonough, Senior Director, Candy at Mondelēz International. “This is the first taste of the SOUR PATCH KIDS 13 Days of Mischief program, and transforming our signature SOUR THEN SWEET flavors into a wing flavor is exactly the kind of unexpected mischief our fans love. On Oct. 27, the flavor expands to Wingstop menus nationwide, just in time for Halloween week. Bring it to a costume party, break it out during a scary-movie marathon or serve it after trick-or-treating for one final Halloween dare. articles.title: Alexandria Restaurant Partners Names Nazia Millwala President
articles.titleKo: Alexandria Restaurant Partners Names Nazia Millwala President
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . As president, Nazia Millwala will oversee ARP’s operations, finance, people and culture, marketing, and food and beverage execution. Alexandria Restaurant Partners (ARP), a leading Northern Virginia-based restaurant group that owns and operates concepts across Northern Virginia and Orlando, has appointed Nazia Millwala as president. Millwala most recently served as ARP’s chief financial officer and brings extensive experience across finance, marketing, development and organizational leadership to her expanded role. Millwala joined ARP in January 2022 as vice president of finance and was promoted to chief financial officer in August 2024. Her appointment as president marks the latest step in her progression within the company and an important new chapter for the Alexandria-based restaurant group. The appointment is part of a planned leadership evolution as ARP partners Dave Nicholas, David Clapp and Scott Shaw shift their focus away from day-to-day management. As president, Millwala will oversee ARP’s operations, finance, people and culture, marketing, and food and beverage execution. Her first-year priorities include ensuring a smooth transition, building an expanded executive leadership team and establishing a strong operational structure for the company’s future. “Scott, David and I are incredibly proud of what our team has built, and we believe this is the right time to transition day-to-day leadership to Nazia,” said Dave Nicholas, co-founder and partner of Alexandria Restaurant Partners. “She has earned the trust and respect of our team through her thoughtful leadership, broad business perspective and genuine commitment to our people. We look forward to remaining involved and supporting her as she leads ARP forward.” Building on more than a decade of growth, Millwala’s strategy will focus on ARP’s people, management development and community involvement. Over the next 18 months, she plans to develop the company’s next generation of managers and leaders, create new opportunities for employees and deepen ARP’s connections throughout Alexandria and Orlando. Her strategy will also include growing sales channels such as catering, strengthening marketing efforts and continuing to evolve the company’s concepts and guest experiences. “ARP’s greatest strength is the people who bring our restaurants to life every day,” said Millwala. “My priority is to give our teams the clarity and support they need to do their best work. We have an incredible opportunity to build on what makes our restaurants special, find new ways to serve our guests and contribute even more to the communities we call home.” Millwala’s people-first, guest-focused philosophy defines hospitality as a genuine human connection between restaurant teams and their guests, an approach that will guide ARP’s next chapter. Before joining ARP, Millwala spent 12 years with Yum! Brands, holding leadership roles across finance, marketing and development for KFC and Pizza Hut in Canada, the Middle East, North Africa, Pakistan and Turkey. Her responsibilities ranged from business analysis and regional marketing strategy to franchise development, market expansion and portfolio growth. Millwala began her career at KPMG, where she worked with Fortune 500 companies and developed a strong foundation in financial analysis, risk assessment and strategic planning. Born and raised in Dubai, she earned a degree in commerce from the University of Wollongong in Australia and an International MBA from IE Business School in Madrid, Spain. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Cicis Pizza, the original all-you-can-eat pizza buffet known for delivering TBPVA (The Best Pizza Value Anywhere), has appointed Kimberly Thompson as Executive Vice President of Development. Bringing over a decade of franchise development leadership experience across some of the restaurant industry’s most recognizable brands, Thompson will help identify new opportunities for expansion nationwide. Thompson joins Cicis following franchise development leadership roles with Bonchon, Walk-On’s Sports Bistreaux, Jack in the Box, Del Taco and Philly Pretzel Factory. Throughout her career, she has worked closely with single- and multi-unit operators, guiding franchise development strategies, evaluating new markets and helping qualified candidates navigate the franchise ownership process. “As we look toward the next chapter of Cicis’ growth, we’re focused on being intentional about where we expand, who we grow with and how we support our franchisees along the way,” said Jeff Hetsel, President of Cicis Pizza. “We see tremendous opportunity to build on the brand’s established presence while introducing Cicis to new communities across the country. Kimberly brings the leadership and strategic perspective to help us pursue that vision while maintaining the relationships and support that have been central to Cicis’ success.” In her new role, Thompson will focus on expanding Cicis’ franchise development pipeline, identifying qualified operators and supporting strategic growth across priority markets. Working alongside the brand’s leadership, operations and real estate teams, she will help prospective franchisees evaluate development opportunities while leveraging Cicis’ established training, site selection and supply chain resources. “When you look at Cicis, you have a brand that families have known and loved for decades, a value proposition that resonates with today’s consumers and a business model that gives operators multiple ways to serve their communities,” said Thompson. “What excites me most is the opportunity ahead. We have an established foundation, strong franchisee support and strong potential to introduce Cicis to new markets. Our goal is to double the brand’s footprint over the next five years, and I’m looking forward to connecting with ambitious operators who want to be part of that growth.” The appointment comes as Cicis continues investing in restaurant operations, technology and guest engagement. The brand offers multiple revenue opportunities through its signature all-you-can-eat buffet, carryout, catering, delivery and arcade game rooms, supported by national marketing resources, franchisee training, real estate expertise and its distribution partner, JMC Restaurant Distribution. With nearly 300 restaurants across more than 23 states, Cicis is pursuing new development opportunities in Texas, the Carolinas, Georgia, Alabama, and Florida. For more information about franchise opportunities with Cicis Pizza, visit https://www.cicis.com/franchising. articles.title: Corner Bakery Cafe Announces Daily Complimentary Surprise Dessert Samples
articles.titleKo: Corner Bakery Cafe Announces Daily Complimentary Surprise Dessert Samples
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Corner Bakery Cafe’s began in 1991 with artisan bread-making in Maggiano’s kitchens in Chicago. As its menu expanded to breakfast, lunch and dinner, the brand maintained its bakery foundation, emphasizing quality ingredients, thoughtful preparation and welcoming hospitality. Beginning today, Corner Bakery is offering a complimentary surprise dessert sample every day from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. and 5 to 7 p.m. at all corporate-owned cafes. Timed for a sweet treat around lunch or dinner, the program features seven treats, including custom butter cakes and a lemon tart developed especially for Corner Bakery. “Guests often come in knowing exactly what they want, and it’s easy to overlook something new when you already have a favorite,” said Erin Hasselgren, president of Corner Bakery Cafe. “We wanted to give them a chance to try a treat before committing to an order. It also gives our cafe teams a reason to start a conversation, hear what guests think and help them discover more of the menu.” The custom desserts were developed with French Gourmet and ShellsbyDesign, including butter cakes, which Datassential identified as the fastest-growing dessert. “The advantage of a custom recipe is that the brand gets a say in the dessert itself, beyond simply choosing something from a catalog,” said Don Smith, CEO of French Gourmet/ShellsbyDesign. “For Corner Bakery, we want these butter cakes and tarts to become something guests stop in for, even when they weren’t planning to stay for a meal.” The sampling lineup includes Tuxedo Butter Cake, Lemon Tart, Salted Brown Butter Crispy Bar, Almond Butter Cake, Pecan Chocolate Chunk Bar, Fudge Brownie and Chocolate Peanut Butter Cake. Guests can check Corner Bakery Cafe’s social media daily to discover the surprise sample of the day. To explore the full menu and find their nearest cafe, visit cornerbakerycafe.com. articles.title: Stonefire Grill Introduces New Seasonal Menu Lineup
articles.titleKo: Stonefire Grill Introduces New Seasonal Menu Lineup
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . These updates reflect Stonefire Grill’s continued focus on an evolving menu based on guest preferences while maintaining the quality and familiar flavors guests have come to expect. Stonefire Grill, a premier fast-casual family dining destination for more than 25 years, serving generous portions of scratch-made, classic American-inspired dishes, has introduced a new lineup of seasonal menu offerings featuring comforting flavors and fresh takes on familiar favorites. Available starting today at all Stonefire Grill locations throughout Southern California, the menu features six new dishes, from scratch-made soups and satisfying sides to fresh salads and pizzas. The new lineup arrives at a time when gathering around the table takes on special meaning, giving families and friends more opportunities to share a meal, reconnect and enjoy Stonefire Grill together. “Seasonal menus give us the chance to build on the dishes our guests already know and love while bringing the flavors of special times of the year to the table,” said David Youngberg, CEO of Stonefire Grill. “We’re intentional about creating seasonal menus that feel familiar, approachable and comforting, while still giving families something new to discover. That balance is central to the Stonefire Grill experience. Every seasonal launch carries our ‘Happy to Serve’ approach and gives our guests one more reason to gather around the table and share a meal.” Stonefire Grill’s scratch-made seasonal menu additions include: Baked Potato Soup — Creamy potato and bacon soup topped with shredded cheddar cheese and green onions. Margherita Pizza — Classic combination of margherita sauce, fresh mozzarella and fresh basil. Harvest Salad — Seasonal salad featuring mixed greens, butternut squash, candied walnuts, feta cheese, dried cranberries and apple chips, tossed in a maple vinaigrette. Bacon Cheddar Loaded Mashed Potatoes — Stonefire Grill’s signature Garlic Mashed Potatoes, made from scratch with roasted garlic, butter, sour cream, cream cheese and cheddar cheese, loaded with bacon and topped with green onions and cumin crema. Chili Loaded Mashed Potatoes — Stonefire Grill’s signature Garlic Mashed Potatoes, made from scratch with roasted garlic, butter, sour cream, cream cheese and cheddar cheese, topped with tri tip chili, green onions and cumin crema. Italian Sausage Pizza — Savory pizza topped with Italian sausage, then finished with oregano and parmesan cheese. Other fall menu updates give guests more ways to enjoy Stonefire Grill favorites, including the popular protein-packed Mediterranean Market Salad, which debuted as part of the summer menu and is now a permanent offering. Stonefire Grill is also expanding its signature burger offering by giving guests the option to enjoy a Classic Cheeseburger or BBQ Bacon Cheddar Burger as a single or double patty, with either one 4-ounce patty or two 4-ounce patties. The Classic Cheeseburger features melted cheddar cheese, fresh lettuce, juicy tomato, caramelized onion, crisp pickles and Stonefire Grill’s special sauce, while the BBQ Bacon Cheddar Burger features crisp bacon, melted cheddar cheese, Stonefire Grill’s Signature BBQ sauce and Stonefire Grill’s special sauce. Both burgers are served on a potato brioche bun with kettle chips. These updates reflect Stonefire Grill’s continued focus on an evolving menu based on guest preferences while maintaining the quality and familiar flavors guests have come to expect. To view the full menu, order online or find your nearest location, visit www.stonefiregrill.com. The post Stonefire Grill Introduces New Seasonal Menu Lineup appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Potbelly Opens in Ocala, Florida
articles.titleKo: Potbelly Opens in Ocala, Florida
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Potbelly, the iconic neighborhood sandwich shop, is expanding its Central Florida footprint with a new shop opening Tuesday, Oct. 13, at Corta Commons in southwest Ocala. The opening marks the brand’s entry into Marion County and joins more than 15 shops currently operating across Florida. Situated within the Shoppes of Corta Commons, a growing, Sprouts-anchored, mixed-use destination along the State Road 200 corridor, the new location puts Potbelly amid an expanding mix of retail, dining and residential development in one of southwest Ocala’s active growth areas. Experienced multi-unit restaurant operator and Potbelly franchisee Danish Alidino is behind the new Corta Commons shop. Alidino and his partners at Deli Management LLC own and operate multiple restaurant concepts throughout Central Florida, bringing extensive experience leading teams and serving communities across the region. After opening his first Potbelly shop in Lady Lake, Florida in 2025, Alidino is continuing to grow with the brand while expanding his longstanding presence in the Ocala market. “I’ve been part of the restaurant community in Ocala for years, so I’ve had a front-row seat to how much this area has grown and evolved,” said Alidino. “Bringing Potbelly here gives us another way to serve a community we already know well. Our goal is for this shop to feel like part of the neighborhood from day one.” To celebrate the opening, Potbelly will host a Grand Opening celebration on October 24 from 10 a.m. to 12 noon, where the first 50 people in line will win Free Potbelly for a Year. A ribbon-cutting and other festivities will also be available for all attendees to enjoy. The Corta Commons shop will serve the brand’s signature lineup of toasty sandwiches and wraps, fresh salads, hand-dipped shakes and freshly baked cookies. Regular operating hours are 10 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily. Guests can order ahead or place catering orders through Potbelly.com or the Potbelly App. Delivery will also be available through Potbelly and participating third-party services. Opening in Ocala is part of a broader Potbelly Florida growth strategy, with more than 80 shops under development agreements across the state, including Tampa, Sarasota-Bradenton, Fort Myers-Naples, Broward County, Fort Lauderdale, West Palm Beach, Gainesville, Ocala and Panama City Beach. For exclusive offers and rewards, Potbelly invites guests to join the Potbelly Perks program, where members can unlock free sandwiches, cookies and special offers throughout the year. To sign up, visit www.potbelly.com/perks. For more information about the new Potbelly location, visit www.potbelly.com. The post Potbelly Opens in Ocala, Florida appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Huey Magoo’s Opens in Independence, Missouri
articles.titleKo: Huey Magoo’s Opens in Independence, Missouri
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Huey Magoo’s, the fast-casual brand known for its bold flavors and handcrafted chicken tenders, is bringing its fan-favorite tenders to Independence with the grand opening of its newest location. The opening marks Huey Magoo’s 93rd restaurant nationwide, further expanding the brand’s commitment to bold flavors, fresh ingredients and made-to-order meals. Every tender starts with the best 3 percent of the chicken, the tenderloin, and is served hand-breaded, 24-hour marinated and grilled or “sauced” and tossed in buffalo, sweet red chili, lemon pepper or garlic parmesan. The 2,200-square-foot restaurant features a drive-thru, curbside pickup, a pickup window and patio seating, offering guests a variety of convenient ways to enjoy their meals, including dine-in, takeout, catering and online ordering through the Huey Magoo’s mobile app, website and third-party delivery services, including DoorDash, Uber Eats and Grubhub. The location is operated by Midwest Restaurant Group, which brings 10 years of restaurant industry experience and a passion for delivering an exceptional guest experience. It is the group’s first of ten planned Huey Magoo’s restaurants. “We are thrilled to open our first Huey Magoo’s restaurant and introduce the Independence community to the brand’s premium chicken tenders and welcoming hospitality,” said a Midwest Restaurant Group spokesperson. “Our team looks forward to drawing on its restaurant experience as we grow with Huey Magoo’s and establish a strong presence in the market.” The menu includes a robust selection of customizable options, including fresh-made salads, sandwiches, wraps and the most popular choice, tender meals. Guests can also enjoy hand-spun chips, freshly prepared coleslaw, banana pudding and house-made specialty dips, including Magoo’s, Spicy Magoo’s and Ranch, showcasing the brand’s commitment to quality and freshness. Six additional signature dips – Buffalo, Honey Mustard, BBQ, Garlic Parmesan, Sweet Red Chili and Bleu Cheese – and a variety of sides are available to customize every meal. There’s even more to love with the recent launch of the Magoo’s Rewards™ loyalty program , where members earn points toward free food with every purchase. New users receive a Buy One Get One Free 10-piece Tender Bites meal with a beverage purchase to redeem within 30 days. Members earn 10 points per $1 spent, with catering orders earning one point per $1, making every meal—whether a quick bite or a group gathering—more rewarding. The Huey Magoo’s mobile app makes ordering, tracking rewards, and accessing exclusive offers easier than ever. “Midwest Restaurant Group brings a decade of restaurant experience, strong operational expertise and a shared commitment to exceptional hospitality,” said Mike Sutter, Chief Operating Officer of Huey Magoo’s. “They are an ideal partner to lead our continued growth in Missouri, and we are thrilled to support them as they open their first Huey Magoo’s and introduce the brand to the Independence community.” Huey Magoo’s Independence is now open at 4049 Little Blue Parkway, Independence, MO 64057. Hours of operation are Sunday through Thursday, 10:30 a.m. to 10 p.m.; Friday and Saturday, 10:30 a.m. to midnight. For more information, visit HueyMagoos.com, to download the app, click here or contact the restaurant directly at 816-393-0465.
